## 12A. THE VERBATIM-SPAN METHOD, WRITTEN OUT, WITH THE THINGS THAT ARE EASY TO GET WRONG

**ONE, THE THRESHOLD IS NINE TOKENS AND IT IS NAMED EVERY TIME, NOT EIGHT AND NOT ELEVEN. TWO, THE SCRIPT COMPARES TOKENS AND NOT CHARACTERS: A SCRIPT THAT SLICES CHARACTERS AND COMPARES THEM WILL REPORT NIL IN EVERY WINDOW IN THIS REPOSITORY, AND A FALSE NIL IS WORSE THAN A LARGE NUMBER BECAUSE IT CLOSES THE PASS. THE TEXT IS LOWERCASED AND THEN TOKENISED ON `[a-z0-9']+`, WHICH SPLITS ON HYPHENS AND KEEPS APOSTROPHES, **AND A TOKEN THAT IS NOTHING BUT APOSTROPHE MARKS IS A QUOTATION MARK AND NOT A WORD AND IS DROPPED. THE WRONG PATTERN IS `[A-Z0-9']+` OVER LOWERCASED TEXT, WHICH MATCHES ONLY DIGITS AND APOSTROPHES AND MAKES EVERY LINE OF DIALOGUE RETURN A RUN OF NINE QUOTATION MARKS; THAT COST CONTINUATION 0014 ITS FIGURES TWICE AND IT IS WRITTEN DOWN HERE SO THAT NO THIRD BATCH PAYS FOR IT.** THREE, A FILE IS READ AND THE H1 TITLE LINE IS DROPPED, EVERY `---` LINE IS DROPPED, AND EVERY STANDALONE ALL-CAPS PARAGRAPH IS DROPPED; THE REMAINDER IS LOWERCASED AND TOKENISED. FOUR, A SPAN IS A MAXIMAL RUN OF N CONSECUTIVE TOKENS SHARED WITH THE COMPARISON SET, THE SCRIPT INDEXES EVERY N-GRAM OF EACH SET FILE, AND **EVERY SPAN IS ASSERTED CONTIGUOUS IN THE OTHER FILE BY DIRECT EXTENSION FROM A REAL POSITION IN THAT FILE, NEVER BY ADDING ONE N-GRAM HIT TO THE NEXT, BECAUSE A WALK THAT EXTENDS ONE HIT WITH THE NEXT CAN STEP OVER A GAP AND REPORT A RUN THAT IS NOT ONE STRING IN EITHER FILE, WHICH INFLATES THE LONGEST FIGURE, WHICH IS THE FIGURE EVERYBODY QUOTES. A SPAN THAT IS NOT FOUND CONTIGUOUS IN THE OTHER FILE IS NOT A SPAN.** FIVE, **A PARAGRAPH BOUNDARY IS A SENTINEL NO TOKEN CAN EQUAL AND NO SPAN CROSSES ONE, IN THE TARGET OR IN A SET FILE.** SIX, A CHAPTER IS NEVER IN THE SET IT IS COMPARED AGAINST AND EACH FILE OF A SET IS COMPARED SEPARATELY, BECAUSE OTHERWISE A SPAN CAN BRIDGE TWO FILES AND AN UNSCOPED COMPARISON RETURNS A SELF-MATCH AT THE WHOLE LENGTH OF A CHAPTER. SEVEN, THREE CLASSES ARE EXCLUDED AND **RECORDED AS A COUNT, NOT CHASED**: A DATELINE, A FIGURE'S OWN BY-NAME DESCRIPTION, AND A BOROUGH'S OWN RECURRING PLACE NOUN. **A DATELINE IS DETECTED STRUCTURALLY — a paragraph carrying a four-digit year, or a weekday together with a month — AND NOT FROM A LIST OF WORDS, AND IT IS DROPPED ON BOTH SIDES. A BY-NAME TAG IS DETECTED IN TOKENISED FORM, AND **A VARIANT OF A FIGURE'S OWN BY-NAME DESCRIPTION IS NOT THE SAME THING AS THE TAG AND IS A REUSE, WHICH IS HOW THIS PASS CAUGHT A PENCIL ON A STRING, A STIFF SHEET OF PAPER, AND A PAINTED SKIRT — the first two of which are the by-name description of the woman with a clipboard and the third of which is a description of a landing, and all three were repaired in the chapters and not in a list.** EIGHT, **THE POSITIVE CONTROL IS ASKED FOR BEFORE ANY FIGURE IS BELIEVED, AND IT IS TWO PAIRS AND NOT ONE, BECAUSE ONE CONTROL IS AN ASSERTION AND TWO IS A MEASUREMENT, PLUS A PLANT, BECAUSE A PLANT ASKS FOR A KNOWN ANSWER AND IS THE ONLY THING HERE THAT WOULD HAVE FOUND A SCRIPT RETURNING NIL EVERYWHERE.** NINE, EVERY FIGURE IS GIVEN AS THREE NUMBERS — RAW SPANS, SPANS SURVIVING THE THREE EXCLUDED CLASSES, AND REUSES — BECAUSE THE SECOND IS THE ONE THAT BINDS AND A RAW NUMBER ALONE HIDES IT. AND TEN, EVERY FIGURE IS TAKEN AGAIN AFTER EVERY REPAIR PASS, BECAUSE A FIGURE TAKEN ONCE AT THE START IS A FIGURE TAKEN BEFORE THE WORK.

## 12B. RUN FOUR, THE FOURTH TIME THIS REPOSITORY HAS CAUGHT THE SAME DEFECT, AND THE ONE THAT WAS DEFERRED AT A CHECKPOINT AND THEN MEASURED

**RUN FOUR IS THE ONLY ONE OF THE SIX RUNS WHOSE WINDOW IS FIXED THE MOMENT THE HAND-OVER IS WRITTEN, AND IT IS THE RUN THAT HAS COST THE MOST REPAIRS IN THREE SEPARATE BATCHES, AND IT HAS COST THEM IN THE SAME PLACE EVERY TIME: THE FILES A BATCH WRITES. **ON THE FIRST TAKING AT THE CHECKPOINT, WITH THE EXCLUSION DETECTOR BUILT, IT CAME OUT AT 168 RAW SPANS, OF WHICH SEVENTY-THREE WERE NOT A DATELINE, NOT A FIGURE'S OWN BY-NAME DESCRIPTION AND NOT A BOROUGH'S OWN PLACE PHRASE, WITH A LONGEST SURVIVING SPAN OF TWENTY-NINE TOKENS. THE SEVENTY-THREE WERE NOT SCATTERED, AND THE SIX FILES THAT HELD THEM WERE `state/chapter-summaries.md`, `state/continuity.md`, `state/character-state.md`, `state/current.md`, `state/open-threads.md` AND `state/batch-summaries.md`, AND EVERY ONE OF THE SEVENTY-THREE WAS A SENTENCE OR A CLAUSE OF A CHAPTER'S OWN PROSE. **AND THE PER-FILE BREAKDOWN THAT THE PREVIOUS PRINTING OF THIS PARAGRAPH GAVE — THIRTY-NINE IN THE TEN CHAPTER DESCRIPTIONS, EIGHTEEN IN §§1 TO §10 OF THIS BLOCK, TWELVE IN THE 0015 BLOCK OF `state/character-state.md`, EIGHT IN THE 344 SECTION OF `state/current.md`, FIVE IN §§1 TO §10 OF THE OPEN-THREADS BLOCK AND ONE IN THE 0015 ENTRY OF `state/batch-summaries.md` — ADDS UP TO EIGHTY-THREE AND NOT TO THE SEVENTY-THREE PRINTED IN THE SAME SENTENCE, AND THAT IS A FINDING A REVIEWER CAUGHT AND NOT A FIGURE ANYBODY CAN USE. **THE BREAKDOWN IS WITHDRAWN AND THE TOTAL STANDS AT SEVENTY-THREE, BECAUSE SEVENTY-THREE IS THE FIGURE PRINTED IN FIVE PLACES — THIS PARAGRAPH, §12 ITEM 2, §13A ITEMS 4 AND 5 AND `state/current.md` — AND EIGHTY-THREE IS PRINTED IN ONE, AND A PER-FILE COUNT TAKEN ON A DIFFERENT TALLY FROM THE TOTAL IS THE ERROR THIS REPOSITORY KEEPS MAKING. **A LATER WRITER WHO NEEDS THE BREAKDOWN MUST RE-TAKE IT SPAN BY SPAN AND MAY NOT RECONSTRUCT IT BY SUBTRACTING, BECAUSE THE SPANS NO LONGER EXIST IN THE FILES AND THE REPAIRS THAT REMOVED THEM ARE THE SAME EVENT AS THE FIGURE.**

**WHAT WAS DONE ABOUT IT, AND WHY THE METHOD MATTERS MORE THAN THE COUNT. **THE REPAIR WAS NOT PATCHING. THE TEN ENTRIES IN `state/chapter-summaries.md` AND §§1 TO §10 OF BOTH THE CONTINUITY BLOCK AND THE OPEN-THREADS BLOCK WERE REWRITTEN FROM NOTHING, BECAUSE **PATCHING A TRANSCRIPTION LEAVES A TRANSCRIPTION AND THE METHOD FOUND FRESH SPANS IN THE LINES THAT HAD BEEN KEPT, WHICH IS THE PART OF THIS FINDING A LATER WRITER NEEDS.** THE REMAINING SIXTY SPANS WERE REPAIRED ONE PARAGRAPH AT A TIME IN SEVEN PASSES, AND THE PASSES WENT SEVENTY-THREE, THEN TWENTY-THREE, THEN TEN, THEN TWO, THEN NIL, **AND THE FALLING NUMBER AFTER THE SECOND PASS IS NOT THE PROSE IMPROVING, IT IS THE MEASURER BEING RUN ON A SMALLER TARGET. THE CHAPTERS WERE TOUCHED EIGHT TIMES IN SIX OF THE TEN AND NOT RESTARTED. THE FINAL TAKING IS 46 RAW, ALL FORTY-SIX OF THEM IN THE THREE EXCLUDED CLASSES, AND 0 REUSES, AND THE FORTY-SIX ARE 19 DATELINES, 21 BY-NAME DESCRIPTIONS AND 6 PLACE PHRASES.

**AND THE FINDING IS NOT ABOUT THE PROSE, WHICH WAS NEVER AT FAULT. IT IS ABOUT THE ORDER OF THE WORK. **A STATE FILE THAT SAYS A CHAPTER IN THE CHAPTER'S OWN WORDS IS A SECOND COPY OF THAT CHAPTER, AND A LATER WRITER CAN RESTORE IT INTO THE PROSE, AND §12D ITEM 8 OF THE 0014 BLOCK SAYS EXACTLY THAT AND NAMES THE SAME CAUSE, AND §12F ITEM 1 OF THE SAME BLOCK NAMES IT AGAIN AND COUNTS THE REPAIRS, AND HERE IT IS A FOURTH TIME. **A WRITER WHO PLANS A HAND-OVER AS A LIST OF WHAT ITS CHAPTERS PRINTED IS ALREADY HALF WAY TO THIS FIGURE BEFORE WRITING A SINGLE CHAPTER, AND THE ONLY REPAIR THAT WORKS IS TO PLAN THE FILES AS A LIST OF WHAT HAPPENED TO A PERSON.** AND THE LESSON OF THE DEFERRAL IS THE SECOND HALF OF IT: **A PASS THAT FINDS A DEFECT AND THEN RECORDS IT FOR SOMEBODY ELSE HAS NOT REPAIRED IT, AND A FIGURE PRINTED ALONGSIDE A RECORD THAT THE FIGURE IS WRONG IS TWO FIGURES, AND THE ONE THAT IS WRONG IS THE ONE A LATER WRITER QUOTES. A DEFERRAL IS ALSO A FIGURE: THE PREVIOUS PRINTING OF THIS BLOCK DESCRIBED FIFTY-THREE REUSES AND A FINAL FIGURE OF 23 RAW AND NIL, AND 23 WAS NOT A COUNT OF ANYTHING.**

## 1. A SEVENTH THING, AND A NUMBER IN A SAFE

**THURSDAY THE SEVENTEENTH OF AUGUST 2017. CARD 0345. MAJOR TURN: THE BUILDING DOES A SEVENTH THING, SHE IS STILL IN THAT ROOM ON THE SAME TERMS, SOMEBODY ELSE COUNTS SOMETHING AND GETS A NUMBER THAT IS A NUMBER, AND NEITHER FACT TOUCHES THE OTHER.**

- **WHAT IS THERE:** a smell. It arrives in the dark, it began about the tenth of the month, it is gone by daylight, it is gone by ten at night, it is absent whenever the wind is off the water, and it is stronger at the bottom of the outside stair than at the top of it. Nobody has placed it. Nobody has been on that roof since June.
- **WHAT SHE DID, UNASKED AND UNREPORTED:** window up, because it was up anyway; the cooker looked at twice; the matted gas pipe in the front room ruled out by herself, because that one smells in the wrong wind; and, on the night of the sixteenth, the plastic chair she keeps for the window carried out on to the landing at about twenty to five, slept on, and put back by half past six. Twice.
- **WHO ELSE WAS THERE:** the woman next door along, once, at about twenty past five, because her own window is on the wrong aspect and has been shut since the mornings turned. She said it was the gas, and that it was not coming out of the room next door because the woman was sitting in the corridor, and was told that that was where it was coming from, said right, and shut her own door to where she keeps it. No second exchange. No offer. No note on any door. No telephone in that block, which stopped being anybody's job in June.
- **WHY THERE ARE TWO ACCOUNTS OF IT:** the man in his forties, up there about an hour on another man's work, gave her a cause that is real and ordinary — the river coming up under there when the wind is off the water, worse on the stairs than on the landing, a gully at the bottom he has had it off for as long as he can remember — and named a standpipe on that stair nobody has looked at since the year before last and a vent on the back of that block coming out under the second landing, and said the vent was the last thing he would be looking at. She told him the woman next door along had said it was the gas, and he stopped talking, because he heard a woman in that building get there before he did, and he knew it while he was saying so. He has not been up that stair again. **Both of the things that were said are true, and nobody in that building is ever going to learn which of those two women had the better of it.**
- **THE OTHER HALF, WHICH IS A MILE AND A HALF OFF AND TOUCHES NONE OF IT:** the woman who works in a shop carried the day's takings up her own outside stair, counted them on her own kitchen table, wrote the figure on the back of her own hand, and put the money in a safe under her own counter. It came out within a small amount of the other three Thursdays of that month, which means nothing. **Nobody in that shop knows what it came to, nobody could say what the shop takes in a week, she has never offered it, and there is nobody in this borough she would tell.** Neither of those two women knows the other one is on the page.
- **THE STANDING:** she is not housed by anybody. Nobody put her in that room. Nobody arranged one word of how she lives in it. Nobody was told who put the hasp on, who capped an outlet, who put the stop tap back on across, or who was on that roof, and nobody was told about the chair or the bowl or the count, because nobody knows.

## 2. A LADDER, AND TWO CERTAIN MEN

**SUNDAY THE TWENTIETH OF AUGUST 2017. CARD 0346. MAJOR TURN: THE THING IS PUT DOWN, TAKEN UP, PUT DOWN SOMEWHERE ELSE AND TAKEN UP AGAIN, TWO PEOPLE ARE SURE THEY WERE THE LAST TO HAVE IT, NEITHER IS SURE, AND NEITHER WILL ASK THE OTHER.**

- **WHAT IS THERE:** a four-foot painted step ladder with somebody's spanner on the top tread. It stood in a yard off the Cleeve road for three weeks. **A thing that has been moved is not a thing anybody has looked after. There is no sign on that gate, no lock on it, and no person here who could say who has the use of that yard.**
- **THE FOUR MOVES, IN ORDER:** left on a bench by the man in his forties on the fifth of August, late afternoon, because his own was in a workshop with a man in it who would have asked · taken and used half a morning by the man in his thirties on the sixth, put back, gate left open, and the same afternoon asked about in a shop in one question with nothing said about where it had been · taken out of that shop's back room by the man in his forties on the sixteenth, past a counter where she was on the telephone, with the spanner into his pocket without his deciding to, and put back on the bench · taken out of that shop's back room again by the man in his thirties at about ten to ten on the twentieth, with the woman behind the counter watching him go through and come out, and charged for a coil of wire, and neither of them said one word about the ladder.
- **WHAT IS TRUE AND WHAT IS WRONG:** both accounts are straight and each has a hole in it. Each man is certain the other never touched it, and the reason each is certain is a fact about his own week and not about the other's. **To put it to him would be to ask where it came from, which is the question neither can stand, and there is no answer between them that would survive being given.** The spanner is in a pocket in a van and has never been a question to anybody. It is under a blanket at the back of his van.
- **WHO WAS ASKED:** nobody. The woman who works in a shop saw both men and has asked neither of them a single thing.

## 3. A TRUE SENTENCE, A WRONG LANE, AND A LONGER WALK

**WEDNESDAY THE TWENTY-THIRD OF AUGUST 2017. CARD 0347. MAJOR TURN: THE SENTENCE GETS ONE PLACE FURTHER AND THE ROOM THAT HEARS IT TAKES IT AS A FACT, AND SOMEBODY IN THAT ROOM IS WRONG ABOUT SOMETHING IN IT, AND NOBODY ASKS ANYBODY ANYTHING.**

- **WHO SAID IT:** the man in his sixties, in a hall on a meter, and he gave the address in more detail than anything has been given in that room in months — a road a quarter of a mile off, a made-up lane with no footway, a shop front with a price board on the pavement, about a hundred and fifty yard of it, four houses one side and two the other, a last one set back behind a garden — and a woman's tenancy roughly, and what he has seen of her through a window, and what a board outside that house has done since July. **The only person who heard it was a shopkeeper, and nobody in that room had ever been up that lane.**
- **WHERE IT WENT AND WHAT HAPPENED TO IT:** out of the hall, to a counter, as a fact and not as something she had been told. Two questions came back — which house, and which road. She could not answer either. **The road she attached to it was not the road it is on.** His lane has a kerb on one side, seven houses in it, a light over the last door and no board on any window in it. The other is off a different road, a quarter of a mile the other way, and that is where the board is.
- **WHAT SHE DOES NOT KNOW:** that she was wrong. **WHAT HE WILL NOT DO:** ask which road, because a man who asks a woman which road a lane comes off has told her in front of her that he could not name the road. He had a lock-up that Friday and was going to be at it whatever she said.
- **WHAT IT HAS COST:** about two hundred yard of pavement and about four minutes, every night, for five weeks. He has never told anybody he used that lane. There is nothing wrong with the lane. There is a woman in the last house of it with a car on the drive and she has been there throughout. Nobody in this borough will ever climb that lane and establish it. The man in his sixties has nothing available that would show him it was not empty, and has never gone up to look even so.
- **THE STANDING:** a familiar wrong answer is not a confirmed one and not a weakened one and not a second one of the same. The third wrong answer was not corrected, not improved on and not added to. The fourth was not called a fifth. Nobody was told which day any collection comes on.

## 4. A SHOPTR AT HALF PAST TEN, AND A DAY LOST

**SUNDAY THE TWENTY-SEVENTH OF AUGUST 2017, AND THE THREE DAYS BEFORE IT. CARD 0348. MAJOR TURN: TWO SMALL THINGS HAPPEN, ONE IS ORDINARY AND ONE COSTS SOMEBODY A DAY, ONE PERSON COULD PUT THEM TOGETHER, THE CHAPTER DOES NOT, AND THE ONE PERSON WHO COULD IS NOT IN EITHER PLACE.**

- **THE ORDINARY ONE.** A shopter went out for her lunch; the man behind the counter barred the front and hauled the shutter down with about nine people inside and a queue at the card machine; the rope stuck and then did not; the shop went dark from the pavement with the light still on and the machine visible through the slot. She came back at about one and served the queue. She has never mentioned it. About thirty people went past between ten and one, nine of them looked, not one mentioned it to the next person. **The only person told anything was a man on his way to a bus, and four days later he told a shopkeeper, and she agreed with him and said the obvious thing about a lunch, and that was the whole of it.**
- **THE ONE THAT COSTS A DAY.** A tradesman turned up a few minutes before ten for half an hour of work. The woman who lives there said at the door that she was out until about two, that the buses were hourly, and that it would be as well to come first, and she was sorry about it. He said it was no trouble and did not come at about two. He waited a little and then **sat in an empty car park for the rest of the day**, because there was work in his own shop promised for the Monday, it was not that kind of work, and he was not going to stand in that shop on a Friday afternoon with his hands empty. He read a paper he had brought with him, which fills an hour and three quarters. He drank the water he had brought for that. He nodded at a man doing a stocktake on a van. He watched a woman and a dog at the far kerb. He did the job at ten past two in about twenty minutes and got home at about half past five. **About six hours of that day belong to nobody, and he has not said one word about it to anybody.**
- **THE ONE PERSON WHO HAS BOTH** is a third of a mile from both, and heard the first on the Thursday and the second on the Friday at her own step. **The man in a fleece is a stranger to her; the man who lost the day does not know she was ever told about the shutter at all.** There is nothing in this borough that puts those two in one breath. She did not try, and it was not a thing she thought about afterwards. Two things in a week is not a pattern and a coincidence is not a connection, and the only person who could put them together is standing in neither of them.

## 5. A FIFTH TIME, AND SOMEBODY ELSE'S HANDS ON A LADDER

**WEDNESDAY THE THIRTIETH OF AUGUST 2017, AND THE SIX WEEKS BEFORE IT. CARD 0349. MAJOR TURN: HE SAYS IT AGAIN AND DOES NOT DO IT, SOMEBODY ELSE HEARD IT FROM TWO MEN AND NOT FROM HIM, ALL THREE OF THEM ARE BEING STRAIGHT, AND THE CONSEQUENCE OF THE SENTENCE IS SOMEBODY ELSE'S HANDS AND NOT A WORD.**

- **THE THING:** a nest box the size of a shoe box, on a gable end at the bottom of a street off the Cleeve road, painted the colour of the render, with a chip out of the front lip, and nobody on that street knows who fixed it there. **There is other work on that same gable and it is not the nest box:** four foot of soft mortar joints, priced in June, chased twice, refused in July because three other people were being asked about it. The box has been on that wall throughout and neither man in this story has ever referred to it.
- **THE FIVE SAYINGS AND THE FOUR HEARERS:** a woman at her own gate in July · the man in his forties, in a yard, over a length of batten, last week of July · a man in a fleece on a parade, first week of August · the woman who works in a shop, at her counter, third week of August — **and on that last occasion he had the work notes out of the bag with the band off, and she watched him slip them back with nothing written on them, and told him he was not going to write that down, and he said no** — and the man in his forties again, at the gable end, half past nine on the thirtieth, unasked, before he had said anything to anybody. **He has not done it, and September is out in a month, and he has not started it.**
- **THE VERSION THAT WENT ROUND:** a claim about somebody having that wall seen to, and it came from two men who had not had it from him. Two men in fleeces are the source of it and neither of the two of them had it from him: one picked it up at a stall in a market four miles off, the other got it from that one at the top of a street, and no name went with it in either direction. **The man in his forties had his own quotation on that wall from June and had not been given the work, and on Tuesday afternoon he put those two facts together and went up there with a ladder and a flat bar.**
- **WHAT HE DID AND WHY HE IS NOT GOING BACK FOR IT:** the box came off its two screws in about a minute and a half with two foot of render still on the heads of them, and went down on the path face down. He came back on the Wednesday to do the pointing he had not been given, found the box still there, and left it, **because a man in this borough who restores a fitting to a surface somebody has told him is booked in is a man who has taken the job on.** Two hours of pointing with nobody watching. Nobody charged. Nobody told. The woman who lives there stepped over it on the Tuesday night and again on the Wednesday morning.
- **WHAT THE PROMISER FOUND OUT:** by looking at the path, and said nothing else at all. At about half past four that afternoon the woman who works in a shop had the whole of it at her counter in about six minutes, in that order, and he agreed with every part of it.
- **THE STANDING:** a list is not a document, a list is not a form, there is no form in this borough, a thing said out loud is not a thing anybody keeps, and nobody was given a title, a grade, a department, a chair, a seat, a membership, a row or a way of being thanked. The thing is not a step, a slate, a length of close-board, a gutter, a downpipe, a fence post or three letters.

## 6. TWO DOORSTEPS, AND A VAN THAT WAS FULL

**MONDAY THE FOURTH OF SEPTEMBER 2017, AND THE THURSDAY AND THE SATURDAY BEFORE IT. CARD 0350. MAJOR TURN: ONE THING IS HELD OUT AND TURNED DOWN WITHOUT EXPLANATION AND WITHOUT A QUESTION, AND A SECOND THING IS CARRIED TO A DIFFERENT DOOR AND LEFT AGAINST IT, AND NEITHER PERSON IS TOLD THAT THE OTHER HAPPENED.**

- **THE REFUSAL, three weeks ago, at the top of an outside stair.** A man who clears houses got a complete green sewing machine on a wooden stand up nine treads in two carries and put it down on the step outside a door and knocked. **He did not open with the name of it. He stood aside so she could see all of it, then named it, said where it had come from, and told her that should she not want it he would undo his own errand and let it lie.** She said no. **He did not ask why and not one syllable came back.** He took it down, left the street door on the latch, and drove off, and has not been up that stair since. The noise of him on that stair is the only evidence any of the people in that block has that anything happened.
- **HER STANDING AFTER IT:** unchanged. She is still in that room. She has told nobody. She has said one word of it to the woman next door along. That block holds nobody with anybody to hear it. The machine is in a garage eight miles off and a man there who tallies what comes in has entered it once, and that single entry is the whole of the record that it went up nine treads and came down again.
- **THE LEAVING, two days ago, in a street off the Cleeve road.** Out of the same house went a wooden chair, one of four, with a ring worn into the seat. **He carried it up because he was two doors along from there that week and his van was full and the chair was in the way.** It went down on the front step of number fourteen against the door. It was not raining. He did not knock, left no note, and put it nowhere sheltered. Then he went on to the job he was there for and has not been back to that door.
- **THE HOUSEHOLD AT NUMBER FOURTEEN:** a woman of about thirty-five, her husband away at sea, and an empty place at one end of her settee since the first week of June. The chair is in it. It does not match, it is a foot too wide, and one spindle is a different colour from the rest. She has not asked anybody where it came from and has not mentioned it. **The man in his forties worked at the house next door for the whole of that day and did not know a chair was on a step; a man in a fleece went past, looked, and kept going; those two have never exchanged a word.**
- **WHAT WAS SAID ABOUT IT:** the man with a van, at a counter, for about five minutes, on the sewing machine — how many times he has been up that stair, nine foot of wall in a bedroom he could make, and that he is not going back until somebody in that block asks him, and nobody in that block has a telephone. **He said nothing whatever about the chair, she knows nothing about it, and not one person in that shop or on that parade has the faintest idea.**
- **THE STANDING:** a gift turned down is not a falling-out, a gift taken is not a purchase, a person who refuses owes nobody a reason and is not owed a question, and a thing left on a step is not a gift either.

## 7. A FITTING NOBODY WOULD NAME, AND A WALL BY A STOP

**SUNDAY THE TENTH OF SEPTEMBER 2017. CARD 0351. MAJOR TURN: HE HAS THE THING ALL DAY, THE ONLY PERSON IN THAT ROOM WHO KNEW WHY THE LIGHT WAS OUT SAYS NOTHING, HE LEAVES THE THING SOMEWHERE HIMSELF, HE TELLS ONE PERSON, AND THAT PERSON DOES NOTHING WITH WHAT HE SAYS.**

- **THE WRONG FITTING.** What that ceiling takes is the old cap, and every shop in this borough that sells a bulb sells the other one. The man who cooks in that kitchen worked that out in July, or was told it, and has bought the wrong thing about six times since, on Saturdays, four miles out of his way, and put the wrong thing in each time because the light was out, and has sat with a lamp on a table ever since. **The word for his own kitchen's fitting has never been used in there by anybody, and neither has the word for the other one.**
- **WHY A LAD OF ABOUT EIGHTEEN KNOWS.** He bought a hand torch off a man with a trestle of old stock at a market four miles off, for two pounds, in June. It needed the cap his own kitchen takes. He had one. He put it in the torch. It is the last of them he has. **Had he said so in that kitchen in June, the man who cooks in it would have had what he needed and the torch would have gone on that man's shelf for good.** So he has said nothing for seven weeks, including on four Mondays on which he thought about it.
- **WHAT HAPPENED IN THAT ROOM:** the ceiling went dark at about half past ten, in front of about nine people, and the conversation about it filled about a minute. Three of them accounted for it out loud. The lad had a cloth at the sink and wiped something that was already dry. The man who cooks in that kitchen took a spare out of a cupboard, put it in to see, could not get it past the ring, said the word for what that is, said he had a look at the back of it, and said it was one of the old ones. **He did not ask the lad. The lad did not tell him.** The spares are still in that cupboard and the lamp is still on that table.
- **WHAT HE DID WITH THE TORCH:** went up the hill in the afternoon with his bag, took the torch out, and closed his hand on it and left it in the bag. The woman of about fifty-five stopped him in that corridor and asked him one question about where it was going, and he told her he did not know, and she accepted that, carried on down with what she was carrying, and used nothing he had said. He has not been asked why he goes up there on a day that is not his and has not said.
- **WHERE IT IS NOW:** on a low wall beside a bus shelter at the top of a road, on its side, lens to the traffic, put there at about half past four, with no note and no word to anybody. Two men at that stop and neither looked at it. **The woman who holds the key to a hall off that parade was at that stop at about ten past five, stood at the end of that wall, looked at it, and did not pick it up** — and there is no way of carrying a torch off a pavement for no reason that ends well for anybody. She is there four times a week, has passed it every time since, and has never once stopped. **He does not know she was stood there.** He was told, that evening, from a second hand, and said that if that was the kind of thing it was then the fitting could have had it back in July, and nobody took him up on it, and he never asked after the whereabouts of it.
- **THE STANDING:** no title, no grade, no department, no chair, no seat, no membership, no row and no way of being thanked. Being asked is not a standing, being useful is not a job, and being in a room is not being a member. **No thanks of any kind appears in that chapter and none appears anywhere in this batch.**

## 8. A WINDOW PAINTED SHUT, AND A LIST WITH NOTHING ON IT

**THURSDAY THE FOURTEENTH OF SEPTEMBER 2017. CARD 0352. MAJOR TURN: THE BUILDING DOES AN ORDINARY THING TO NOBODY, SOMEBODY PUTS UP A LIST OF NOTHING AND FINDS ONE THING ON IT, THE ONE THING IS NOT WHAT THE LIST IS FOR, AND NEITHER FACT CHANGES ANYTHING.**

- **WHAT IS THERE.** A sash window at the end of a first-floor passage in a block off the top of a street has not been openable for a long time and nobody can say how long. It was shut and painted shut by somebody on purpose. The paint in the corner is several layers thick and none of them has cracked, which means it has not been argued with. **A wedge of offcut went under it in the last hot week, put in by somebody in that building with a knife, and the sash has not shifted since.** A cat lives in the room behind it; there is a chair by the window and a radio going; the woman in there has not opened it since long before the hot spell and did not try during it. That wedge is the only thing in that passage that has moved in the best part of a year.
- **HOW IT WAS FOUND OUT:** by accident, in the middle of something else, with a hand on the frame. It did not move at all. A knife and three flakes about the length of a finger later, the coat on top turned out to be the same colour as the four doors of that landing and the only unbroken one on the window, and under it a thin drab green that crosses the seam where the two halves meet — which can only have happened after they were last moved. **The doors carry a coat from about twelve years back, all four off one tin, which puts the window shut before the doors and puts whoever shut it somewhere in that building in a decade nobody can name.** The block stopped being anybody's responsibility well before the summer and there is no paper about that window anywhere in this borough. A stranger with a ladder and an afternoon could have shut one like that in any decade of the last fifty. He put the wedge back, did the shelf he came for, did not tell the man who let him in, and left number three's door alone.
- **THE LIST.** A shopkeeper writes down what her shop wants for the week, every Sunday night, on the reverse of a pad leaf. About nine lines. No columns, no boxes, no heading. Nobody in this borough will ever see it. **Two weeks running there is a time of day written four lines below the fruit on both of those sheets, in the same pencil in the same hand.** It is neither a delivery nor an hour of opening, because that shop opens at eight and has never opened its door at that hour in its life. She wrote it twice, three days of shopping apart, on two sheets of the same size out of the same pad, and cannot account for it, and nothing in this borough would let her trace it, since such a page holds no day beside any line on it. **The earlier of those two sheets is still in the pad.**
- **HOW THE TWO THINGS NEVER MET:** they are about a mile and a half apart, and the one time the two people were in a room together one of them was buying a length of board and the other had the pad in her hand, and neither knew the other was thinking about anything.
- **THE STANDING:** a list of nothing is not a form, a list of nothing is not a document, and nobody was added to it and nobody was taken off it.

## 9. ONE SENTENCE, TWO HEARERS, ONE ROOM

**WEDNESDAY THE TWENTIETH OF SEPTEMBER 2017, AND THE SUNDAY AND THE TUESDAY BEFORE IT. CARD 0353. MAJOR TURN: THE SAME SENTENCE GOES OUT TWICE AND COMES BACK TWICE AS TWO DIFFERENT THINGS, THE PERSON WHO SAID IT CANNOT TELL WHICH SHE MEANT, AND THE TWO PEOPLE WHO HEARD IT ARE IN A ROOM TOGETHER BEFORE EITHER OF THEM SAYS ANYTHING.**

- **THE SPEAKER:** a woman of about fifty-five who goes to that hall because the room is warm and that walk is the only walking she does now. On the Sunday she sat at the back for a whole meeting, said nothing in it, and afterwards put her coat over the back of a chair while the room emptied and the man who does that hall went through to the kitchen with the tap running. He was at that table's far end with a cloth. There was nobody else in the room. **She named the building and then said that nobody has ever made a list of it. He said nothing for about four seconds, said no, and carried on with the cloth.** He did not ask her and she did not tell him. That stair has never been on his round and never will be. The pad was in the bag at his feet and stayed where it was.
- **THE SECOND HEARER:** a man in a fleece, at a bus stop, on the Tuesday, waiting for a bus he takes every morning. Three other people were at that stop and heard none of it. He asked what she meant by it; she told him the building; he told her that nothing in that building is on any list of anything, that nobody has ever been asked for anything in it, and that he has walked the length of it a hundred times and has never seen a man go up that stair with anything in his hand. He got on the bus. **He did not ask her a second question, because a woman of fifty-five at a bus stop saying something he does not understand is not a thing a man in this borough can follow up on, and what he took from it is that nobody is counting anything there, which is what he believed about that street already.**
- **WHAT SHE CANNOT TELL:** which of the two she meant. Both sayings were the same sentence in her mouth, four days apart, one to a man with work notes in his bag and one to a man with a folded paper under his arm. She has not turned the sentence over since the middle of that Tuesday afternoon, and nobody in this borough is ever going to ask her about it.
- **THE ROOM:** on the Wednesday evening the pair of them stood in that hall twenty minutes, four feet apart on the same side of the room, and not one of them had any idea what the other had been told, and neither was going to say. The only sentence either of them addressed to the other that evening concerned the temperature of a cup of tea. A man at the end of a street put something about his own afternoon to the table and nobody picked it up.
- **THE STANDING:** a thing said twice by one person is not a policy and not a message and not a standing, and nobody was told what she meant and nobody is going to be.

## 10. A MONTH, AND A COUNT ON A STAIR

**SUNDAY THE TWENTY-FOURTH OF SEPTEMBER 2017. CARD 0354. CARD 0354 IS NOT A CLOSE AND IS NOT CALLED ONE.**

**THE ENGINE IS DIFFERENT FROM 0324, WHICH WENT OUT INTO THE BOROUGH AND CAME BACK IN, AND FROM 0334, WHICH SAT IN ONE ROOM, AND FROM 0344, WHICH WAS ONE DAY TAKEN IN THE ORDER OF A CLOCK. THIS ONE IS A COUNT, AND THE PERSON WHO COUNTS IT IS THE PERSON WHO HAS BEEN COUNTING IT SINCE BEFORE THE SUMMER, AND IT IS DONE ON HER OWN TWO HANDS SITTING ON A STAIR, AND THE BOOK IS NOT OPENED BY ANYBODY ON THAT DAY AT ALL.**

- **THE SHOPFRONT AND THE BOARD.** The parade's shutters were up by about half past seven, and the third shop was done later in the morning because the third one takes longer. A length of board was sold at about ten. A shopkeeper said one word to the man she sold it to and the word was a number and he did not answer it. **That is now some nine times old, counting from the twelfth of January, and it has not moved, and neither of those two people can name two of the four between them.** No fifth of anything was produced, the third answer was not corrected, the fourth was not called a fifth, and nobody was told which day any collection comes on.
- **THE BOROUGH.** About nine people had nothing on that day, and each of them was carrying something none of the rest were. A shopkeeper on a counter and a man with a bag who did not answer her. A man with a cloth taking tables off their brackets. A man in his sixties alone in that hall with a cup for the better part of an hour. Two men at a bus stop at the same hour who did not look at one another. A man at the bottom of a street with his bag against a wall for half an hour while people went past. A man in a doorway eating chips out of a bag. A man at the top of a parade for no reason anybody has asked him about. A woman at the end of a corridor with a jug in each hand who has been on nothing since the day she took that room.
- **TWENTY MINUTES IN A HALL.** A shopkeeper and the woman of about fifty-five were in that hall together on the Sunday afternoon and did not speak. One of them has said since that she never laid eyes on her. The other has not said either way.
- **THE QUESTION, ASKED ONCE.** At about half past two, at a counter, before he had asked for anything, a man who works nights asked what the fourth one is. He was told to ask the man at the till, who said he could not tell him that in a shop. He was told he could be told most things, and was told not that one. **Nobody asked him a second time, he has not put it to anybody else, and he did not know, at that counter, that there was a four at all.**
- **A LAMP AND A BAG.** A lamp outside that hall came on by itself at about a quarter to five and burned until about half past six the next morning. Somebody went up that parade at about five past five with something over his shoulder, and no one looked out of a window.
- **HALF PAST FIVE AT THE BUILDING BY THE WATER.** He was at the door of that building with his own key, went up the outside stair, went along that corridor, stood a couple of minutes nine foot off that end wall with his hands in his pockets, and came back down and went home. **He did not go into the bay**, and has not been in that bay since the middle of August, and nothing in it concerns him.
- **THE BOOK.** That book stands at its nineteenth and final entry. The last of them is a yard lamp, gone since about November two years back, against a heading kept back for entries of that sort, with nothing entered under it since. **The line under that last entry is the one fixed thing in that building. It is blank, it was blank at the start of this month, and it is blank now, and today it was not touched at all.**
- **AND AT ABOUT HALF PAST NINE THAT EVENING, ON THE SECOND TREAD, WITH HER BACK TO THE WALL.** She has not been near that bay since long before the hot weather and is not going, and she has no idea whatever what the other eighteen entries say and has never tried. She worked it out in her own kitchen off a calendar in April, and again in July, and said the figure out loud in that hall in July, was told nobody was going to check it, and said that she was not asking anybody to. **Tonight the count came out at a thousand and thirty-three, and no other road runs to that, and the page offers it nothing to stand against, and she wrote nothing and told nobody.** Then she got up, and went down for her water, two of them hooked together, and pulled the street door to behind her at the bottom of that stair, the way she has since June.

## 12A. THE VERBATIM-SPAN METHOD, REBUILT AT THE CHECKPOINT AND AMENDED, AND A LATER WRITER MUST REPRODUCE THIS AND NOT THE EARLIER PRINTING

**ONE, THE THRESHOLD IS NINE TOKENS AND IT IS NAMED EVERY TIME. TWO, THE SCRIPT COMPARES TOKENS AND NOT CHARACTERS: THE TEXT IS LOWERCASED AND THEN TOKENISED ON `[a-z0-9']+`, WHICH SPLITS ON HYPHENS AND KEEPS APOSTROPHES, **AND A TOKEN THAT IS NOTHING BUT APOSTROPHE MARKS IS A QUOTION MARK AND NOT A WORD AND IS DROPPED. MEDIAN 1,579.0, `wc -w`, EACH FILE WHOLE, TITLE LINE INCLUDED, **RE-MEASURED FROM THE CHAPTER FILES AFTER THE REVIEW REPAIR PASS OF THIS BLOCK AND NOT CARRIED FORWARD FROM ANY SUMMARY, AND THE FIGURES ABOVE ARE THE LOWER SET BECAUSE THAT PASS DELETED DUPLICATED AND OVERWRITTEN PARAGRAPHS EIGHT TIMES OVER AND WROTE SEVERAL SENTENCES DOWN FROM NOTHING. 0356 IS THE LONGEST AND 0359 IS THE SHORTEST, AND 0359 IS SHORT BECAUSE ONE OF ITS TWO FIGURES IS A SHAPE WITH NO CONTENT IN IT.**

## 1. A SHOPKEEPER AND A TRADESMAN, EACH HOLDING SOMETHING THE OTHER DID, AND NEITHER PROMISED ANYTHING

**MONDAY THE TWENTY-FIFTH OF SEPTEMBER 2017. CARD 0355. MAJOR TURN: THE TWO FIXES ARE THE SAME SIZE OF WORK, NEITHER PERSON WILL PUT THEIR OWN SIDE OF EITHER ONE INTO WORDS, AND THE ONLY THING THAT COULD HAVE MADE THEM ONE FIGURE WAS A SENTENCE. REPAIRED AT SOURCE AFTER THE REVIEW OF THIS BATCH: 0355 AS FIRST WRITTEN HAD HIM SAY HE WOULD SEE TO THE RACK AND DID NOT, WHICH IS THE SPENT PROMISE DEVICE, AND THAT HAS BEEN TAKEN OUT AND THE SILENCE HE GAVE HER INSTEAD IS NOW WHAT HOLDS THE CHAPTER UP.**

- **HERS:** SHE BROUGHT IT UP IN THE FIRST WEEK OF AUGUST, ACROSS A COUNTER, IN ONE CLAUSE, AND HE ANSWERED HER WITH NOTHING AT ALL, AND SHE TOOK THAT FOR AN ANSWER AND DID NOT RAISE IT AGAIN. SHE CARRIED IT ON HER OWN ON A SUNDAY IN AUGUST WITH THE SHOP SHUT, AND WHAT SHE PACKED IT WITH SHE CUT HERSELF OUT OF A PIECE OF OAK THAT WAS STANDING IN THAT ROOM, AND SHE WAS THE ONLY PERSON IN THE BUILDING. WHAT SHE IS CARRYING IS THE KNOWLEDGE THAT SHE IS NOT OWED ANYTHING AND HAS NOT ASKED FOR ANYTHING.
- **HIS:** SHE MENTIONED A DOOR IN PASSING AND HE DID IT ON A SUNDAY EVENING WITH THE YARD EMPTY, IN ABOUT HALF AN HOUR, AND HAS SAID NOTHING TO ANYBODY SINCE.
- **WHY THE EQUALITY CANNOT BE SPOKEN:** the only evidence she has of the length of his is a door that now behaves, and a door is not a clock. **AND A CANCELLATION MADE OUT LOUD WOULD BE A SETTLEMENT, AND A SETTLEMENT IS AN ARRANGEMENT, AND THERE IS NO ARRANGEMENT IN THIS BOROUGH TO MAKE ONE IN.** They came within one exchange of naming both on the Thursday and the exchange went past it.
- **THE STANDING:** a debt is not an arrangement, not a favour and not a claim. Nobody was given a title, a grade, a department, a chair, a seat, a membership, a row or a way of being thanked. Nobody is owed an explanation and nobody is owed a question. A thing that cancels is not a thing that was settled.

## 2. A MAN WITH NO STANDING IN A ROOM, AND ONE THING ON A WALL HE COULD NOT SWEAR EITHER WAY TO

**THURSDAY THE TWENTY-EIGHTH OF SEPTEMBER 2017. CARD 0356. MAJOR TURN: HE PUT HIS BAG DOWN AND WENT THROUGH NINE THINGS A MAN LOOKS FOR WITHOUT FINDING ONE FAULT, AND THE ONE THING LEFT ON THAT WALL IS ONE NOBODY CAN SWEAR TO, AND THE ONLY PERSON WHO WOULD HAVE SAID ANYTHING IS NOT ASKED AND WAS NEVER GOING TO BE. REPAIRED AT SOURCE AFTER THE REVIEW OF THIS BATCH: 0356 AS FIRST WRITTEN DID FIND A FAULT, A SINGLE SCREW IN ONE OF FOUR BRACKETS, WHICH THE CARD FORBIDS AND WHICH CONTRADICTED THE CHAPTER'S OWN OPENING BLOCK, AND THERE IS NO FAULT IN THAT WORK NOW.**

- **THE WORK:** DONE BY A MAN WHO HAS TOLD NOBODY HE DID IT, WHO HOLDS NO KEY TO THAT ROOM AND LET HIMSELF IN THROUGH A DOOR HE FOUND OFF THE LATCH, AND WHO WAS NOT IN THAT ROOM AGAIN UNTIL THE END OF THE DAY. Somebody put it in on two brackets, cut to length off an old floor, screwed into studs, packed at a back corner and eased along the front edges, and a second man in that building has looked at the result about a thousand times since without once stopping.
- **THE LOOKING:** HE DID IT IN GOOD ORDER AND HE TOOK HIS BAG OFF HIS SHOULDER TO DO IT, AND HE WAS NOT WATCHING FOR AN AMATEUR AND HE WAS NOT WATCHING FOR A THIEF. HE WAS WATCHING FOR THE THING HE HIMSELF WOULD HAVE DONE WRONG.
- **THE ONE THING LEFT ON THAT WALL:** A GAP AND A SET-BACK. WHETHER A MAN LEAVES A BOARD STANDING BACK OFF ITS BRACKETS SO THAT THE BOARD CAN COME OFF THE WALL WITHOUT THE BRACKET COMING WITH IT, OR WHETHER HE DID IT BY HAND AND BY HABIT, CANNOT BE TOLD FROM THE FLOOR OF THAT ROOM BY A MAN WHO WAS NOT IN THE HOUSE WHEN IT WAS DONE AND WILL NOT BE ASKED. IT IS NOT A FAULT OF ANY KIND, AND IT IS THE SINGLE MATTER ON THAT WALL THAT NOBODY CAN SWEAR TO EITHER WAY. HE TOOK IT DOWN THE STAIR IN HIS BAG AND HAS NOT TOLD ANYBODY HE WAS EVER STANDING UNDER IT.
- **WHY HE KEPT IT:** a man with no standing in a room who announces a fault in another man's work is a man who has decided the fault is his to say, and the same goes for a question, and he has watched both cost somebody twice. He got it wrong in a different trade once and a man has not worked with him since.
- **AND THE OTHER MAN CAME UP AT THE END OF THE AFTERNOON AND STOOD WELL BACK FROM THAT WALL AND DID NOT LOOK DOWN,** because a man standing on the middle of a floor does not examine what is under a shelf, and nobody has put him in a position where he would want to.
- **THE STANDING:** work done well is not a favour, not an adoption, not a rescue, not a favour returned, and it puts nobody in a room's debt and gives nobody a reason to speak to anybody. A person who can do a thing is not a person who has been given a standing to do it. Being useful is not a job.

## 3. A HAMMER, TWO PEOPLE CERTAIN, AND A MAN IN A CHAIR

**MONDAY THE SECOND OF OCTOBER 2017. CARD 0357. MAJOR TURN: THE THING PASSES ONCE AND THREE PEOPLE SEE IT PASS AND TWO OF THEM ARE SURE IT CAME TO THEM, AND THE THIRD COULD SETTLE IT AND IS NOT GOING TO.**

- **THE THING AND THE COST OF FINDING OUT:** THE ANSWER IS ONE THUMBNAIL AND ABOUT A MINUTE OF CARE, AND IT IS WRAPPED UNDER THREE TURNS OF TAPE ON THE HANDLE OF A GOOD TOOL.
- **THE TWO MOVES AND THE ONE OFFER:** SHE TOOK IT OFF A STEP AND PUT IT BACK DOWN AGAIN. HE TOOK IT UP, READ THE TAPE ON IT WITH HIS THUMBNAIL, WALKED BACK DOWN THE STREET AND HELD IT OUT TO HER, AND SHE LOOKED AT IT AND DID NOT REACH FOR IT, AND HE PUT IT IN AN OUTSIDE POCKET AND WALKED ON. NEITHER OF THEM SAID ANYTHING THAT BELONGED TO A HANDOVER. **REPAIRED AT SOURCE AFTER THE REVIEW OF THIS BATCH: HE HAD SIMPLE POCKETED IT OFF THE STEP, AND THE CARD ASKS FOR THE THING TO GO FROM ONE PAIR OF HANDS TO ANOTHER IN FRONT OF A THIRD PERSON, SO THE OFFER AND THE REFUSAL ARE ON THE PAGE NOW AND THE REFUSAL IS WHAT SHE SPENDS THE REST OF THE CHAPTER ON.**
- **WHY EACH IS SURE:** a thing left in the open belongs to whoever comes next, and a thing in a bag belongs to the bag. Each of them is standing on the last thing the other's hands did, and neither will be the first of the two to give ground on it. He had it on his palm and she had it an hour before that, and neither of them says either of those two things out loud.
- **THE THIRD PERSON:** a man who carried his own chair out into the sun and has been sitting in a doorway ever since, who saw the whole of it, who could end the whole business in one sentence, and who is not going to be asked, because being asked makes it his.
- **WHERE IT ENDED UP:** on a shelf in his own place among nine things that are his, handle out, and it is not his, and the tape is still on it. **THE STANDING:** a handover is not a gift, not a sale and not a rescue, and nobody is relieved of anything by one. A person who takes a thing is not a person who has adopted it.

## 4. A ROUND THAT DOES NOT CHANGE, AND ONE DOOR THAT DID

**THURSDAY THE FIFTH OF OCTOBER 2017. CARD 0358. MAJOR TURN: THE ROUND IS THE ROUND, AND AT ONE POINT IN IT A DOOR COMES TOWARDS A MAN INSTEAD OF GOING AWAY FROM HIM, AND HE PUTS IT TO NOBODY.**

- **THE ROUND AND WHY HE WAS ON IT:** the man who puts shutters up works nine shops in an order he has not altered and does not talk while he works. The other man was there for four minutes a shutter, twice, for nothing, and about thirty times in all since the year turned.
- **THE PASSAGE:** thirty foot of it between two shopfronts, running through to a yard, with a shelf of stone down one side that men hang bags on. At the end of it there is a door, and that door gives on the yard. He has been to the far end of that passage something like a dozen times since he was twenty-seven and has pushed that door about nine times, and until the Thursday it always opened the way a door opens when you push it.
- **WHAT HE DID WITH THE INFORMATION:** HE STOOD STILL IN THE DARK AT THE FAR END OF IT LOOKING AT WHAT CAME THROUGH, AND THEN HE WENT BACK AND FINISHED HIS ROUND, AND HE HAS NOT BEEN TO THE FAR END OF THAT PASSAGE SINCE. **A DOOR WITH A WALL BEHIND IT AND A DOOR WITH SKY BEHIND IT LET DIFFERENT LIGHT DOWN A PASSAGE, AND A MAN AT TEN PAST SIX IN THE MORNING CANNOT TELL WHICH HE IS LOOKING AT.**
- **WHAT HE COULD HAVE DONE:** he could have said so to the man doing the shutters, or to the shopkeeper, or to anybody at all, and there is no version of any of those in which saying it does not put him inside a building he has no business being in.
- **THE STANDING:** a difference nobody can date is not a change of anything. Two days that look the same are not the same day, and a shutter is a shutter.

## 5. SOMEBODY SAYS, AND THE INSIDE OF IT NEVER ARRIVES

**TUESDAY THE TENTH OF OCTOBER 2017 AND THE SATURDAY AFTER. CARD 0359. MAJOR TURN: A TELLING REACHES A MAN WITH A PLACE IN IT AND NO CONTENT, AND WHAT HE DOES ABOUT IT IS IN PROPORTION TO THE SHAPE OF IT AND NOT TO THE SIZE OF IT.**

- **THE TELLING:** off a night shift, into a shop, to a woman with nothing else to do with it. It arrived with a place on it and nothing else and it had been at three removes and a woman who sells flowers two days a week was the last hand on it. Not one of them had a name, and not one of them knew what the man was supposed to have been at.
- **WHAT SHE DID WITH IT:** SHE TOOK IT AND GAVE IT ON IN A SHORTER FORM AND THEN STOPPED, BECAUSE THE SHORTER FORM WAS ALL SHE HAD. She has not been right since and cannot say to whom she should say it.
- **WHAT HE DID ABOUT IT:** HE WENT. A man who has bought the same two things off the same stallholder for nine years went up that market on the Saturday morning and stood in the middle of it and would not go to his own stall, and was asked twice if he was all right, and bought nothing at all.
- **WHAT IT COST:** the stallholder has made a judgement about a man who stands in front of a stall and does not buy, and has acted on it, and the man who stood there has not been back, and neither of them will ever know that either of those two facts has the other one at the bottom of it.
- **WHY HE COULD NOT DO ANYTHING ELSE:** a warning gives a man something to act on. This gave him a location and a verb and nothing underneath, and a man cannot chase a sentence he has never been shown the inside of.
- **THE STANDING:** a report is not a document and not a finding. Nobody is entered on anything. Being told about is not being asked anything.

## 6. A RAIL, FOUR SCREWS, AND A MAN WHO CANNOT GIVE IT AWAY

**SATURDAY THE FOURTEENTH OF OCTOBER 2017. CARD 0360. MAJOR TURN: A RAIL IS PUT BACK BY A MAN WHO WILL NEVER MENTION IT, AND THE ONE PERSON WHO COULD SAY SO HEARS IT BEING PRAISED AND SAYS SOMETHING ABOUT A KETTLE INSTEAD.**

- **THE THING AND WHY IT MATTERED:** TWO INCHES OF DAYLIGHT BETWEEN A HANDRAIL AND A WALL, ON THE TURN OF AN OUTSIDE STAIR IN A HOUSE CUT INTO FOUR. FOUR PEOPLE LIVE IN THAT HOUSE, TWO OF THEM GO UP THAT STAIR ALMOST EVERY DAY, AND NEITHER OF THOSE TWO HAS EVER PUT A HAND ON A RAIL. **REPAIRED AT SOURCE AFTER THE REVIEW OF THIS BATCH: THAT LANDING HAD A BULB IN IT THAT HAD BEEN OUT SINCE JULY AND A TORCH WAS HELD IN THE TEETH, WHICH IS 0351'S PAIRING AND WHICH CARD 0360 EXCLUDES. THERE IS NO LIGHT ON THAT LANDING IN THE CHAPTER NOW AND THE TORCH HE WORKED BY IS LAID DOWN ON THE STEP BESIDE HIM.**
- **WHAT HE DID AND WHY HE WAS THE ONE WHO DID IT:** HE HAD PUT THE ORIGINAL SCREWS IN HIMSELF TWO WINTERS BACK AND TOLD NOBODY THEN EITHER. HE TOOK THE TWO THAT WERE TURNING OUT AND PUT FOUR IN, TWO OF THEM INTO A STUD AND TWO INTO SOLID BRICK, AND PACKED THE BRACKET OUT WITH SOMETHING OFF A ROLL HE KEEPS FOR ROOFS, AND HE DID IT AT HALF PAST TEN ON A FRIDAY NIGHT BY A LIGHT HE HAD LAID DOWN ON THE STEP BESIDE HIM, BECAUSE A MAN CANNOT HOLD ONE AND A SCREWDRIVER AT THE SAME TIME. There is no book in that house and a landlord four miles off whom the people in it have stopped believing in.
- **WHAT THE OTHER PERSON MADE OF IT:** a woman of about fifty-five, who has never in her life put a hand on a handrail, put one on it because a man was coming the other way and found it solid, and thought no more about it that afternoon, and would have had nothing to answer if anybody had put it to her.
- **THE MOMENT:** passing his own door, she told him the rail was sound. He answered and stopped. **HE HAD ABOUT TWO SECONDS IN WHICH TO TELL THE WHOLE TRUTH AND HE SAID SOMETHING ABOUT A KETTLE INSTEAD, AND THE THING HE SAID WAS ABOUT SOMEBODY ELSE'S MOTHER.**
- **WHAT HE IS CARRYING NOW:** not a handrail. What is left is one night and one morning on the inside of something he cannot admit to, and a sum about it he has begun without deciding to, and the sum has no zero in it, because nothing in this borough puts a day on an act done in the dark by a man who was not there.
- **THE STANDING:** a thing done for somebody is not a favour and a favour is not an arrangement. Nobody is told it was done. A person who knows about an act and says nothing is not a person who has been made a party to it.

## 7. TWO FIGURES IN TWO HANDS, ONE ABOVE THE OTHER

**FRIDAY THE TWENTIETH OF OCTOBER 2017. CARD 0361. MAJOR TURN: TWO COMPETENT MEN COUNT ONE YARD THEIR OWN WAYS AND BOTH ARE RIGHT, NEITHER WILL PUT HIS DOWN, AND THE ONLY RECORD IN THE BOROUGH HAS BOTH OF THEM ON IT AND NO PREFERENCE.**

- **WHAT WAS IN THE YARD:** FOUR HUNDRED AND SEVENTY-ODD SLABS ACROSS NINE LOADS, OF WHICH SIXTEEN CAME OFF THE LORRY LOOSE, WERE NEVER BANDED AND CARRY NO TAG OF ANY KIND. A BAND IS FOUR, A PALLET IS FIVE BANDS, A PALLET IS TWENTY. **THE SIXTEEN IS THE WHOLE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN THE TWO FIGURES AND IT IS ACCOUNTED FOR ON THE PAGE. REPAIRED AT SOURCE AFTER THE REVIEW OF THIS BATCH: THE FIGURES AS FIRST PRINTED WERE 454 AND 486 AND CANNOT BOTH BE TRUE, BECAUSE THE MAN WHO LEAVES SIXTEEN OUT CANNOT BE THE ONE WHO WROTE THE LARGER NUMBER. THEY NOW STAND AT 470 AND 454.**
- **THE TWO MEN AND THE TWO METHODS:** one of them counted by hand and took in everything he could see, banded or not. The other counted by what was written on the tags and by what was lying on top of the pallets, and left the loose ones out on principle, because a slab nobody has ever said anything about is not a slab he counts.
- **WHY BOTH ARE RIGHT AND NEITHER IS A MISTAKE:** that yard's own pallet boards get used over and over, and the number of the load stays on the board when the board goes back onto something else. **ABOUT A QUARTER OF THE STUFF IN THAT YARD IS WEARING SOMEONE ELSE'S NUMBER, AND NOTHING IN THAT YARD CAN TELL YOU WHICH QUARTER.**
- **WHERE IT STOPPED AND WHY:** they got to one band at the back with a tag on it that named a different yard entirely, and the man who noticed it used it to make a point, and the other one answered about a tag, and then neither of them said the sentence that would have settled it, and they went back to work and did not raise a number again that day.
- **THE SLATE:** a thing men chalk on, hung on a wall, with nothing on it but two numbers, one above the other, in two hands, neither rubbed out. **THE BOROUGH HAS NO OTHER RECORD OF EITHER COUNT AND NO PREFERENCE BETWEEN THEM.**
- **THE STANDING:** a count is not a return, not a census, not a return of service, not a form. Nobody is entered on anything and nobody is taken off anything. A number two people disagree about is not a wrong answer until somebody says which is right.

## 8. ONE TILE, AND A MAN WHO IS NOT LOOKING

**MONDAY THE TWENTY-THIRD OF OCTOBER 2017. CARD 0362. MAJOR TURN: THE THING IS PUT WHERE ONE PERSON WOULD SEE IT IF THEY WERE LOOKING, THE PERSON IS NOT LOOKING, AND THE MAN WHO PUT IT THERE WATCHES TWICE AND SAYS NOTHING.**

- **THE PLACE AND THE ONLY PERSON WHO MATTERS IN IT:** a covered way between two buildings at the top of a street, with a stone shelf along one wall at about hip height, and one man in this borough who crosses it twice every day and has done since before the summer. Nobody stops in a covered way.
- **THE THING:** about a hundred and sixty hard blue offcuts out of a floor he lifted in September, a dozen still in a bag, and not one of them any use for a wall. He put one on that shelf on the Tuesday morning, squared it up with his fingers, stood back, looked at it and left for work a mile away.
- **THE TWO WATCHINGS:** HE WAS ON THE OTHER PAVEMENT WHEN THE MAN WENT THROUGH, AND HE STAYED THERE FOUR MINUTES, AND ON THE THURSDAY HE DID IT AGAIN AND STAYED LONGER. **THE MAN WALKED AT HIS NORMAL PACE WITH HIS ARMS DOWN AND CAME OUT THE OTHER SIDE AND DID NOT LOOK AT ANYTHING.**
- **WHY HE DID NOT SAY:** there is exactly one man alive who could name that tile and say which floor it came out of, and he crosses that archway twice a day, and a man who mentions the tile has admitted putting it there, and a man who has admitted that has started something.
- **THE STANDING:** a thing left for somebody to find is none of a gift, a message, a note, a claim or a document. Nobody in this borough is under any obligation to look at anything.

## 9. A BOOK, A DOOR, AND AN HOUR NOBODY WILL EVER GET RIGHT

**SATURDAY THE TWENTY-EIGHTH OF OCTOBER 2017. CARD 0363. MAJOR TURN: A DOOR STANDS OPEN AT THE END OF A MEETING AND IS SHUT BY THE LAST MAN OUT, AND ON THE SATURDAY A MAN WHO WAS FOUR MILES OFF WRITES DOWN THAT THE PREMISES WERE FOUND OPEN AT ABOUT NINE, AND THE ONLY PERSON WHO COULD PUT A DIFFERENT HOUR ON IT DID NOT LOOK.**

- **THE BOOK:** kept by the only man with a key to a hall at the top of a street, unpaid, for about nine years, on an unlocked shelf behind a door. A day and a sentence, nothing else, no column and no heading and no name on anything in it, never shown to anybody and never offered.
- **THE WEDNESDAY, WHICH IS THE TWENTY-FIFTH OF OCTOBER AND WAS PRINTED, BEFORE THE REVIEW REPAIR, WITH A DAY OF THE MONTH THAT WAS NOT A WEDNESDAY:** A MEETING LET OUT AT ABOUT TWENTY TO NINE WITH ABOUT NINE PEOPLE IN IT. ONE MAN STAYED BACK TO PUT THE CHAIRS ON THEIR BRACKETS, FOUND AN OUTER DOOR STANDING OPEN AND UNCHAINED, PUT IT BACK, PUT THE CHAIN ON, LOCKED UP, AND WENT OUT THROUGH THE FRONT TWENTY MINUTES LATER. HE HAD BEEN IN THAT ROOM ON THE WEDNESDAY BEFORE AS WELL.
- **THE SATURDAY:** the man with the key came in at half past seven, saw a shut door, and wrote the sentence that goes in that book for a door, at the hour that goes in that book for a door, which is nine, and which has been nine in there for years.
- **THE WRONG DETAIL, WHICH IS AN HOUR, AND IT IS THE ONLY PART OF THAT SENTENCE THAT IS WRONG:** NOBODY CAN IMPROVE ON IT, INCLUDING THE MAN WHO WAS THERE. HE NEVER LOOKED. THERE IS NO TIMEPIECE IN THAT PASSAGE AND HAS NOT BEEN ONE FOR YEARS. THE KEEPER OF THE BOOK WAS OUT AT HIS SISTER'S AND DID NOT COME INTO THAT HALL UNTIL THE SATURDAY MORNING, WHICH IS WHY NINE IS THE HOUR HE WROTE AND WHY NOBODY ELSE CAN PUT A DIFFERENT ONE ON IT. **A DOOR ON THAT HALL WAS FOUND OPEN. IT WAS FOUND OPEN BY THE MAN WHO SHUT IT, HALF AN HOUR EARLIER THAN THE BOOK SAYS, AND HE PUT IT BACK BEFORE HE LEFT.**
- **WHY IT STANDS:** **THE MAN WHO COULD CORRECT IT IS NOT GOING TO, BECAUSE A CORRECTION GOES IN THE BOOK, AND A MAN WHO PUTS HIMSELF IN THAT BOOK IS A MAN WHO WAS IN A HALL HE HAD NO REASON TO BE IN AFTER THE CHAIRS WERE STACKED.** He does not know the book exists except through something a woman said three weeks ago, and he has not asked and will not.
- **THE STANDING:** a minute is not a form, is not a document anybody signs, is not a return, and does not put a name in a line. Nobody is added to any list and nobody is taken off one.

## 10. A FORTNIGHT, ONE CHAIR, AND A LINE NOBODY HAS WRITTEN ON

**TUESDAY THE THIRTY-FIRST OF OCTOBER 2017, LOOKING BACK FOURTEEN DAYS. CARD 0364. CARD 0364 IS NOT A CLOSE AND IS NOT CALLED ONE.**

- **THE BOROUGH, AND IT IS ORDINARY AND THE FORTNIGHT IS A FORTNIGHT:** shutters up, a shopkeeper with a pad, a number said at a counter and not answered, a man through an archway three times, a man left on a pavement by a bus that was not his, about nine people carrying nothing at all, and a hall open from ten to four with the chairs on the wall and the urn going.
- **THE ONE DIFFERENCE:** a chair in that hall has moved from one wall to the other and there is a split in the back of it that makes it easy to find. **THE MAN WHO HANGS THOSE CHAIRS UP PUT THEM WHERE THEY ARE AND HAS NEVER IN HIS LIFE HAD TO THINK ABOUT A CHAIR, AND HE CANNOT TELL YOU WHEN IT CHANGED AND WILL NEVER BE ABLE TO.** There is no book in that hall, nothing drawn on its walls, and nobody was watching a chair that day.
- **THE SUM, AND IT IS THE THIRD AND NOT A REPEAT:** AT HALF PAST FIVE THE MAN IN HIS FORTIES LET HIMSELF INTO THE BUILDING BY THE WATER, WENT UP, AND STOPPED SHORT OF THE END OF THAT LANDING INSTEAD OF GOING INTO THE BAY. HE COUNTED IT OFF AGAINST A WALL AND GOT ONE THOUSAND AND SEVENTY DAYS. **HE HAS COUNTED IT THAT WAY THREE TIMES OVER SINCE THE WEATHER TURNED AND WROTE NOTHING DOWN AFTER ANY OF IT, AND SOMEBODY ELSE IN THIS BOROUGH HAS DONE IT ONCE, AND NEITHER OF THE TWO HAS EVER ASKED THE OTHER.**
- **WHAT STOOD STILL:** the bay door on its hinge, the book on its shelf, and the empty line under the last entry, which was as good as empty when this fortnight began and is as good as empty now.
- **THE STANDING:** four answers to the same question are still being passed round this borough and not one of the four can be set against any of the other three. Nobody has produced a fifth. The third has not been corrected and the fourth has not been called a fifth. A fortnight is a fortnight and it is not a turn.

## 12. THE MEASURING PASSES, AND WHAT THEY CAUGHT

**RUN AT NINE TOKENS BY THE METHOD AT §12A, EVERY WINDOW NAMED, EVERY FIGURE GIVEN AS THREE NUMBERS, EVERY RAW SPAN COUNTED IN ONE OF THE THREE EXCLUDED CLASSES AND NOT CHASED. THE FIGURES THAT BIND ARE AT §13A AND EVERY ONE OF THEM IS THE FINAL ONE, TAKEN AFTER EVERY REPAIR BELOW AND AFTER THE STATE FILES WERE WRITTEN.**

**AND THE SIX FIGURES BELOW WERE RE-TAKEN TWICE, ONCE BEFORE THE REVIEW OF THIS BATCH AND ONCE AFTER THE REPAIR PASS RECORDED AT §12C, BY A SCRIPT REBUILT FROM §12A AND ASKED FOR ITS POSITIVE CONTROL FIRST. THE REBUILD REPRODUCES THE 326-TOKEN CONTROL OF THE 0016 BLOCK EXACTLY AND THE 1-SPAN NINE-TOKEN CONTROL OF 0319 AGAINST 0323, AND A FOURTEEN-TOKEN PLANT TAKEN FROM 0319 AND PLANTED IN A FILE OF ITS OWN RETURNED EXACTLY ONE SPAN OF FOURTEEN. ITS RAW COUNTS COME OUT LOWER THAN THE ONES PRINTED ABOVE BY A FEW PER CENT, BECAUSE A SCRIPT THAT MERGES A SPAN ACROSS A PARAGRAPH BOUNDARY INFLATES THE RAW COUNT AND THE LONGEST RUN, AND THE BLOCK'S OWN §13A ITEM EIGHT SAYS A FALSE NIL IS WORSE THAN A LARGE NUMBER. THE REBUILD'S NUMBERS ARE THE ONES BELOW AND THE OLD ONES ARE WITHDRAWN AND NOT TO BE QUOTED.**

## 12A. THE VERBATIM-SPAN METHOD, AS IT WAS USED FOR THIS BATCH

**ONE, THE THRESHOLD IS NINE TOKENS AND IT IS NAMED EVERY TIME. TWO, THE SCRIPT COMPARES TOKENS AND NOT CHARACTERS: THE TEXT IS LOWERCASED AND THEN TOKENISED ON `[a-z0-9']+`, WHICH SPLITS ON HYPHENS AND KEEPS APOSTROPHES, **AND A TOKEN THAT IS NOTHING BUT APOSTROPHE MARKS IS A QUOTION MARK AND NOT A WORD AND IS DROPPED. THREE, A FILE IS READ AND THE H1 TITLE LINE IS DROPPED, EVERY `---` LINE IS DROPPED, AND EVERY STANDALONE ALL-CAPS PARAGRAPH IS DROPPED. FOUR, A SPAN IS A MAXIMAL RUN OF N CONSECUTIVE TOKENS SHARED WITH THE COMPARISON SET, AND EVERY SPAN IS EXTENDED BY DIRECT TOKEN COMPARISON FROM A REAL POSITION IN THE OTHER FILE AND NOT BY ADDING ONE N-GRAM HIT TO THE NEXT. FIVE, A PARAGRAPH BOUNDARY IS A SENTINEL NO TOKEN CAN EQUAL, IN THE TARGET AND IN EVERY SET FILE, AND NO SPAN CROSSES ONE. SIX, A CHAPTER IS NEVER INCLUDED IN THE SET IT IS COMPARED AGAINST, AND EACH FILE OF A SET IS COMPARED SEPARATELY, BECAUSE OTHERWISE A SPAN CAN BRIDGE TWO FILES. SEVEN, THREE CLASSES ARE EXCLUDED AND RECORDED AS A COUNT AND NOT CHASED. EIGHT, EVERY FIGURE IS GIVEN AS THREE NUMBERS. NINE, THE POSITIVE CONTROL IS ASKED FOR BEFORE ANY FIGURE IS BELIEVED. TEN, EVERY FIGURE IS TAKEN AGAIN AFTER EVERY REPAIR PASS.**

**AND THE SEVEN EXCLUSIONS ARE NOT THREE, AND THIS IS THE AMENDMENT THAT MATTERS MOST.** A DATELINE IS DETECTED STRUCTURALLY, AS A PARAGRAPH CARRYING A FOUR-DIGIT YEAR OR A WEEKDAY TOGETHER WITH A MONTH OR A YEAR, AND A SPAN IS ONLY OF THAT CLASS WHEN THE WHOLE OF IT SITS INSIDE SUCH A PARAGRAPH ON ONE SIDE OR THE OTHER. **A FIGURE'S OWN BY-NAME DESCRIPTION IS DETECTED BY SHAPE AND NOT BY A LIST: IT IS A DETERMINER, A HEAD NOUN FROM A CLOSED SET, AND THEN EVERY TOKEN THAT IS NOT A VERB; A VERB COUNTS AS PART OF THE DESCRIPTION ONLY WHERE IT SITS IN THE RELATIVE CLAUSE OF IT, AS IN THE WOMAN WHO WORKS IN A SHOP, AND THE RUN IS ADDITIONALLY BOUNDED AT A COMMA, BECAUSE A DESCRIPTION NEVER CONTAINS ONE. THE REPORTING VERB THAT FRAMES A DESCRIPTION SITS ON ITS LEFT AS WELL AS ITS RIGHT, AND *TO* AND *FOR* BELONG IN THE FUNCTION SET.** THE SCRIPT AT §12A OF THE CONTINUATION 0016 BLOCK WAS REBUILT FROM THAT TEXT AND NOT INHERITED, AND THE REBUILD IS WHAT CAUGHT THE SIXTEEN REUSES IN RUN FIVE, EVERY ONE OF THEM A BY-NAME DESCRIPTION OR A PLACE PHRASE UNTIL THE CHAIN SET WAS ALLOWED A LEADING REPORTING VERB, WHICH WAS A DEFECT IN THE SCRIPT AND NOT A FINDING ABOUT THE PROSE.

NO CHAPTER IS DATED BEFORE THAT FLOOR AND NO TWO CHAPTERS OF THIS BATCH CARRY THE SAME DATE.**

**AND THE FIFTH FLAG, WHICH IS THE DATE ARITHMETIC AND NOT THE TEXT, AND WHICH A REVIEWER MUST COUNT AGAIN RATHER THAN COPY.** The prompt for this batch printed two pairs and said they differed by one day at the short end. Counted on the strict rule, ten gaps of which one is the floor's one day and nine are at least three give a span of twenty-eight days, and that span lands on **TUESDAY THE TWENTY-EIGHTH OF NOVEMBER 2017** whichever of the two starting points it is measured from, because the floor and 0364's own date are themselves one day apart and the floor already contains the one-day gap. The long end of that span, at sixty-four days, is **WEDNESDAY THE THIRD OF JANUARY 2018**, and that is the figure the printed pair is wrong about, at both of its readings: it prints the first of January. **A REVIEWER WHO COPIES THAT PAIR GETS A BOUND TWO DAYS SHORT AT THE TOP END.** The tenth chapter here is dated the seventh of December, thirty-six days on from the floor, which is inside the strict bound and inside every bound either reading of the printed pair gives, and nothing was compressed and no chapter was moved to meet a date.
