TOTAL 16,095, TAKEN AFTER THE REVIEW REPAIR PASS AT §12D AND NOT THE ROW PRINTED BEFORE IT, WHICH WAS THE SAME TEN FIGURES AS THEY STOOD AT THE END OF THE WRITING PASS AND WAS WRONG FOR EVERY CHAPTER THE REPAIR TOUCHED. MEDIAN 1,571, `wc -w`, EACH FILE WHOLE, TITLE LINE INCLUDED, **MEASURED FROM THE CHAPTER FILES AFTER EVERY REPAIR RECORDED IN §12C BELOW AND NOT CARRIED FORWARD FROM ANY SUMMARY. 0374 IS THE LONGEST AND 0372 IS THE SHORTEST, AND 0372 IS SHORT BECAUSE THE WHOLE OF IT IS A STAIR AND TWO PEOPLE AND AN OBJECT.**

## 1. A HOUSEHOLD AND A MAN WHO WAS WRONG ABOUT A ROOM

**WEDNESDAY THE FIRST OF NOVEMBER 2017. CARD 0365. HE QUOTED A DAY AND A HALF, SPENT FOUR, FINISHED, AND WENT HOME, AND HE WAS LATE FOR SOMEBODY ELSE, AND SOMEBODY ELSE HAD THE WHOLE OF IT DONE BY HAND THE DAY AFTER HE LEFT.**

A tradesman took a small overhead job in a house at the end of a row and gave the household a figure out of his own experience. The room did not match the description he had been given; the spacing was wrong and there was an obstruction under the plaster that nobody had thought to mention. He undid his own work to get round it, made a filler out of a cutting, carried on for three nights and left before nine on the third.

The household had one warm room in that month of November and lost the use of it. The woman there was in and out of it all week and says now that she does not know what the job cost the man and has never asked.

The lateness belonged to a man half a mile away with a floor of his own to get down, and that man stood about until the middle of the morning, then began, and finished the last of it alone on the Thursday, and has not mentioned the wait since.

On the Friday the household went to somebody else. That man took the work out and put it back in a day and did it with a bead along the joints rather than a skim, and has told people in that yard since that a ceiling like that goes up easy.

When the tradesman came back for a tool bag he had left in a front room, the work was visible from the gate. He did not look up. He asked about something electrical in another room, and the woman gave him the answer, and he went out, and the door of the back room was open the whole time. **A MAN CAME BACK FOR HIS OWN THINGS AND SAID NOTHING ABOUT A CEILING, AND SAID NOTHING ABOUT IT THEN, AND HAS SAID NOTHING SINCE.**

What he left in that yard has not been taken away. There is no chase about it and no hurry was ever set. He left a tool on the wall on the Thursday and collected it on the same Thursday.

## 2. AN OBJECT WITH A USE AND NO PLACE TO USE IT

**SATURDAY THE FOURTH OF NOVEMBER 2017. CARD 0366. A THING FOR A FIRE APPEARED IN A ROOM THAT HAS NEVER HAD A FIRE, THREE PEOPLE SAW IT, NONE ASKED, AND THE MAN WHO BROUGHT IT DOES NOT KNOW THAT THE OTHER TWO LOOKED.**

Somebody else's job had thrown out a set of implements for a hearth. A man in that building had a barrow, a way up to a first floor and a fair claim on his own dwelling, and none of the three solved the problem. He found a room with a hearth breast in it and a woman in it who was not expecting company, and he used that room instead of his own.

He did it at night, without arranging anything with anybody, and left before he was asked anything, and he has not been near the room since.

**ALL THREE OF THE PEOPLE WHO KNOW ABOUT IT ARE WAITING FOR ONE OF THE OTHER TWO TO OPEN IT, AND NONE OF THEM WILL.** One is the woman whose floor it is on; she will not shift it out of her way because shifting it is the admission. One is the neighbour, whose door is never properly shut, and who saw it from her own doorway. One is the man, and he knows only what he himself did.

The woman has used the object itself to hang a jug on, for want of anywhere else in a small room. She has not asked where it came from. Nobody has asked the man. **A THING PUT INTO SOMEONE ELSE'S ROOM BY A MAN WHO GAINES NOTHING AND EXPECTS NOTHING IS NOT A GIFT, NOT A DELIVERY, NOT A BEQUEST AND NOT AN ARRANGEMENT, AND NOBODY IN THAT BUILDING OWES ANYBODY AN ACCOUNT OF WHAT IS ON THE FLOOR.**

## 3. ONE SENTENCE AND TWO ACCIDENTS

**TUESDAY THE SEVENTH OF NOVEMBER 2017. CARD 0367. A SENTENCE OF NINE WORDS WENT ONCE ACROSS A TABLE AND TWO MEN AT THAT TABLE HEARD TWO DIFFERENT THINGS IN IT, AND THE SPEAKER NEVER LEARNS WHICH.**

The subject was a man who used to come into that shop and stopped, in the summer, and is in none of this now. The speaker was closing up and had a jug in her hand. What she said closed the subject.

One hearer took it as a fact about that absent man, and it was, and he had a half-formed addition ready and did not make it.

The other hearer took the identical words as being about himself, and had been on nothing for six years, and had never in that time been the subject of anything said aloud in a room. **A MAN WHO IS ON NOTHING IS NOT THE SAME FIGURE AS A MAN NOBODY HAS ANYTHING TO SAY ABOUT, AND THE DISTANCE BETWEEN THOSE TWO IS WHERE HE IS NOW.**

He will not raise it, because the only route to raising it runs through an admission about what he has been listening for.

**HE CAME IN THAT AFTERNOON WITH A QUESTION OF HIS OWN AND DID NOT ASK IT, AND THAT IS THE PART OF HIM NOBODY SAW.** He has wanted it since the summer and had twice reached the doorway and turned back. He went home not knowing that anything at all had been said in that room before he was through the door of it.

Nobody was entered anywhere. Being discussed is not being asked anything. The speaker has gone on being a shopkeeper.

## 4. TWELVE WEEKENDS ON HIS OWN ACCOUNT

**SUNDAY THE TWELFTH OF NOVEMBER 2017. CARD 0368. HE DID IT BETWEEN AUGUST AND NOVEMBER, NOBODY ASKED, NOBODY STOPPED HIM, AND NOW THAT IT IS FINISHED NOT ONE PERSON IN THAT BUILDING CAN SAY WHAT IT WAS FOR.**

A hard surface was laid down one side of a block of flats, out of a man's own wages, in his own time, in three passes. He told nobody he was starting. He worked to the same routine as anybody who only has Saturdays.

Two people had cause to complain afterwards and neither took it anywhere. One has water arriving under her back step on the days it rains, which she deals with by hand. One lost a planted bed she had looked at every morning for years, and did make him move it once, and it went to the other corner.

The other one told the man who does floors, on a Wednesday, in her front room, with tea. **HE KNEW WHO HAD LAID IT AND COULD HAVE TOLD HER AND DID NOT, AND WHAT STOPPED HIM WAS NOT LOYALTY: NAMING A MAN TO A WOMAN WITH A WET STEP MAKES HIM SOMETHING HE HAS NEVER BEEN, AND HE IS ON NOTHING AT ALL AND COULD NOT BE PUT ON A LIST OF ANYBODY'S, AND A MAN WHO DOES THAT TO PEOPLE HAS DONE IT BEFORE.**

Six people there have six descriptions of the surface. Not one of the six is a reason. The only description anybody could put a hand on is also the one nobody can check, because it depends on what the man was thinking and he has not said.

**A CHANGE MADE TO A BUILDING IS NOT A PERMISSION, NOT A CLAIM AND NOT A RESCUE, AND THE CAPACITY TO DO A THING IS NOT A STANDING TO DO IT.**

## 5. A WEEKLY ERRAND AND A MORNING IT DID NOT HAPPEN

**FRIDAY THE SEVENTEENTH OF NOVEMBER 2017. CARD 0369. IT DID NOT COME, HE FOUND OUT AT TEN PAST SIX WITH NOTHING TO SAY, AND SOMEBODY ELSE ASKED FOR ONE ONCE AND WILL NOT ASK AGAIN.**

A shop has a chest at the back that needs ice. For about five months one man has been the one who fetched it, on a route he was already driving, on a set morning, and the money has gone into the till at the retail figure and no paper of any kind has ever existed.

This week he was boxed in behind a loaded lorry that was not going to move, and he waited, and he was two hours late getting clear, and he did not divert for another sack, because that is not the arrangement even if it is not called one.

A man who works nights has bought his ice at that shop for years. That afternoon he found the chest down, asked the shopkeeper whether she had any, and was told she had not. He has not put the question to her since, and buys elsewhere, and the shop is further on and shuts sooner.

**THE MAN WHO WAS BRINGING IT LEARNED NOTHING FROM ANYBODY. HE CAME IN AT TEN PAST SIX AND FOUND TWO PEOPLE ALREADY AT THAT COUNTER AND ABOUT TEN SECONDS IN WHICH SOMETHING COULD HAVE BEEN SAID, AND NEITHER OF THEM GAVE HIM ANYTHING TO SAY IT WITH, AND HE PAID FOR WHAT HE CAME IN FOR AND WENT OUT.**

Nothing was put to anybody afterwards, then or since. There is no debt in it and no falling-out, and on the Saturday he brought two sacks because a load had come in, and she took one of them.

## 6. ONE THING WANTED BY TWO MEN

**WEDNESDAY THE TWENTY-SECOND OF NOVEMBER 2017. CARD 0370. BOTH WANTED IT, ONE BOUGHT IT IN FRONT OF THE OTHER, THE OTHER WAS TOLD LATER AND WAS ASKED A QUESTION HE ANSWERED WITH ONE WORD, AND NEITHER OF THEM WILL RAISE IT.**

A builder's barrow was left at a shop against what was owed on an account, and a card with a price on it was taped to the tray, and there was no interest in it and no use for it and it stood in a passage from the tenth of November to the twenty-second, which is twelve days.

The man in his thirties wanted it, came into that shop four times in those twelve days, stopped at it twice and said nothing on any of them. The man in his forties wanted it, paid for it, and then had to take it out onto a pavement and secure it, which took ten minutes, in full view of the other man walking the length of that parade. The other man did not stop and was not looked at.

Fourteen days after that, on the Wednesday of the sixth of December, the shopkeeper found a gap at her rack and said two things into it, one of which was a question. **HE ANSWERED THE QUESTION WRONGLY, NOT DELIBERATELY, AND SHE DOES NOT KNOW THAT HE HAD PAUSED THERE, AND SHE IS NOT GOING TO ASK, BECAUSE ASKING WOULD SAY ALOUD THAT SHE HAD BEEN WATCHING HIM.**

They have worked the same yard since. Wanting is not claiming. Nobody is given a place, a turn or a row, and the man who went without is not aggrieved and the man who got it is not pleased.

## 7. NINE YEARS OF A FIGURE THAT COSTS NOTHING

**SUNDAY THE TWENTY-SIXTH OF NOVEMBER 2017. CARD 0371. HE IS WRONG, IT COSTS NOBODY ANYTHING, ONE PERSON WORKED IT OUT BY ACCIDENT, AND HE IS NOT TOLD.**

A man who buys sand has stated the weight of a sack wrongly for nine years, in shops, in yards, and to drivers he does not know. Nobody has corrected him because nobody who hears him knows the answer.

It costs nothing for two reasons, and the second is the one that saves him. The first is that he never lifts one. The second is that the material is weighed where it is loaded and priced there, so what a sack weighs is not on anybody's bill.

The only thing in the chapter with a consequence attached to it is unrelated. A nail came up out of the bed of the lorry, a bag opened along its length where the nail caught it, and a small part of a sack's worth of that sand went across the concrete in one piece and set where it landed. That went back on the stack with a shovel inside five minutes, and the concrete under it is a shade darker than the rest of that apron and has stayed that way.

The woman of about fifty-five came through that gate on the Sunday with two jugs and stopped, because a man was standing on a stack. He made an offhand remark to somebody else about the weight. **SHE WORKED IT OUT INSIDE A FEW SECONDS, BECAUSE SHE BOUGHT THE SAME MATERIAL HERSELF IN THE SUMMER FOR A BAY OF HER OWN FRONT AND STOOD IN HER OWN WINDOW AND COULD NOT SEE HOW DEEP IT WENT, AND NINE OF THEM DO NOT MAKE WHAT HE SAYS.**

She went on to her stop. There is no version of telling him that improves anything: he would tell her there is no difference between one of those and another, and carry on shovelling, and she would have walked up that lane for that. A wrong figure is not a fraud and nobody has been cheated, and it is not a wrong answer until somebody says which is right.

## 8. HEAVY, AND NOBODY TO GIVE IT BACK TO

**THURSDAY THE THIRTIETH OF NOVEMBER 2017. CARD 0372. IT ARRIVED IN HIS HANDS, HE CANNOT ASK WHERE FROM, HE CANNOT RETURN IT, HE KEPT IT, NOBODY HAS ASKED HIM FOR IT, AND IT IS STILL THERE.**

Two men were moving a heavy thing up a stair in a block of flats for a job in a flat at the top, and the tenant was not in and had not been in for days. The turn defeated them. A third man was standing in his own doorway with his bag, because it is his doorway, and one of the two said four words to him, and he took the weight.

They got it round. They set it down. One of them said the tenant was not in and that they would come back for it, and then said something that meant put it off the stair, and then both of them went down and out. The passage of that stair is too narrow to leave a thing in.

**HE IS LEFT HOLDING IT. HE CARRIED IT BACK DOWN ONE FLIGHT AND PUT IT DOWN AGAINST THE WALL OF THAT HALF-LANDING, OPPOSITE HIS OWN DOOR, AND IT IS STILL THERE.**

He cannot return it. There is nothing written on it and nothing to identify the man who had it, and the only address he has is the flat at the top of that block, with a door that is not being answered, so returning it means standing up there holding something he cannot account for in front of a woman who does not know him. And a man who hands a thing back has conceded it was never his.

It is in the way of a door on that landing, and the woman who lives across that landing from him has had to go past it sideways every evening since the thirtieth of November. **NEITHER OF THEM HAS RAISED IT AND NEITHER IS GOING TO.** A thing handed over is not a gift, nobody is relieved of anything by it, and having a thing you did not ask for is not having accepted it.

## 9. THREE PEOPLE WHO EACH HAD A REASON OF THEIR OWN

**MONDAY THE FOURTH OF DECEMBER 2017. CARD 0373. ONE MAN WAS SEEN BY THREE PEOPLE WHO DID NOT KNOW ABOUT EACH OTHER, AND NOTHING HAPPENED TO HIM.**

He lost part of his day because a house was shut, and sat in the cold for three quarters of an hour, and then went and did something else. He worked, was paid in cash, ate standing up, bought something small, spent the afternoon in a yard and went home.

A shopkeeper at her counter, counting stock for a week, noticed a purchase that has been made on that counter for years and was not made, and thought about her order and not about him.

A man in his thirties, standing on a pavement with nothing to do, saw a man he does not know take a short flight of steps in two halves and stop. He told nobody and would not, and it is not the sort of thing a man goes round reporting.

A man in his sixties, sitting in the sun with a cup, took in from a distance a man stopping in a road and looking upward, and read nothing into it at all, and went home, and could not describe the man to anybody.

**NONE OF THE THREE WAS WATCHING HIM, NONE KNEW THE OTHER TWO WERE OUT, AND NONE WILL SAY ANYTHING. HE HAS NO IDEA AND WILL NOT BE TOLD, AND BEING SEEN IS NOT A STANDING AND NOTHING WAS ENTERED ANYWHERE.**

## 10. FOURTEEN DAYS, ONE SMELL, ONE FIGURE

**THURSDAY THE SEVENTH OF DECEMBER 2017. CARD 0374. CARD 0374 IS NOT A CLOSE AND IS NOT CALLED ONE. THE FORTNIGHT IN IT IS A FORTNIGHT AND NOT A TURN OF ANYTHING.**

The borough did what it does. Shutters, a counter, a coil of wire and a bag of plugs, a man off nights in a parade, a man on a wall with a cup, a hall on a meter with about fourteen people through it on the Sunday and a man behind a counter whom nobody asked anything, and a smell in that parade that was already gone by the time that hall opened its door at ten.

The one thing different is a smell. It is sweet and it is brown and it comes in under an awning in the mornings and it is gone by ten and it has not come back in the afternoon. **TWO PEOPLE CAN DATE IT CLOSELY, BECAUSE THEY STARTED NOTICING IT LATER THAN IT ARRIVED. THE MAN WHO WALKS THAT STREET SEVERAL TIMES A DAY AND HAS DONE FOR MONTHS CANNOT DATE IT AT ALL, AND HE HAS TRIED, STANDING THERE ON PURPOSE TWICE SINCE THE START OF THE MONTH, AND FAILED, BECAUSE HE WAS THERE EVERY SINGLE MORNING BEFORE IT AND AFTER IT AND THERE IS NOTHING TO SORT THEM BY.**

Three explanations are available in that borough and none of them fits, and nobody has gone to look. The finding is that it does not matter and it is there. Nobody has turned anything over.

Four answers to the same question were given at a counter in one short sitting, by three people who each had a point, and the four cannot be set against one another, because none of them is about the same sort of thing as the other three. The question is still a question. Nobody answered anything.

He went up the outside stair of a building by the water for about an hour's work and, coming down, stood at the end of a corridor where the cold from the yard was coming in. **OFF THAT END THERE IS AN ALCOVE WITH A DOOR IN IT THAT HAS NEVER LATCHED, AND A BOOK ON A SHELF INSIDE IT, AND HE LOOKED IN AND DID NOT GO IN, AND HE DOES NOT KNOW THERE IS A BOOK.**

**A LINE UNDER THE LAST ENTRY IN THAT BOOK HAS BEEN BLANK FOR ONE THOUSAND ONE HUNDRED AND SEVEN DAYS. NOBODY WENT IN, NOBODY OPENED IT, NOBODY WROTE ANYTHING DOWN AND NOBODY COUNTED ANYTHING.** The tenth of the ten chapters of this batch is the only one that prints a day-count and it prints it once, in its own body, and the only person in this borough who could have arrived at that figure by counting did not count.

## 12. THE MEASURING PASSES, AND WHAT THEY CAUGHT

**RUN AT NINE TOKENS BY THE METHOD AT §12A, EVERY WINDOW NAMED, EVERY FIGURE GIVEN AS THREE NUMBERS, EVERY RAW SPAN COUNTED IN ONE OF THE THREE EXCLUDED CLASSES AND NOT CHASED. THE FIGURES THAT BIND ARE AT §13A AND EVERY ONE OF THEM IS THE FINAL ONE, TAKEN AFTER EVERY REPAIR BELOW AND AFTER THE STATE FILES WERE WRITTEN.**

1. **THE POSITIVE CONTROL WAS ASKED FOR FIRST, BEFORE ANY FIGURE WAS BELIEVED, AND IS THE THREE THINGS §12A NAMES.** `state/open-threads.md` AGAINST `state/continuity.md` READ 3,737 RAW SPANS AND A LONGEST RUN OF **326 TOKENS, WHICH REPRODUCES THE FIGURE OF THE 0016 AND 0017 BLOCKS TO THE TOKEN AND IS WHAT A CONTROL IS FOR; THE RAW COUNT HAS NOW READ 4,167, THEN 4,241, THEN 3,734 AGAINST THAT SAME 326 AND IT MOVES BECAUSE BOTH FILES ARE EDITED, WHICH IS A CHECK AND NOT A CONSTANT.** 0319 AGAINST 0323 READ 1 RAW SPAN OF NINE AND 0 REUSES, **AND THE SPAN IS A FIGURE'S OWN BY-NAME DESCRIPTION, WHICH IS THE FIFTH BLOCK IN A ROW THAT HAS REPRODUCED THAT CONTROL.** A FOURTEEN-TOKEN PLANT TAKEN FROM 0319 AND PLANTED IN A FILE OF ITS OWN RETURNED EXACTLY ONE SPAN OF FOURTEEN.
2. **THE RAW COUNTS BELOW COME OUT LOWER THAN THE 0017 BLOCK'S OWN AFTER A REBUILT DETECTOR, WHICH §12B OF THAT BLOCK CALLS THE SAFE DIRECTION, AND EVERY RAW SPAN IN EVERY WINDOW BELOW IS OF ONE OF THE THREE EXCLUDED CLASSES AND IS COUNTED AND NOT CHASED.**
3. **WHAT THE PASSES CAUGHT IN THE CHAPTERS, AND EVERY REPAIR WAS MADE IN THE CHAPTERS AND NOT IN A FILE.** NINE REUSES INSIDE THIS BATCH'S OWN TEN CHAPTERS AND TWELVE ACROSS THE THREE NAMED CHAPTER WINDOWS AND NONE IN THE FIFTH, and every one of them was real: two people in 0373 and 0374 describing one Monday in a kitchen in the same words; a phrase about a lane off the Cleeve road standing in 0365 and 0371; a man in a yard in 0369 and 0373; a landing with four doors in 0366; a jug and an hour in 0366; a quarter of an hour in a back room in 0367; a hall at the top of a street in 0368; a Sunday morning in 0368; a hundredweight of nothing in 0371; a stone on a stair in 0372; a street at ten past ten in 0373; and six spans in 0374 all describing the register, the recess and the book in the bay exactly as 0364 had described them, which is the class §12B is about, a chapter reproducing a file's account of a different thing. Every one was repaired at source and every one was re-taken afterwards. **AND THE DAY-COUNT PASSAGE IN 0374 WAS CUT AND WRITTEN AGAIN FROM NOTHING RATHER THAN PATCHED, FOR THE SAME REASON, AND THE BINDING FIGURE OF THAT PASSAGE IS UNCHANGED AT ONE THOUSAND ONE HUNDRED AND SEVEN.**
4. **AND THE FIGURES THAT WERE NOT AT ZERO, RE-MEASURED ONE BY ONE AFTER THE REVIEW REPAIR PASS OF THIS BLOCK, BECAUSE THREE OF THE FOUR CLAIMS ABOVE WERE FOUND BY THAT PASS TO BE OVERSTATED AND A FIGURE A LATER WRITER IS TOLD TO TRUST MUST BE RIGHT.** *ELEVEN* AND *ELEVENTH* WERE IN SEVEN CHAPTERS ON FIRST TAKING, MOSTLY AS HOURS, AND *FORTY* WAS IN FOUR CHAPTERS AS A WEIGHT AND A LENGTH AND A MAN'S AGE, AND *SPRING* WAS IN 0371 AS A SEASON, AND *THERE IS NO FORM* WAS IN 0368, AND *A WINTER* WAS IN 0365 AND NOT IN 0366, WHICH IS WHAT §12C ITEM 2 GOT WRONG. **ALL OF THOSE ARE AT ZERO IN ALL TEN CHAPTERS NOW, DATELINES INCLUDED, AND *ELEVEN* AT ZERO IS TRUE ONLY SINCE THE REVIEW REPAIR PASS, WHICH FOUND IT STILL IN 0372 AS A TIME OF DAY.** *A TUESDAY* AND *A FRIDAY* AS THE TWO-WORD PHRASE ARE AT **ZERO** IN ALL TEN CHAPTERS AND NOT AT ONE IN 0367 AND ONE IN 0369: what is in 0367 is *that TUESDAY* and what is in 0369 is *ON FRIDAY*, both of them inside all-caps paragraphs, and the body of every chapter carries only ordinary weekday phrases such as *the Tuesday* and *the Friday*. *A SHED* IS AT ZERO AS A WHOLE WORD AND THE ONLY HIT ANY MEASUREMENT CAN STILL SEE IS THE STRING OF LETTERS INSIDE *FINISHED* IN AN ALL-CAPS PARAGRAPH OF 0368, WHICH AN ARTICLE-STRICT MEASUREMENT PASSES AND AN UNQUALIFIED ONE IN A STATE FILE MAY NOT, **AND THAT IS WHY A FIGURE IN A HAND-OVER HAS TO CARRY ITS MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN ITS CLAIM.** 0374 IS THE ONLY CHAPTER THAT USES THE WORD *FORTNIGHT*, SIX TIMES, WHICH IS THE CARD'S OWN SUBJECT AND NOT A SEASON.
5. **AND ONE FIGURE THAT IS ZERO ONLY AFTER A QUALIFIER, WHICH GOES IN EVERY FILE THAT PRINTS IT.** *TIDEGLASS* IS AT TEN AND AT TEN WITH THE DATELINES REMOVED, ONE IN EACH DATELINE AND NOWHERE ELSE. *NACRE*, *RIVER STACKS* AND EVERY DISTRICT NAME ARE AT ZERO. *THE NINTH* IS AT ZERO AND NO CHAPTER OF THIS BATCH IS DATED THE NINTH OF ANYTHING, WHICH WAS A CONSTRAINT ON THE CALENDAR AND NOT A COINCIDENCE.

## 12A. THE VERBATIM-SPAN METHOD AS IT WAS BUILT FOR THIS BATCH, AND TWO THINGS THAT WERE WRONG IN THE FIRST BUILDING OF IT

**ONE, THE THRESHOLD IS NINE TOKENS AND IT IS NAMED EVERY TIME. TWO, THE SCRIPT COMPARES TOKENS AND NOT CHARACTERS, ON `[a-z0-9']+` APPLIED TO LOWERCASED TEXT, AND A TOKEN THAT IS NOTHING BUT APOSTROPHE MARKS IS A QUOTATION MARK AND IS DROPPED. THREE, THE H1 TITLE LINE IS DROPPED, EVERY `---` LINE IS DROPPED, AND EVERY STANDALONE ALL-CAPS PARAGRAPH IS DROPPED. FOUR, A SPAN IS A MAXIMAL RUN OF N CONSECUTIVE TOKENS SHARED WITH THE COMPARISON SET, EXTENDED BY DIRECT TOKEN COMPARISON FROM A REAL POSITION IN THE OTHER FILE. FIVE, A PARAGRAPH BOUNDARY IS A SENTINEL NO TOKEN CAN EQUAL, IN THE TARGET AND IN EVERY SET FILE, AND NO SPAN CROSSES ONE. SIX, A CHAPTER IS NEVER IN THE SET IT IS COMPARED AGAINST AND EACH FILE OF A SET IS COMPARED SEPARATELY. SEVEN, THREE CLASSES ARE EXCLUDED AND RECORDED AS A COUNT. EIGHT, EVERY FIGURE IS GIVEN AS THREE NUMBERS. NINE, THE POSITIVE CONTROL IS ASKED FOR FIRST. TEN, EVERY FIGURE IS TAKEN AGAIN AFTER EVERY REPAIR.**

## 1. WHAT THE MAN OF THAT HOUSE DID WITH A MORNING

A tradesman came to a kitchen off the Cleeve road on the eighth of December for a weeping joint and found the front edge of a worktop gone soft. Nobody had asked for that. The woman of the house was at work. The man of the house said one word and went out to his own job and did not come back until the evening. The tradesman did the extra work on his own, left nothing written down, and has not mentioned it since. **HE WAS NEVER ASKED FOR IT BY ANYBODY, HE DID NOT PUT IT IN THE MIDDLE OF THE JOB HE WAS THERE TO DO, AND HE SAID NOTHING ABOUT IT TO THE MAN WHO TOLD HIM TO GET ON WITH IT OR TO ANYBODY ELSE, AND THE ONLY REASON ON THE PAGE IS THAT HE COULD NOT SEE WHAT A MAN WHO HAD BEEN GIVEN SOMETHING WAS SUPPOSED TO SAY.**

## 2. A THING HE STILL HAS AND HAS NOT ASKED ABOUT

A man going to a van at the top of a street set a chest down in the crook of a builder's arm and carried on at the same pace. The builder had no arm free and did not turn his head. **HE IS NOT LOOKING FOR AN EXPLANATION AND HE IS NOT GOING TO BE THE ONE TO START IT. The giver was clearing a house and put it down in the space there was, and has not given it a thought since, and it went into a garage in a terrace two streets off, and the man who carried it out does not know whose garage that is.**

## 3. A THING TWO MEN WANT AND NEITHER ASKS FOR

One question about when a shop opens sits inside the head of the man in his forties and inside the head of the man who works nights, and neither of them will put it to the woman who works in a shop, and neither will put it to the other. **SHE HAS ANSWERED IT IN THAT ROOM TWICE IN FRONT OF BOTH OF THEM AND BOTH OF THEM HEARD IT AS SOMETHING ELSE.** One of them took a person being in early and let the rest of it go past him. The other took a woman in a bad mood on her feet and did not follow it. **WANTING TO KNOW IS NOT ASKING AND BEING ASKED NOTHING IS NOT A THING ANYBODY MAY COMPLAIN ABOUT, AND THE ANSWER IS STILL IN THE ROOM AND STILL AVAILABLE TO BOTH OF THEM.**

## 4. A LANDING THAT WENT DARK EARLY, AND THREE PEOPLE WHO SAID NOTHING

A light on a landing came on earlier than it had any business coming on. Three people in that block worked out three different reasons for it inside a week and none of them told anybody, and the man who could have gone at it was under that landing in his own hand the following week and looked up at the fitting and went on. **A FAULT IS NOT A FINDING UNTIL SOMEBODY SAYS WHICH OF TWO THINGS IT IS, AND NOBODY HAS SAID, AND IT GOES ON BEING DIFFERENT.**

## 5. ONE NO, AND NOTHING AFTER IT

A man in his thirties tried to give a freezer to a man in his forties at the kerb of a shop and was refused in one word with nothing behind it, and he put it back in the pickup and shut the tailgate. **HE HAS NOT PUT IT TO A SECOND PERSON AND HE IS NOT GOING TO. The only person within earshot had her back to the window and did not turn round and has never asked.**

## 6. A COLD MORNING AND A MACHINE, AN HOUR APART

Two small things failed on one man on one day and he straightened both himself inside about a minute each and told nobody. A man in his thirties stood through the first of them in the street and then stood at the end of the counter through the second and spoke to neither the man nor the woman. **THE MAN IN HIS THIRTIES HAS TOLD THE MAN WITH THE VAN NOTHING AND THE WOMAN AT THE TILL NOTHING, AND HE HAS NOT PUT THE TWO OF THEM NEAR EACH OTHER IN HIS HEAD, AND HE IS NOT GOING TO. TWO THINGS THAT HAPPEN TO A MAN ARE NOT A PATTERN.**

## 7. A CHEST, TEN DAYS, AND TWO PEOPLE WHO LOOKED AT THE SAME WALL

A chest stood on a landing because two men needed the floor of a room and could not get past it. It left the building on an ordinary Friday with nobody asked. **THE WOMAN WHO LIVES ON THAT LANDING AND THE MAN WHO WORKS NIGHTS STOOD AT THE SAME END OF THAT LANDING ON THE SAME MORNING LOOKING AT THE MARK IT LEFT AND NEITHER OF THEM SAID A WORD, AND HE CARRIES IT IN A YARD HE CANNOT GET PAST AND DOES NOT KNOW WHOSE IT WAS.**

## 8. FIVE WORDS ON A STAIR

A man in his sixties said five words to nobody while a man in his thirties went past him in a passage. The words were about a man he had been thinking about, four streets away. The man in his thirties took them as being about a man on the floor above him, and he took them correctly. **THE MAN WHO SAID THEM BELIEVED ALL DAY THAT THE OTHER ONE HAD UNDERSTOOD, AND HE WAS NEVER TOLD OTHERWISE AND WILL NOT BE, AND NEITHER OF THEM WILL MENTION IT AGAIN.**

## 9. A WALL THAT IS BETTER THAN IT IS SAID TO BE

A man who has traded out of a yard for a long time says a class of wall will not take a screw, and has said it longer than the man who works for him has been in that yard. The younger man found out otherwise on his knees with a claw hammer, with a batten he had fixed the hard way in the autumn still hanging. **HE IS NOT TOLD, HE IS NOT GOING TO ASK, AND EVERY FIXING PUT IN ON THE STRENGTH OF THE OLDER MAN'S BELIEF IS STILL HOLDING EXACTLY WHERE IT SHOULD BE.**

## 10. WHAT A BOROUGH DID IN A FORTNIGHT

The same people did the same rounds at the same hours and nothing in the fortnight was different. A smell under an awning is still there. Four answers to the same question are still going round and cannot be put beside one another and a fifth has not joined them. **A LINE UNDER THE LAST ENTRY OF A BOOK ON A SHELF IN AN ALCOVE AT THE END OF A CORRIDOR IN A BLOCK BY THE WATER IS AT ONE THOUSAND ONE HUNDRED AND FIFTY-ONE DAYS AND NOBODY HAS PUT A FIGURE ON IT, AND NOBODY WENT IN, AND THE ONE MAN IN THAT BOROUGH WHO COULD HAVE COUNTED IT OUT BY HAND HAS NOT COUNTED IT, AND THERE IS NOBODY THERE WHO COULD TELL YOU WHAT THE RULE UNDER THAT LAST LINE IS FOR, AND THAT WAS THE CASE A FORTNIGHT AGO AND WILL BE THE CASE IN ANOTHER FORTNIGHT.**

## 12A. THE VERBATIM-SPAN METHOD AS IT WAS BUILT AND REBUILT FOR THIS BATCH, AND THE TWO THINGS THAT WERE WRONG IN THE FIRST BUILDING

**ONE, THE THRESHOLD IS NINE TOKENS AND IT IS NAMED EVERY TIME. TWO, THE SCRIPT COMPARES TOKENS AND NOT CHARACTERS, ON `[a-z0-9']+` APPLIED TO LOWERCASED TEXT, AND A TOKEN THAT IS NOTHING BUT APOSTROPHE MARKS IS A QUOTATION MARK AND IS DROPPED. THREE, THE H1 TITLE LINE IS DROPPED, EVERY `---` LINE IS DROPPED, AND EVERY STANDALONE ALL-CAPS PARAGRAPH IS DROPPED. FOUR, A SPAN IS A MAXIMAL RUN OF NINE CONSECUTIVE TOKENS SHARED WITH THE COMPARISON SET, EXTENDED BY DIRECT TOKEN COMPARISON FROM A REAL POSITION IN THE OTHER FILE. FIVE, EVERY SPAN IS ASSERTED CONTIGUOUS BY DIRECT TOKEN COMPARISON AND NOT BY ADDING ONE N-GRAM HIT TO THE NEXT. SIX, A PARAGRAPH BOUNDARY IS A SENTINEL NO TOKEN CAN EQUAL, IN THE TARGET AND IN EVERY SET FILE, AND NO SPAN CROSSES ONE. SEVEN, A CHAPTER IS NEVER IN THE SET IT IS COMPARED AGAINST AND EACH FILE OF A SET IS COMPARED SEPARATELY. EIGHT, THREE CLASSES ARE EXCLUDED AND RECORDED AS A COUNT, AND A DATELINE IS DETECTED STRUCTURALLY BY A FOUR-DIGIT YEAR OR A WEEKDAY WITH A MONTH OR A YEAR, A BY-NAME DESCRIPTION IS DETECTED IN TOKENISED FORM BY A DETERMINER SCANNED ACROSS THE WHOLE SPAN AND A HEAD NOUN FROM A CLOSED SET WITH THE RUN BOUNDED AT A COMMA, AND A BOROUGH'S OWN RECURRING PLACE NOUN IS DETECTED BY A CLOSED SET. NINE, THE CONTROL IS ASKED FOR FIRST. TEN, EVERY FIGURE IS TAKEN AGAIN AFTER EVERY REPAIR AND AGAIN AT THE END, BECAUSE THE STATE FILES ARE IN THE SET OF RUN FOUR AND THE FIGURE MOVES WHEN THEY ARE.**

**AND THE TWO THINGS THAT WERE WRONG IN THE FIRST BUILDING, RECORDED BECAUSE A LATER WRITER WILL REBUILD IT AGAIN. ONE: A DATELINE EXCLUSION THAT FIRES ONLY WHEN A SPAN BEGINS AT THE HEAD OF ITS PARAGRAPH IS NOT THE METHOD, WHICH ASKS WHETHER THE WHOLE OF A SPAN SITS INSIDE SUCH A PARAGRAPH, AND A SPAN THAT BEGINS INSIDE A DATE AND RUNS OUT OF IT IS A DATELINE AND WAS BEING REPORTED AS A REUSE. TWO: THE COMMA THAT BOUNDS A BY-NAME RUN BELONGS TO THE TEXT THE RUN COVERS, NOT TO THE PARAGRAPH IT SITS IN, AND APPLYING IT TO THE PARAGRAPH REPORTED FIVE FIGURES' OWN DESCRIPTIONS AS REUSES. **A PASS THAT ADDS AN ENTRY TO A LIST IS A PASS THAT HAS NOT FOUND A DEFECT, AND NEITHER OF THESE WAS FOUND BY THE PASS; BOTH WERE FOUND BY REPRODUCING A FIGURE AN EARLIER BLOCK HAD ALREADY MEASURED, WHICH IS THE WHOLE ARGUMENT FOR HAVING SOMETHING TO REPRODUCE.**

## 12B. RUN FOUR, AND WHAT A HAND-OVER COSTS WHEN IT IS WRITTEN FROM THE CHAPTERS

**RUN FOUR IS THE TEN CHAPTERS AGAINST THE SIX STATE FILES THIS BATCH WROTE, TAKEN AT THE END AND AGAIN AFTER EVERY REPAIR. THE FINDING OF THE 0018 BLOCK WAS THAT PLANNING A HAND-OVER AS A DESCRIPTION IS NOT A REPAIR AND THAT A REWRITE TAKEN WITH THE CHAPTERS OPEN IS ALSO A TRANSCRIPTION, AND THAT FOUR FURTHER PASSES AT ONE SENTENCE AT A TIME IS WHAT ACTUALLY CLEARS IT. THIS BATCH TOOK THE REPAIR THE FOURTH TIME AND THE METHOD WAS THE SAME AND IT WORKED: EVERY DESCRIPTIVE SENTENCE IN ALL SIX BLOCKS WAS COMPOSED FROM WHAT A PERSON DID, WAS REFUSED, WAS TOLD, OR IS CARRYING, IN THAT ORDER, AND THE VERBS WERE CHOSEN BEFORE THE NOUNS WERE CHECKED. THE FIGURES ARE AT §13A ITEM 4 AND THE FIRST TAKING IS THERE TOO, BECAUSE A FIGURE IN A HAND-OVER HAS TO CARRY ITS MEASUREMENT AND NOT ITS CLAIM.**

**AND ONE REPAIR WAS MADE IN A CHAPTER THAT IS NOT ONE OF THIS BATCH'S OWN TEN, WHICH IS RECORDED HERE BECAUSE A REUSE IS REPAIRED WHERE THE LATER TEXT IS. RE-TAKING THE 365–374 WINDOW AT THE START OF THIS BATCH, THE METHOD OF §12A OF THAT BLOCK, RETURNED 16 RAW SPANS AT A LONGEST OF FOURTEEN AND NIL, WHERE THAT BLOCK PRINTED 25 RAW AT THE SAME LONGEST AND NIL. THE THIRD NUMBER REPRODUCED AND THE RAW COUNT DID NOT, AND THE RAW COUNT IS A CHECK AND NOT A CONSTANT, AND NOTHING OUTSIDE THE TEN WAS TOUCHED.**

**SIX THINGS WERE WRONG ON THE PAGE AND EVERY ONE WAS REPAIRED IN A CHAPTER.**

1. **A RUN TWO TOTAL BUILT BY HAND WITH THE CHAPTER BEING MEASURED INSIDE ITS OWN SET CAME BACK AT 356 RAW, 233 SURVIVING AND A LONGEST OF 133 TOKENS, WHICH IS EVERY CHAPTER MATCHED AGAINST ITSELF, AND IT IS THE FOURTH TIME THAT FIGURE HAS COME BACK LOOKING LIKE A FINDING.** THE READER WAS AT FAULT AND NOT THE PROSE, AND THE FIGURE THAT BINDS IS 14 AND NIL. **A WRITER WHO BUILDS A RUN TWO TOTAL BY HAND MUST EXCLUDE THE FILE BEING MEASURED, BECAUSE NOTHING IN THE OUTPUT SAYS WHICH FILE WAS IN THE SET.**
2. **A SCENE-BREAK CAP WAS BROKEN IN 0376, 0379, 0381, 0382 AND 0384, AND TWENTY-ONE MORE BREAKS THAN THE CAP ALLOWS WERE CUT ACROSS FIVE CHAPTERS WITH NOT ONE WORD OF PROSE CHANGED.** A BATCH THAT ADDS BREAKS THAN THE CAP ALLOWS HAS CHANGED A FACT ABOUT ITS OWN SHAPE WITHOUT CHANGING A SENTENCE.
3. **A DAY-COUNT WAS PRINTED TWICE IN 0384.** The same figure stood in its own opening caps and in its body. **A FINDING IS NOT TO BE PRINTED TWICE IN ONE CHAPTER IN ANY FORM, AND PRINTING IT IN A CAPS PARAGRAPH AND A BODY PARAGRAPH ARE TWO PRINTS.**

## 12E. THE REVIEW REPAIR PASS ON THIS BATCH, WHAT THE REVIEW FOUND, AND WHAT WAS REPAIRED WHERE

**A REVIEW OF THIS BATCH ON 28 SEPTEMBER 2026 READ THE TEN CHAPTERS AND THE SIX STATE FILES AND FOUND FIFTEEN THINGS. FOURTEEN WERE REPAIRED AND ONE WAS RULED ON AND RECORDED. THE BATCH WAS NOT RESTARTED, NO CARD WAS REWRITTEN, NO DATE WAS MOVED, NO DAY-COUNT WAS CHANGED, NO STANDING WAS TOUCHED AND NOTHING WAS RESOLVED THAT THE CHAPTERS DID NOT ALREADY RESOLVE. THE LIST IS THE WHOLE RECORD AND IT IS HERE BECAUSE A HAND-OVER THAT DOES NOT CARRY THE FINDINGS OF THE REVIEW THAT PASSED OVER IT WILL BE READ AS A CLEAN BLOCK.**

1. **AN IMPOSSIBLE WEEKDAY IN 0381, IN FOUR PLACES.** THE CHAPTER PRINTED *THE SUNDAY OF THE THIRTIETH OF DECEMBER* AND THE THIRTIETH OF DECEMBER 2017 WAS A SATURDAY. THE CHAPTER'S OWN CHAIN — TWO MEN LIFT A FLOOR ON A SUNDAY, THE BOX STANDS SIX DAYS, IT GOES ON THE FRIDAY, TWO PEOPLE LOOK AT THE MARK ON THE SATURDAY, WHICH IS THAT CHAPTER'S OWN DATELINE — ONLY CLOSES IF THE FLOOR WAS PULLED ON **SUNDAY THE THIRTY-FIRST**. FOUR PRINTINGS WERE CORRECTED IN THE CHAPTER AND THE ERROR HAD PROPAGATED INTO `state/current.md`, WHERE IT WAS CORRECTED THERE TOO, AND IT HAD ALSO PUT THE COUNT OF DAYS OUT BY ONE IN §7 OF THE 0019 BLOCK OF `state/open-threads.md`, WHICH SAID THE BOX WENT OUT ON THE SEVENTH DAY AND WAS WRONG. **A WEEKDAY IN A CHAPTER IS A MEASUREMENT AND NOT A FIGURE OF STYLE, AND A CHAPTER THAT NAMES A DAY OF THE MONTH NAMES A DAY THAT WAS COUNTED.**
2. **A FORWARD REFERENCE IN 0379 THAT A MAN COULD NOT HAVE MADE.** THE CHAPTER IS DATED THURSDAY THE TWENTY-EIGHTH OF DECEMBER AND SAID THE FREEZER *WAS THERE THROUGH JANUARY AND IT WAS THERE AT THE END OF THAT MONTH*, WHICH IS THE END OF THE BATCH'S OWN SCHEDULE AND NOT A THING A MAN ON THE TWENTY-EIGHTH OF DECEMBER CAN KNOW. IT NOW SAYS OVER CHRISTMAS AND IN THE NEW YEAR.
3. **A CONTRADICTION INSIDE 0379.** THE BODY SAID THE WOMAN *DID NOT TURN ROUND* AND THE CLOSING BLOCK SAID SHE *TURNED ROUND AFTERWARDS*. THE BODY WAS THE BETTER BEAT AND WAS KEPT AND EXTENDED: SHE DID NOT TURN ROUND WHILE EITHER MAN WAS AT THAT KERB, AND SHE TURNED ROUND WHEN THE TAILGATE HAD GONE UP AND THE PICKUP HAD GONE, AND THERE WAS NOTHING TO LOOK AT. **A CLOSING BLOCK THAT CONTRADICTS ITS OWN CHAPTER IS NOT A LANDING, IT IS A SECOND VERSION OF THE CHAPTER, AND THE SECOND VERSION IS ALWAYS THE ONE THAT WAS WRITTEN FIRST.**
4. **A DOUBLED WORD IN 0384**, *AND AND*, IN THE OPENING CAPS, AND IT WAS THE ONLY GENUINE DOUBLED WORD IN THE TEN. (*HAD HAD* IN 0377, 0380 AND 0382 IS CORRECT ENGLISH AND WAS LEFT ALONE.)
5. **A MAN WHO WORKS NIGHTS GIVEN TWO HOURS FOR ONE ROUTINE ON ONE DAY IN 0384**, TWENTY TO FIVE IN THE MORNING AND HALF PAST FOUR IN THE AFTERNOON, **AND NEITHER 0383 NOR 0384 ACKNOWLEDGED THE CHANGE 0377 SETS OUT, WHICH IS THAT SINCE THE BEGINNING OF DECEMBER HE GOES UP THAT PARADE AT SEVEN IN THE MORNING INSTEAD OF AT HALF PAST FOUR.** ALL THREE CHAPTERS WERE PUT STRAIGHT: HE GOES UP THAT PARADE BEFORE THE SHOPS ARE OPEN, HE IS IN IT AGAIN IN THE AFTERNOON AS A SECOND AND SEPARATE SIGHTING, AND 0383'S ARRIVAL AT A YARD IS NO LONGER EXPLAINED BY A CLOCK THAT 0377 HAD ALREADY CHANGED.

## 1. WHAT A MAN CARRIED OUT OF A GATE

A man went back to a yard off a side turning for a tin of grease that had been left on a concrete bench, and it was not there, and the man who keeps that yard was thirty foot away with a broom and was not asked. A crate of Cox's apples was sitting where the tin should have been, and he carried it out of that gate in front of the man who was watching him. He has not mentioned either half of that morning to anybody since and is not going to. **THE GREASE IS IN THAT YARD OR IS NOWHERE AND NOBODY IS GOING TO LOOK, AND HE PUT WHAT WAS ON THE BENCH ON A KERB OF HIS OWN STREET AND IT WAS GONE BY TWO O'CLOCK ON THE FIFTH OF FEBRUARY AND HE DOES NOT KNOW WHO HAS IT.**

## 2. WHAT A MAN SAID THAT HE HAD NEVER HAD DONE

A woman who runs a shop off a parade asked a man in his forties, once, whether there is anybody in this town who can look at a bell in her own shopframe that has not rung since the middle of December. He thought about it for about three seconds and said that he has never had one done, and that was true and gave her nothing. She did not ask again, and she tore the number off a card in her kitchen and put the rest of the card in the bin. **A MAN IN HIS THIRTIES WAS AT THE FAR END OF THAT COUNTER AND HEARD BOTH HALVES OF IT AND HAS PUT IT TO NEITHER OF THEM, AND THE MAN SHE ASKED DOES NOT KNOW THE QUESTION WAS EVER PUT.**

## 3. WHAT WOULD NOT GO PAST A LEDGE

A churn has stood on a brick ledge in a shared back passage since a Saturday in November. A man in his thirties found that a bicycle could not get past it on the twenty-seventh of January, with a man in his sixties coming out of a gate ten foot off at the same moment, and both of them looked at the churn and neither of them said a word. He went round by the parade and lost a quarter of an hour. **THEY HAVE BOTH GOT A REASON OF THEIR OWN AND THE REASONS ARE ABOUT DIFFERENT THINGS, AND HE HAS BEEN DOWN THAT PASSAGE SIX TIMES SINCE AND GONE ROUND IT EVERY TIME.**

## 4. WHAT WAS LAID IN A ROOM THAT IS NOT A FLAT

Just under thirty square foot of chipboard, and a length of sheet vinyl, went down over the floor of an unlet room at the head of that stair, in a building the man who laid it has no connection with, and another man steadied the far end of two of the sheets while he did it. There was nothing the matter with it. A woman with the flat below saw him in there at about twenty to one on the Sunday and has told nobody. **HE HAS BEEN BACK IN THAT BLOCK ONCE SINCE, FOR HALF A DAY'S WORK IN ONE OF THE FLATS, AND WAS NOT SPOKEN TO DIFFERENTLY BY ANYBODY, AND HE IS NOT TOLD THAT ANYBODY KNOWS.**

## 5. WHAT TWO MEN PUT UP WITHOUT KNOWING

There are two lengths of rail on two sets of brackets on the same four foot of brickwork at the back of an outbuilding in a yard, one at about five foot and one at about six foot two, three weeks apart, put there by two men for two reasons that are both right. A woman with the letting of the shop alongside went into that building for a box, stood in it four minutes and saw one of them. **THE LOWER ONE IS BEHIND A STACK OF SHEET MATERIAL AND THE UPPER ONE IS NOT VISIBLE FROM THE FRONT OF THAT BUILDING, AND NEITHER MAN KNOWS, AND THE BENCH THE UPPER RAIL IS FOR HAS NOT BEEN BUILT.**

## 6. WHAT A MAN PUT BACK BETTER

A man carried a chair out into the middle of a front room to reach a floor that turned out to be sound, and walked it back inside the hour, and knocked a loose joint down and put a piece of the rug's stiff backing under a short leg while it was out. The man it belongs to sat in it at about ten past one and noticed nothing. **HE TOLD NOBODY HE TOUCHED IT, THE WOMAN WHO WATCHED HIM GO UP THAT STREET AND COME BACK DOWN IT HAS NOT TOLD THE MAN IN HIS SIXTIES EITHER, AND NEITHER OF THEM WILL.**

## 7. WHAT TWO COMPETENT MEN DID WITH TWO TRUE FACTS

There was words between two men for about a minute and a half, standing up, in a shop, over a square of plaster that has since fallen out of a ceiling above that shop. Each gave one thing that was true, neither gave the other what the other one needed, neither conceded, and it stopped when somebody else came up to be served. They stood two foot apart at that counter twice in the week after and raised nothing. **ABOUT TWO FOOT OF THAT CEILING IS STILL OPEN UNDER A PLASTIC SHEET HOOKED OVER A RAIL, AND NEITHER OF THE TWO MEN HOLDS THAT HE IS AT FAULT.**

## 8. WHAT WENT INTO A HAND AND BACK ONTO A LEDGE

A man in his sixties put a tin into a man in his forties' hand on a street off the parade in the middle of a sentence about work at the Cleeve road, and said nothing about the tin. The man in his forties carried it in his van for four days, did not open it, and put one question to the man in his sixties on the Monday, and was answered about where the tin had been kept rather than about why it changed hands. He set it down on that ledge again on the Tuesday, when the other man was not there. **THE OTHER MAN TOOK IT OFF ON THE WEDNESDAY AND PUT IT BACK ON THE WARDROBE IT CAME OFF, AND NEITHER HAS MENTIONED IT AND THE MAN WHO WAS GIVEN IT HAS NOT MANAGED TO FIND A REASON FOR IT.**

## 9. WHAT WAS PUT DOWN ON A TABLE AND LEFT THERE

A man carried a boxed electric fire in his van for a fortnight without being able to put it anywhere, and on the Friday of that week he set it on a table in a room at the back of a shop, said nothing to the three people in it, and went at about five. He has not been through that hatch since. **THE MAN WHO WORKS NIGHTS MOVED HIS BAG OF ICE, THE WOMAN WHO WORKS IN A SHOP PUT HER CUP ON IT, THE MAN IN HIS SIXTIES DID NOT LOOK AT IT, AND NONE OF THE THREE HAS ASKED ANYBODY ANYTHING.**

## 10. WHAT A BOROUGH DID ON THE THIRD OF MARCH

A gate off a side turning kept a man in his forties waiting for about ten minutes because he had turned up fifty-five minutes after the hour he had in his own head, for something nobody had asked him to come for, and neither man said anything about the hour and nobody in this borough knows it happened. A shutter at the top of that parade has been stopping about a foot above the pavement since the twelfth of February, and a paving slab in the middle of that parade has stood an inch and a half out of its bed for some time, and both of them are still wrong and nobody in that borough has put either of them right. The same nine people did the same rounds. **A HALL ON A METER WAS OPEN ON THE SATURDAY MORNING WITH THE URN ON AND ABOUT TWENTY PEOPLE THROUGH IT AND A MAN BEHIND A TABLE THAT NOBODY PUT ANYTHING TO, AND A BOX IS STILL ON A TABLE AT THE BACK OF THAT SHOP WITH NOBODY CLAIMING IT.**

2. **THE FIGURES THAT WERE NOT AT ZERO, RE-MEASURED ONE BY ONE AFTER EVERY REPAIR.** *ELEVEN* AND *FORTY* AND *SPRING* AND *SHED* AND *STONE* AND *DRAWER* AND *FOUR YEARS* AND *A FRIDAY* WERE IN THE DRAFTS OF 0385, 0386, 0387, 0388, 0389, 0390, 0392 AND 0394 AND ARE AT ZERO IN ALL TEN NOW. **A CARD MAY NOT BE A SHEET OF PAPER AND A CRATE IS NOT A CARD, AND A TIN DOES NOT COME OUT OF A DRAWER, AND THE TELLING OF IT WAS THE POINT.** **AND *CARD* IS THE ONE ON THAT LIST THAT WAS NOT AT ZERO AND WAS BEING PRINTED AS THOUGH IT WERE, WHICH IS THE FINDING A REVIEW OF 0020 CAUGHT AND WHICH IS THE SIXTH TIME IN THIS REPOSITORY THAT A FIGURE HAS BEEN ASSERTED IN A STATE FILE AGAINST A CHAPTER THAT DISAGREED WITH IT. IT WAS AT NINE ACROSS THREE CHAPTERS — SEVEN IN 0386, ONE IN 0388 AND ONE IN 0394 — AND THE REVIEW'S COUNT OF SEVEN WAS A COUNT OF LINES AND NOT OF OCCURRENCES, WHICH IS THE SAME ERROR AS COUNTING A CHAPTER IN A LIST TWICE. ALL NINE WERE LEGITIMATE ENGLISH FOR A THING IN A ROOM AND NONE OF THEM WAS LOAD-BEARING: 0386's SLIP OF STIFF PAPER WITH FOUR TELEPHONE NUMBERS ON IT, 0388'S STRIP OF BROWN PAPER IN A MAN'S HAND WHILE HE IS ON HIS KNEES, AND A PIECE OF PAPER IN A SHOP WINDOW. THE THREE HAVE BEEN CHANGED AT SOURCE AND THE FIGURE IS AT ZERO NOW, AND NO CARD, NO DATE, NO DAY-COUNT, NO NAME, NO MAJOR TURN AND NO STANDING WAS TOUCHED TO DO IT. THE REPAIR IS THE SAME KIND OF REPAIR AS THE TIN OUT OF THE DRAWER AND THE ONE THAT BINDS IS THAT A CLOSED FIGURE WAS BEING HELD AT ZERO BY A FILE RATHER THAN BY A CHAPTER.**
3. **AND THREE THINGS NO RUN IN THIS REPOSITORY CAN FIND, WHICH ARE THE CAPS, THE FIGURES AND THE STALENESS.** THE SCENE-BREAK CAP WAS BROKEN IN ALL TEN ON THE FIRST TAKING, WHICH WAS SIX BREAKS IN EVERY CHAPTER, AND FORTY BREAKS WERE CUT WITH NOT ONE WORD OF PROSE CHANGED, AND THE TEN NOW CARRY TWO EACH. A FINDING WAS PRINTED TWICE IN EVERY CHAPTER ON THE FIRST TAKING, ONCE IN THE OPENING CAPS AND ONCE IN THE CLOSING CAPS, AND **EVERY CLOSING BLOCK IN THESE TEN CHAPTERS NOW LANDS ON A PERSON AND A VERB AND NOT ON THE CHAPTER'S OWN FINDING**, WHICH IS THE REPAIR THAT 0019 §12E ITEM 8 ASKED FOR AND WHICH 0020 APPLIED TO ALL TEN RATHER THAN TO ONE. A DAY-COUNT WAS PRINTED TWICE IN 0394 ON THE FIRST TAKING, ONCE IN ITS OPENING CAPS AND ONCE IN ITS BODY, AND THE OPENING CAPS NOW CARRY NO FIGURE AT ALL.
4. **AND THE REUSES, EVERY ONE REAL, EVERY ONE REPAIRED IN THE CHAPTERS AND NOT IN A FILE.** SIX SURVIVED RUN TWO AND FOURTEEN SURVIVED RUN THREE AGAINST 375–384, INCLUDING A THIRTEEN-TOKEN DESCRIPTION OF A DENT SHARED BY 0387 AND 0392, A TEN-TOKEN SENTENCE SHARED BY 0388 AND 0391, A FORMULA ABOUT WHAT PASSED BETWEEN TWO PEOPLE THAT HAD BEEN IN 0375 AND WHICH 0020 PUT INTO TWO CHAPTERS OF ITS OWN, A CARRIER BAG OF ICE REPRODUCED FROM 0377 IN 0393, AND SIX SPANS IN 0394 THAT REPRODUCED 0384'S ACCOUNT OF THAT PARADE AND THAT HALL. **THE HAND-OVER A CHAPTER WAS WRITTEN AGAINST IS THE WORST PLACE IN THIS REPOSITORY FOR A CHAPTER TO REPRODUCE, AND 0394 IS THE PROOF: IT WAS THE TENTH CHAPTER OF A BATCH WHOSE OWN HARD-OVER DESCRIBED AN ORDINARY DAY ON THAT PARADE IN DETAIL, AND EVERY FIGURE AND EVERY SENTENCE IN THAT HAND-OVER WAS AVAILABLE TO IT FOR NOTHING.**

## 12A. THE VERBATIM-SPAN METHOD AS IT WAS BUILT FOR THIS BATCH, AND THE TWO THINGS THAT WERE WRONG IN THE FIRST BUILDING

**ONE, THE THRESHOLD IS NINE TOKENS AND IT IS NAMED EVERY TIME. TWO, THE SCRIPT COMPARES TOKENS AND NOT CHARACTERS, ON `[a-z0-9']+` APPLIED TO LOWERCASED TEXT, AND A TOKEN THAT IS NOTHING BUT APOSTROPHE MARKS IS A QUOTATION MARK AND IS DROPPED. THREE, THE H1 TITLE LINE IS DROPPED, EVERY `---` LINE IS DROPPED, AND EVERY STANDALONE ALL-CAPS PARAGRAPH IS DROPPED. FOUR, A SPAN IS A MAXIMAL RUN OF NINE CONSECUTIVE TOKENS SHARED WITH THE COMPARISON SET, EXTENDED BY DIRECT TOKEN COMPARISON FROM A REAL POSITION IN THE OTHER FILE, AND EXTENDED FROM EVERY REAL POSITION THE NINE-GRAM OCCUPIES, NOT FROM ONE. FIVE, EVERY SPAN IS ASSERTED CONTIGUOUS BY DIRECT TOKEN COMPARISON. SIX, A PARAGRAPH BOUNDARY IS A SENTINEL NO TOKEN CAN EQUAL, IN THE TARGET AND IN EVERY SET FILE, AND NO SPAN CROSSES ONE, WHICH IS IMPLEMENTED AS A TEST THAT NEITHER SIDE OF THE MATCH LEAVES THE PARAGRAPH IT STARTED IN AND NOT AS A TEST THAT THE TWO PARAGRAPH NUMBERS ARE EQUAL. SEVEN, A CHAPTER IS NEVER INCLUDED IN THE SET IT IS COMPARED AGAINST AND EACH FILE OF A SET IS COMPARED SEPARATELY. EIGHT, THREE CLASSES ARE EXCLUDED AND RECORDED AS A COUNT: A DATELINE IS DETECTED STRUCTURALLY BY A FOUR-DIGIT YEAR OR A WEEKDAY NAME AND IS DROPPED ON BOTH SIDES, AND A SPAN IS ONLY OF THAT CLASS WHEN THE WHOLE OF IT SITS INSIDE SUCH A PARAGRAPH; A BY-NAME DESCRIPTION IS DETECTED IN TOKENISED FORM BY A DETERMINER SCANNED ACROSS THE WHOLE SPAN AND A HEAD NOUN FROM A CLOSED SET WITH THE RUN BOUNDED AT A COMMA BELONGING TO THE TEXT THE RUN COVERS; AND A BOROUGH'S OWN RECURRING PLACE NOUN IS DETECTED BY A CLOSED SET. NINE, THE CONTROL IS ASKED FOR BEFORE ANY FIGURE IS BELIEVED AND IS TWO PAIRS AND A PLANT. TEN, EVERY FIGURE IS TAKEN AGAIN AFTER EVERY REPAIR AND AGAIN AT THE END, BECAUSE THE STATE FILES ARE IN THE SET OF RUN FOUR AND THE FIGURE MOVES WHEN THEY ARE.**

**AND A THIRD THING WAS WRONG IN THE SECOND BUILDING AND WAS FOUND THE SAME MORNING, AND IT IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS MOST: THE CLOSED SET OF HEAD NOUNS HAD PLACE NOUNS IN IT, SO A SPAN CONTAINING *THE COUNTER* OR *THE WALL* WAS BEING CALLED A FIGURE'S OWN BY-NAME DESCRIPTION AND WAS BEING EXCLUDED, AND A STATE FILE HOLDING A FORTY-SIX-TOKEN SENTENCE OUT OF 0394 WAS BEING HIDED BY IT. A BY-NAME DESCRIPTION DESCRIBES A PERSON AND A PLACE IS NOT A PERSON. THE SET NOW HOLDS FIGURES ONLY AND THE BOROUGH'S OWN PLACE NOUNS ARE THE THIRD EXCLUDED CLASS, WHICH IS WHERE THEY BELONG. **A PASS THAT EXCLUDES SOMETHING IT SHOULD NOT IS A PASS THAT HAS HIDDEN A FINDING, AND IT IS THE SAME FAILURE AS A PASS THAT ADDS AN ENTRY TO A LIST.**

**AND THE TWO THINGS THAT WERE WRONG IN THE FIRST BUILDING, RECORDED BECAUSE A LATER WRITER WILL REBUILD IT AGAIN. ONE: A PARAGRAPH BOUNDARY IS A SENTINEL AND A PARAGRAPH NUMBER IS NOT A SENTINEL, AND WRITING THE SENTINEL AS AN EQUALITY OF NUMBERS FINDS CONTINUITY WHERE IT SHOULD FIND A BREAK, WHICH IS WHY THE CONTROL CAME BACK FORTY TOKENS AND NOT THREE HUNDRED AND TWENTY-SIX. TWO: A SPAN MUST BE EXTENDED FROM A REAL POSITION IN THE SET FILE AND NOT FROM THE HEAD OF THAT FILE, WHICH IS THE SAME DEFECT AS 0019 §12F POINTED IN ITS OTHER FORM. **BOTH WERE FOUND BY ASKING FOR THE 0016 CONTROL AND BY NOTHING ELSE, WHICH IS THE WHOLE ARGUMENT FOR HAVING SOMETHING TO REPRODUCE, AND A PASS THAT ADDS AN ENTRY TO A LIST IS A PASS THAT HAS NOT FOUND A DEFECT.**

## 12B. RUN FOUR, AND WHAT A HAND-OVER COSTS WHEN IT IS WRITTEN FROM THE CHAPTERS

**RUN FOUR IS THE TEN CHAPTERS AGAINST THE SIX STATE FILES THIS BATCH WROTE, TAKEN AT THE END AND AGAIN AFTER EVERY REPAIR. THIS BATCH DID NOT PLAN ITS HAND-OVER AS A DESCRIPTION. EVERY ENTRY IN ALL SIX BLOCKS WAS COMPOSED FROM WHAT A PERSON DID, WHAT WAS REFUSED OR LEFT UNSAID, WHO WAS TOLD WHAT, AND WHAT THEY DID WITH IT, IN THAT ORDER, AND THE FIGURES ARE AT §13A ITEM 4. **THE FIGURE THAT BINDS IS THE THIRD NUMBER OF EVERY RUN, AND THE FIGURE THAT SAYS WHAT THE PROCESS COSTS IS 227 AND 168 AND 197 AND 117 AND 61 AND 9, AND 0020 IS THE FIRST BATCH IN THIS REPOSITORY WHOSE HAND-OVER WAS WRITTEN WITHOUT ITS CHAPTERS OPEN AND IT IS THE FIRST BATCH WHOSE REUSE FIGURE CAME OUT AT NIL ON THE FIRST TAKING, WHICH IS EITHER A CHANGE OF METHOD OR A LUCK AND A LATER WRITER SHOULD NOT BANK ON IT.**

## 12C. THE REPAIRS, AND WHAT THEY WERE

**FORTY-EIGHT SPANS AND FORTY SCENE BREAKS WERE REPAIRED, TWENTY-ONE OF THE SPANS IN THE TEN CHAPTERS AND TWENTY-SEVEN IN THE SIX STATE FILES, AND A DETECTOR WAS REBUILT IN THE MIDDLE OF IT. NOT ONE WORD OF ANY STATE FILE WAS CHANGED TO CLEAR A SPAN THAT BELONGED TO A CHAPTER.**

1. **A SCENE-BREAK CAP WAS BROKEN IN ALL TEN CHAPTERS ON THE FIRST TAKING**, six breaks in each, and forty were cut with not one word of prose changed. A batch that adds more breaks than the cap allows has changed a fact about its own shape without changing a sentence.
2. **A FINDING WAS PRINTED TWICE IN ALL TEN CHAPTERS ON THE FIRST TAKING**, in the opening caps and in the closing caps, and every closing block was cut and rewritten to land on a person and a verb. **THE REPAIR IS A NEW CLOSING, NOT A NEW CHAPTER, AND A CHAPTER WHOSE LAST THREE PARAGRAPHS COULD BE THE STATE FILE IS WRITTEN WRONG.**
3. **A DAY-COUNT WAS PRINTED TWICE IN 0394**, once in its own opening caps and once in its body, and the caps now carry no figure.
4. **A CHAPTER REPRODUCING ITS OWN CARD, AND ONE REPRODUCING AN EARLIER CHAPTER'S SCENE.** 0389's cold open printed the card's own words about a woman who did not know there were two, 0394's cold open printed the card's own phrase about being an hour late for something not arranged, and 0391's body printed the card's own words about two men standing next to each other at that counter again. 0393 then opened by reproducing 0377's account of the room at the back of that shop, and 0390 by reproducing an hour 0379 had already used. **A CHAPTER THAT REPRODUCES THE CARD IT WAS WRITTEN FROM HAS BEEN GIVEN A SENTENCE INSTEAD OF HAVING TO FIND ONE, AND A CHAPTER THAT REPRODUCES THE CHAPTER ABOVE IT HAS BEEN GIVEN A CLEAN ACCOUNT OF A ROOM.**
5. **AND A FIGURE WHO HAD A SECOND VERSION.** 0386 opened with a woman who runs a shop, which is a second version of the woman who runs the shop that shuts early, and it was rewritten to name her.
6. **TWO FIGURES WERE AGED IN A DRAFT AND BOTH WERE CUT BEFORE THE CHAPTERS WENT DOWN**, a man in his sixties in a shared passage and a man in his thirties with a bicycle, which is the second time in this repository that an age has been proposed and refused before the chapter went out.
7. **AND A MISTAKE THIS BATCH MADE IN ITS OWN FILES, WHICH IS RECORDED BECAUSE A HAND-OVER THAT DOES NOT CARRY THE MISTAKE IS A HAND-OVER THAT LIES. A REGULAR EXPRESSION USED TO REPAIR THIS BATCH'S OWN SENTENCES WAS APPLIED TO THE WHOLE OF A STATE FILE AND NOT TO THE BLOCK AT THE END OF IT, AND IT MATCHED AN IDENTICAL SENTENCE IN AN EARLIER BLOCK AND DELETED THE §13A ITEMS 2 TO 8 OF EIGHT EARLIER BLOCKS IN `state/continuity.md` AND ONE SENTENCE IN AN EARLIER BLOCK OF `state/open-threads.md`. **BOTH WERE RESTORED FROM THE REVISION AND BOTH FILES ARE NOW PURE APPENDS, WHICH WAS CHECKED.** EVERY FIGURE IN THOSE EIGHT BLOCKS WAS THE ONLY RECORD THAT IT HAD EVER BEEN MEASURED AND A REPAIR PASS THAT DELETES AN OLDER BLOCK IS A REPAIR PASS THAT DESTROYS THE ACCOUNT, AND A SCOPE OF A REPAIR MUST BE THE BLOCK AND NOT THE FILE.**
8. **A TIN WAS ORIGINALLY TAKEN OUT OF A DRAWER**, and the word is at zero in all ten chapters of every batch since 0013, and it was changed to the top of a wardrobe. **A NO CHAPTER NEEDS A DRAWER, AND A DRAWER IS ALSO A STANDING OBJECT IN THIS BOROUGH, AND A WRITER WHO REACHES FOR ONE HAS REACHED FOR A THING THAT IS NOT THEIRS.**

## 12D. TWO FLAGS RAISED BY THIS BATCH'S OWN CARDS, WHICH ARE DEFECTS IN THE CARDS AND NOT IN THE CHAPTERS

1. **CARD 0394'S CAPITALISED MAJOR TURN PRINTS THE MAJOR TURN OF CHAPTER 0380**, which is two small things going wrong on one day and being put right and told to nobody. A card that prints the major turn of a chapter already written is a defect in the card, and the repair is a new engine. **THE CHAPTER WAS WRITTEN TO THE GOAL CLAUSE INSTEAD, WHICH ASKS THAT THE TWO SMALL WRONG THINGS IN THE DAY STAY WRONG, AND THEY DO: A SHUTTER AND A PAVING SLAB.**
2. **CARD 0389 ASKS FOR A YARD AND FOR A RAIL, AND 0383 ALREADY SPENT A WALL AND A RAIL'S SIBLING, SO THE REPAIR WAS TO MAKE THE TWO FIXINGS OF 0389 PHYSICALLY DIFFERENT: THE OLDER MAN'S BRACKETS HOOK OVER THE TOP OF THE BRICK AND GO INTO NOTHING AT ALL, AND THE YOUNGER MAN'S GO IN.** A card may name a thing a previous chapter used if the chapter says what is different about this one.

## 12G. THE REVIEW REPAIR PASS ON 0020, TWELVE FINDINGS, TWO OF THEM RULED ON, AND THE FIGURES THAT ARE WITHDRAWN

**A REVIEW OF CONTINUATION 0020 RAN ON 28 SEPTEMBER 2026 AGAINST COMMITT 649763b AND RAISED ELEVEN NUMBERED FINDINGS. TEN WERE DEFECTS AND WERE REPAIRED AT SOURCE, ONE WAS HALF RIGHT AND WAS SPLIT, AND TWO WERE ERRORS IN THE REVIEW ITSELF AND HAVE BEEN RULED ON AND RECORDED RATHER THAN APPLIED, BECAUSE APPLYING EITHER WOULD HAVE PUT A NEW ERROR INTO A FILE THAT IS THE ONLY THING A LATER WRITER IS FORCED TO TRUST. NO CARD, DATE, DAY-COUNT, FIGURE, NAME, MAJOR TURN OR STANDING WAS CHANGED BY ANY OF IT, NO CHAPTER WAS RESTARTED, AND NO PROSE THAT WAS WORKING WAS REWRITTEN FOR ITS OWN SAKE.**

1. **THREE DATELINES PRINTED THE WRONG DAY OF THE WEEK.** 3, 17 AND 24 FEBRUARY 2018 ARE ALL SATURDAYS ON THE REAL 2018 CALENDAR AND WERE PRINTED AS A SUNDAY AND TWO FRIDAYS, WHICH FALSIFIED THE CLAIM AT §0 THAT EVERY WEEKDAY WAS DERIVED FROM THE REAL CALENDAR AND CHECKED AGAINST IT. ALL THREE DATELINES ARE CORRECTED IN THE CHAPTERS.

3. **0394 WAS REPRODUCING 0384 AND 0380.** THE REVIEW NAMED FOUR RUNS OF NINE TO TWELVE TOKENS. **TWO OF THE FOUR WERE REAL AND TWO WERE NOT, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS THE METHOD'S OWN EXCLUDED CLASSES.** THE TWO THAT WERE REAL WERE REWRITTEN IN THE CHAPTER: 0384'S ACCOUNT OF THE WOMAN WHO WORKS IN A SHOP, AND 0384'S ACCOUNT OF THE HALL ON THE METER, WHICH ALSO BROKE A RUN AGAINST 0372. THE ONE THE REVIEW ALSO NAMED AGAINST 0380 WAS A RUN OF EIGHT TOKENS AND DID NOT SURVIVE ON ITS OWN.
4. **A FIFTEEN-TOKEN SENTENCE WAS SHARED BY 0386 AND 0391, WITH A NINE-TOKEN FORM IN 0390.** THIS WAS THE WORST FINDING IN THE REVIEW AND IT WAS REAL, AND IT WAS THE ONE THE RECORD HAD ALREADY REPAIRED AND BELIEVED. THE REPAIR WAS TO CHANGE BOTH ENDINGS AND NOT THE MIDDLE, SO THAT NO TWO OF THE THREE CHAPTERS ANY LONGER SHARE NINE TOKENS WITH EACH OTHER.
5. **THE MEDIAN WAS WRONG.** PRINTED AS 1,885.5 AGAINST A LIST WHOSE MIDDLE PAIR IS 1,866 AND 1,900, AND 1,883.0, WHICH THE REVIEW PUT IN ITS PLACE, IS ALSO NOT THEIR MEAN. THE FIGURE IS 1,877.5 ON THE RE-MEASURED LIST AND THE REVIEW'S OWN REPLACEMENT IS WITHDRAWN, WHICH IS THE SECOND TIME IN THIS REPOSITORY THAT A CORRECTION HAS ARRIVED WITH A FIGURE IN IT THAT IS ALSO WRONG.
6. ***CARD* WAS NOT AT ZERO.** IT WAS AT NINE ACROSS 0386, 0388 AND 0394 AND THREE FILES ASSERTED OTHERWISE, WHICH IS THE SIXTH TIME A CLOSED FIGURE HAS BEEN HELD AT ZERO BY A FILE RATHER THAN BY A CHAPTER. **THE REVIEW'S COUNT OF SEVEN IS ALSO WITHDRAWN AND WAS A COUNT OF LINES AND NOT OF OCCURRENCES, WHICH IS THE SAME ERROR AS COUNTING A CHAPTER IN A LIST TWICE.** ALL NINE WERE LEGITIMATE ENGLISH AND NONE WAS LOAD-BEARING AND ALL NINE HAVE BEEN CHANGED AT SOURCE; SEE §12C ITEM 2.
7. **THE 0021 BOUNDS. RULED ON, PARTLY APPLIED, AND THE FIGURE THAT BINDS IS NOT EITHER SET THE REVIEW OFFERED.** THE PROMPT PRINTED **SUNDAY THE THIRD OF JUNE 2018** AS THE SECOND READING'S LONG BOUND, WHICH IS NINETY-TWO DAYS FROM 0394'S OWN DATE AND NOT SIXTY-FOUR, AND THAT WAS A PERMISSIVE ERROR AND A REAL ONE, AND IT IS CORRECTED. **THE PROMPT'S OWN FIRST PAIR, SATURDAY THE THIRTY-FIRST OF MARCH 2018 TO SUNDAY THE SIXTH OF MAY 2018, WAS CORRECT, AND THE REVIEW'S REPLACEMENT PAIRS — ONE APRIL TO SEVEN JUNE, AND THE THIRTY-FIRST OF MARCH TO THE SIXTH OF JUNE — ARE BOTH WRONG AND ARE BOTH WITHDRAWN, BECAUSE EACH ADDS THE INCOMING ONE-DAY GAP IN TWICE.** BOTH READINGS OF A TEN-GAP RUN GIVE THE SAME PAIR WHEN THE INCOMING GAP IS EXACTLY ONE DAY, AND A PROMPT THAT PRINTS TWO PAIRS WHERE THE ARITHMETIC GIVES ONE IS A PROMPT PRINTING A FIGURE IT HAS NOT COUNTED.
8. **THE FLOOR.** `state/batch-summaries.md` PRINTED **SATURDAY THE THIRD OF MARCH 2018** AS THE NEXT BATCH'S FLOOR, WHICH IS 0394'S OWN DATE AND NOT ITS DATE PLUS ONE, AND A WRITER TAKING IT FROM THERE COULD HAVE DATED 0395 ON 0394'S DAY. THE PROMPT HAD SAID THE FOURTH ALL ALONG. CORRECTED IN THE SUMMARY TO **SUNDAY THE FOURTH OF MARCH 2018**, WHICH IS 0394'S OWN DATE PLUS ONE.
9. **RULED ON AND NOT CHANGED. THE 0021 HAND-OVER SAYS *THE NEXT PHASE IS ANOTHER CONTINUATION BATCH, CHAPTERS 405 ONWARD*, AND THE REVIEW READ THAT AS AN OFF-BY-TEN AGAINST ITS OWN CARDS AT 0395–0404.** IT IS NOT A DEFECT. EVERY PROMPT IN THIS VOLUME NAMES THE FIRST CHAPTER OF THE BATCH AFTER ITS OWN — 0017 SAID 365, 0018 SAID 375, 0019 SAID 385, 0020 SAID 395 — AND 0021 SAYING 405 IS THE SAME CONVENTION. THE REVIEW WAS WRONG AND THE TEXT STANDS, AND IT IS RECORDED HERE SO THAT IT IS NOT RAISED A THIRD TIME.
10. **AND 11, WHICH ARE ONE FINDING SPLIT IN TWO AND BOTH REPAIRED: `state/current.md` WAS STALE AT THE TOP.** IT READ *THE SERIES IS AT 354 OF 720*, *VOLUME 05 IS RUNNING (CHAPTERS 195–354)*, *ELEVEN CONTINUATION BATCHES WRITTEN, WHICH IS SIXTEEN BLOCKS*, AND *CURRENT CREATIVE PHASE (LAST WRITTEN): VOLUME 05, CONTINUATION 0016, CHAPTERS 345–354* — FOUR BLOCKS AND FOUR MONTHS BEHIND THE PAGE. THE WORST PART WAS NOT THE HEADER BUT THE **NEXT PLANNED PHASE** LINE, WHICH HAD HAD ITS PATH CORRECTED TO THE 0021 PROMPT AND ITS BODY LEFT AS THE 0016 HAND-OVER, INSTRUCTING A WRITER THAT NO CHAPTER COULD BE DATED BEFORE MONDAY 25 SEPTEMBER 2017 AND HANDING OVER A COUNT OF 1,033 DAYS AT A CHAPTER THAT IS EIGHT BLOCKS BEHIND THE PAGE. **A LINE THAT NAMES THE RIGHT FILE AND CARRIES THE WRONG TEXT IS WORSE THAN A LINE THAT IS SIMPLY OLD, BECAUSE THE PATH IS WHAT A WRITER CHECKS AND THE BODY IS WHAT A WRITER BELIEVES. BOTH ARE NOW REWRITTEN, AND THE SUPERSEDED 0016 EDITION IS MARKED AS SUPERSEDED IN PLACE AND NOT DELETED.**

**AND THE REVIEW WAS RIGHT ABOUT SOMETHING LARGER THAN ITS OWN LIST, WHICH IS THAT THE SIX RUNS IN THE BLOCK ABOVE DID NOT REPRODUCE. THE DETECTOR WAS REBUILT AT THE METHOD AT §12A, ALL THREE CONTROLS WERE ASKED FOR BEFORE ANY FIGURE WAS BELIEVED, AND TWO MORE DEFECTS FELL OUT OF THE REBUILDING, BOTH OF THEM OVER-DROPPING, WHICH IS THE FAILURE THAT HIDES A FINDING RATHER THAN THE ONE THAT ADDS ONE TO A LIST.**

- **THE CLOSED SET OF HEAD NOUNS STILL HAD A PLACE NOUN IN IT.** §12A THIRD PARAGRAPH RECORDS THIS DEFECT AND SAYS THE SET NOW HOLDS FIGURES ONLY. IT DID NOT, AND THE SET CARRIED *HALL* AND *LADDER*, WHICH ARE PLACES AND ARE NOT FIGURES. A SPAN CONTAINING *A HALL* OR *A LADDER* WAS BEING CALLED A FIGURE'S OWN BY-NAME DESCRIPTION AND WAS BEING EXCLUDED, AND EVERY FINDING BELOW THAT MENTIONS A HALL IS ONE THAT WAS BEING HIDED BY IT.
- **THE DATELINE TEST WAS BEING APPLIED TO THE TARGET ONLY AND NOT TO THE SET.** THE METHOD SAYS A DATELINE IS DROPPED **ON BOTH SIDES** AND THIS DETECTOR DROPPED IT ON ONE, WHICH MEANT THAT A DATELINE IN A COMPARISON CHAPTER WAS STILL IN THE INDEX AND COULD BE MATCHED AGAINST A CHAPTER'S BODY. THE 0394 HALL SENTENCE WAS BEING MATCHED AGAINST 0372'S DATELINE ON the strength of ten tokens that were a date and not prose.
- **AND A DATELINE IS STRUCTURAL, WHICH IS A THIRD THING AND IS THE ONE THAT WOULD HAVE HIDDEN A FINDING.** A DATELINE IS A PARAGRAPH THAT **BEGINS** WITH A DAY OF THE WEEK OR WITH A NUMBER AND A MONTH NAME. TESTING A WHOLE PARAGRAPH FOR A WEEKDAY NAME ANYWHERE INSIDE IT DROPS EVERY STATE-FILE SUMMARY THAT mentions a day in passing, and `state/chapter-summaries.md` IS MOSTLY SUMMARIES THAT mention days in passing, and the false drop was HIDING A REAL FINDING: 0387'S OWN CLOSING BLOCK WAS BEING FOUND INSIDE THE 0142 ENTRY, WHICH IS A FAITHFUL RECORD OF A CHAPTER THAT SAID IT FIRST. **A PASS THAT EXCLUDES SOMETHING IT SHOULD NOT IS A PASS THAT HAS HIDDEN A FINDING, AND IT IS THE SAME FAILURE AS A PASS THAT ADDS AN ENTRY TO A LIST.** ALL THREE WERE FIXED, THE CONTROL WAS RE-ASKED, AND IT STILL READS 326.

**AND WHAT THE REBUILT DETECTOR FOUND THAT THE RECORDED PASS HAD MARKED AS REPAIRED, WHICH IS THE FINDING THAT COST THE MOST: ELEVEN REUSES OF PROSE, OF WHICH SEVEN WERE IN CHAPTERS AND NINE WERE IN THE SIX STATE FILES, AND NOT ONE OF THE ELEVEN WAS IN THE SET OF FIGURES THE RECORD NAMED.** THE SEVEN IN CHAPTERS WERE A FORMULA ABOUT A MAN WHO IS NOT GOING TO BE A MAN WHO IN 0387 AND 0389; A FIVE-WORD OPENING ABOUT A MAN IN HIS FORTIES AND AN ASK IN 0385 AND 0392; THE ARRIVAL OF A MAN IN HIS THIRTIES AT A COUNTER IN 0391 AGAINST 0384; A TIN GOING INTO A POCKET IN 0392 AGAINST 0380; A MESSAGE AND A REPLY IN 0388 AGAINST 0368; A LINE ABOUT SOMETHING NOT SAID IN 0390 AGAINST 0355; AND 0393 REPRODUCING 0142'S OWN CLOSING SENTENCE. THE NINE IN STATE FILES WERE IN `state/chapter-summaries.md` (THREE), `state/batch-summaries.md` (ONE), `state/character-state.md` (ONE), `state/continuity.md` (TWO), `state/current.md` (ONE) AND `state/open-threads.md` (ONE), AND EVERY ONE OF THE NINE WAS REWRITTEN IN THE FILE AND NOT IN THE CHAPTER, WHICH IS THE RULE §13A ITEM 4 SETS OUT. **A FIGURE OF NIL IN A BLOCK THAT A LATER WRITER IS TOLD IS THE FIGURE TO CITE IS WORTH NOTHING IF THE DETECTOR THAT PRODUCED IT HAD THREE DEFECTS OF ITS OWN, AND THE FIGURE THAT BINDS IS NOT THE COUNT AND IS THE METHOD, THE WINDOW, THE THRESHOLD AND THE CONTROL, IN THAT ORDER.**

**AND ONE MORE THING, WHICH IS NOT A DEFECT AND IS THE ONLY THING IN THIS PASS THAT PREVENTED RATHER THAN FIXED: NO CHAPTER OF 0020 WAS RESTARTED, AND NO CHAPTER OF 0020 HAD ITS CARD, ITS DATE, ITS MAJOR TURN OR ITS STANDING TOUCHED, AND THE PROSE THAT WAS WORKING WAS LEFT ALONE, INCLUDING THE 0385 CRATE, THE 0386 BELL, THE 0387 CHURN, THE 0388 FLOOR, THE 0390 CHAIR, THE 0391 MINUTE AND A HALF, THE 0392 TIN, THE 0393 BOX AND THE 0394 GATE, ALL OF WHICH ARE THE SAME EVENTS ON THE SAME DAYS WITH THE SAME FIGURES IN THEM AS THEY WERE AT COMMITT 649763b.**

## 1. WHAT TWO MEN DID TO ONE DOOR AND WHAT THE SECOND ONE FOUND IN IT

A door on a common inside stair in a building of four flats stood about two inch open through the cold. A man in his sixties said so once, in fifteen seconds, to the woman who has the letting, in the second week of February, and did not say it again. She asked the man in his forties, who took the door off on the twentieth, packed two hinge knuckles with torn brown paper, eased the hinge arris, and touched up two patches with the paint that was standing on that landing. In the cold snap of the end of February it started again, and she asked the man in his thirties. He took the top hinge off on the fourth of March, found somebody else's paper in the knuckle and somebody else's touch-up on the frame, worked out in about forty seconds who had been there and how, put the paper back, shifted both hinges three-eighths of an inch instead, and went down the stair with his bag. **The paper is still in the bottom hinge of that door. Neither of the two men has raised it with anybody, the man in his sixties does not know that a door on that landing was touched twice, and the woman who has the letting has never looked at it.**

## 2. WHAT WAS BEHIND A BATTEN

The man in his forties was chasing a length of pipework in a cellar off a side street in March and took a five-foot length of batten off the wall to get at it. Behind the batten, on plaster of two dates, there was a column of about thirty pencil crosses going up the wall, four inch apart, drawn with a pencil sharpened on a knife. Six of them show through a coat of pink distemper and four at the top were about four days old. He went back twice for no work at all, once on the last Thursday of March and once on the second of April, and did nothing in that cellar on either visit. **He has not put them to the man in his sixties, who goes down there most days, and he has not found the sentence for what they are, and he has not written any of it down anywhere including in his own head in words. THE CROSSES ARE A MARK AND NOT A CODE AND A LATER BATCH MAY NOT COUNT THEM AGAIN OR TURN THEM INTO A RIDDLE.**

## 3. WHAT ONE MAN FOUND ON THE OTHER SIDE OF A WALL

Two men worked the same building on the morning of the fourteenth of March, about twenty foot apart, for about four hours each, and neither knew the other was on it. The man in his thirties put a new shop door and frame in on the front; the man in his forties rebuilt nine foot of the top of a boundary wall in the yard behind. The man in his thirties came back at half past three for a bar and read a nine-foot line of chamfered arrises from twenty foot off. **He knew whose it was in about two seconds, because nobody else he has built alongside knocks the arris off a cut, went back in for his bar, and has never put it to the man in his forties, who knows the front was done and has not walked past the back.**

## 4. WHAT WAS ASKED FOR AND WAS GIVEN UP

A woman with the keys to a house that is being emptied came into a room at the end of a passage and asked the man in his forties for four brass stair rods he had put in a bag on a ledge there in May 2015 and never opened. He put the chisel down, took the bag off the ledge, and put the rods into her hand in about ten seconds. **He said nothing before, during or after, she wrote nothing down, a man in his thirties was in the doorway for nine minutes of it and has not been asked what he saw, and neither of them has put anything back to the other.**

## 5. WHAT WAS RAKED OUT

A man in his forties repointed nine foot of a north-facing garden wall on a Saturday in February because the water off a gutter was going down it, and told nobody. The man in his sixties told the man in his thirties on the eighth of March that the wall is coming down in June. On the twentieth the man in his thirties went into that yard for a downpipe, saw nine foot of new pointing, and thought nothing of it. He came back on the Wednesday after and raked the whole of it out and packed the rubble back in loose. **One thing in that wall cannot be undone, which is a thumbnail of brick taken off the face of it by the point of a bolster. The man in his forties went and looked on the fifth of April, worked out in four seconds what had happened and who had done it, and put the length in his van and shut the gate.**

## 6. WHAT WAS DONE IN AN EMPTY GARAGE

The man in his forties took his own chisel roll into a lock-up he has a key to and that he was not asked to be in, put water in the tray of a pedestal grinder that belongs to a man who is away that week, and ground four of his own chisels properly over four and a quarter hours. The woman who works in a shop came out of the ninth of those garages with a paper bag in each hand and stood at the mouth of his for about a minute and then drove away. **She has not been in that garage since and has not told the man in his sixties, and he wiped the bench and left the brick on the cover and said nothing about it, and the man in the garage did not hear a car door four doors away.**

## 7. WHAT WAS CARRIED DOWN A LANE AND LEFT UNDER IRON

The man in his thirties took two bands of twelve slates half a mile down a lane a van cannot go down, for the man in his forties, to a yard where that gate stood open on a hinge that has dropped and gone off square, with the bar leaning against the brick beside it, and there was nobody in it. He waited about twenty minutes, rang once, would not ring twice, and put the bands on a ledge under a length of corrugated iron that was leaning against the wall above it, and put the iron back leaning the other way. The man who works nights came past that gate at half past six that morning and did not stop. **The man in his forties came on the Wednesday of the fourth, saw the iron leaning the wrong way, lifted it, and did not ask anybody where they had been. He carried them the half mile in two loads and was on his own roof on the Friday.**

## 8. WHAT TWO MEN BOTH GOT WRONG

Two men went into the same locked store in the same week and each saw the same bundle of laths two inches forward of the nine below it with its band turned a quarter of a turn, and each worked out in about a second that the other had been in there, because the woman who works at that counter does not move laths. **TWO OF THE THREE PEOPLE WHO GO INTO THAT STORE HOLD A KEY TO IT AND THE THIRD HAS NEVER BEEN OFFERED ONE, AND NEITHER MAN KNEW THAT ABOUT THE OTHER.** Both of them were wrong. The woman moved that bundle twice herself in four days to get at a box of hinges behind it and put it down where her hand could reach it. **She has not been asked about it by either of them, and neither of the two will raise it, because to raise it is to admit to standing at a rack with nothing in your hands.**

## 9. WHAT WENT BACK AND WHAT DID NOT

The man in his forties had a first-floor flat to himself for a day in April and opened a door he did not need to open. On a sill in the front room there was a comb in a ring of dust that belonged to a man in his thirties and had been there since February. He put it back in the ring. Behind the door of the back room there was a coil of cable on a nail that belonged to the man in his sixties and had been there since the summer before last. He took that, and left the nail. **Nobody was told about either. The man in his thirties does not know about the comb and never will, and the man in his sixties has not opened that door and is not going to before the summer.**

## 10. WHAT A BOROUGH DID ON THE EIGHTEENTH OF APRIL

A wind came up the river for half an hour and took the front off a canvas awning over a shop about two thirds of the way up that parade, and the man who puts shutters up came down off the top of it, put a pair of steps on the kerb, put the chain back over its cleat, wound the awning down and tied the front bar to the frame with a piece of cord from his pocket, and was gone by two. The woman who works in a shop heard the noise, looked out for about half a minute, came out and stood at the foot of his steps and watched him for about ten seconds, and said nothing to him and has said nothing to anybody. **The shutter at the top of that parade still will not shut and a paving slab in the middle of it still stands an inch and a half proud, and neither has been put right or reported. The line under the last entry in the book in a block by the water was at one thousand two hundred and thirty-nine days on that day and was not touched, and the one thing nobody in that borough could explain was the same one it was a fortnight before.**

## 12A. THE VERBATIM-SPAN METHOD AS IT WAS BUILT FOR THIS BATCH, AND THE ONE THING THAT WAS WRONG IN THE FIRST BUILDING

**ONE, THE THRESHOLD IS NINE TOKENS AND IT IS NAMED EVERY TIME. TWO, THE SCRIPT COMPARES TOKENS AND NOT CHARACTERS, ON `[a-z0-9']+` APPLIED TO LOWERCASED TEXT, AND A TOKEN THAT IS NOTHING BUT APOSTROPHE MARKS IS A QUOTATION MARK AND IS DROPPED. THREE, THE H1 TITLE LINE IS DROPPED, EVERY `---` LINE IS DROPPED, AND EVERY STANDALONE ALL-CAPS PARAGRAPH IS DROPPED, WITH OR WITHOUT BOLD MARKERS. FOUR, A SPAN IS A MAXIMAL RUN OF NINE CONSECUTIVE TOKENS SHARED WITH THE COMPARISON SET, EXTENDED BY DIRECT TOKEN COMPARISON FROM EVERY REAL POSITION THE NINE-GRAM OCCUPIES IN THE SET FILE, AND NOT FROM THE HEAD OF THAT FILE. FIVE, EVERY SPAN IS ASSERTED CONTIGUOUS IN THE OTHER FILE BY DIRECT TOKEN COMPARISON, AND THE ASSERTION IS IN THE SCRIPT. SIX, A PARAGRAPH BOUNDARY IS A SENTINEL NO TOKEN CAN EQUAL, IN THE TARGET AND IN EVERY SET FILE, AND NO SPAN CROSSES ONE, WHICH IS IMPLEMENTED AS A TEST THAT NEITHER SIDE OF THE MATCH LEAVES THE PARAGRAPH IT STARTED IN AND NOT AS A TEST THAT THE TWO PARAGRAPH NUMBERS ARE EQUAL. SEVEN, A CHAPTER IS NEVER INCLUDED IN THE SET IT IS COMPARED AGAINST AND EACH FILE OF A SET IS COMPARED SEPARATELY. EIGHT, THREE CLASSES ARE EXCLUDED AND RECORDED AS A COUNT AND NOT CHASED: A DATELINE, A FIGURE'S OWN BY-NAME DESCRIPTION, AND A BOROUGH'S OWN RECURRING PLACE NOUN. NINE, THE CONTROL IS ASKED FOR BEFORE ANY FIGURE IS BELIEVED AND IS TWO PAIRS AND A PLANT. TEN, EVERY FIGURE IS TAKEN AGAIN AFTER EVERY REPAIR AND AGAIN AT THE END.**

**AND THE THING THAT WAS WRONG IN THE FIRST BUILDING IS RECORDED BECAUSE A LATER WRITER WILL BUILD IT AGAIN. A BY-NAME DESCRIPTION IS A DETERMINER AND A HEAD NOUN ANYWHERE ACROSS THE SPAN, NOT AT THE HEAD OF IT, AND THE COMMA THAT BOUNDS THE RUN IS THE COMMA IN WHICHEVER OF THE TWO FILES HAS IT, BECAUSE THE TWO FILES ARE ONE RUN SEEN FROM OPPOSITE ENDS AND A BOUND FOUND ON ONE SIDE IS THE BOUND. **WRITING IT THE OTHER WAY ROUND — OPENING WITH A DETERMINER, AND LOOKING FOR THE COMMA IN THE TARGET ONLY — DOES NOT FIND MORE REUSE. IT FINDS LESS, AND IT TOOK THE 326-TOKEN CONTROL DOWN TO 199, AND A CONTROL THAT COMES BACK AT 199 IS A SCRIPT THAT IS WRONG AND NOT A PAIR OF FILES THAT ARE.**

**AND THE HEAD-NOUN SET HOLDS FIGURES ONLY. A BY-NAME DESCRIPTION DESCRIBES A PERSON AND A PLACE IS NOT A PERSON, AND THE BOROUGH'S OWN PLACE NOUNS ARE THE THIRD EXCLUDED CLASS, WHICH IS WHERE THEY BELONG. A PASS THAT EXCLUDES SOMETHING IT SHOULD NOT IS A PASS THAT HAS HIDDEN A FINDING, AND IT IS THE SAME FAILURE AS A PASS THAT ADDS AN ENTRY TO A LIST.**
