## §1. Nine foot of ground, and two people who would not be second

She had it in October and never asked. He has wanted it since about the end of October and has never once taken it.

Twice in one afternoon they were close enough to have spoken about it and neither did, and at six o'clock the ground was as it had been, and she went off to a bus and he shut a gateway up the street.

Neither has the other's half of it. He has not seen her. She has not seen where his things go. Each came to the same conclusion independently, and the conclusion was that whoever goes second is the one who looks like they took something, and neither is willing to look like that, and neither will raise it.

## §2. A store door, and a man who shut it

A door at the back of that kitchen was moving in the draught and he closed it as he passed, and there was a store behind it that had not been empty for some weeks.

What he took out of that room with him was a ring in the dust on a box, and there is no way to account for it.

He has not gone back in, has not questioned the neighbour, and has slowed down for nothing on four passes of that building. She put the boxes to him and he gave her the short answer and she let it lie, and six weeks have gone by with nothing said.

## §3. Six minutes longer, every weekday morning

A woman she has never spoken to was missing from a spot she had been in the habit of seeing for years, and rather than raise it with anybody she altered her own route to avoid passing it, at a cost of six minutes a morning.

Ten days of it, and the whole of that street has seen her pass every morning and has not remarked on anything. She will not open the subject herself.

There is nothing to revert, because nobody was keeping a record but her.

## §4. A door, held for a fortnight and then let go

He had been shutting that door for six years out of habit and she had been leaving it for four months out of a principle about not making people stop, and the two of them had never discussed either.

She did it once, and he understood inside a couple of seconds that the change was hers, and he sat on it for a fortnight before doing the same.

Both know and neither has said anything, and the door is now shut more often than it is not, and nobody could date the change.

## §5. A true answer to the wrong question

She put a question to him in a passage that she could not put in any other way, and he gave her an answer that was true and that he believed he had earned.

He worked out four days later that she sleeps at the front and that stair is at the back and that there is a woman on the third floor and a man on the ground floor, and that her question had not been about his sight at all.

She has asked him nothing since, of anything. He will not go back and take the answer back, because withdrawing it would hand her a different problem and he does not know which one.

## §6. A building worked out through two windows

Seven weeks of watching from her own front room, and what she has is not a thing anybody told her but a thing she assembled out of what that building gives away to anybody on the opposite pavement.

She has also worked out that the man who stands outside that shop is not a passer-by, and he has not spoken to her once in all of the seven weeks and could not say who she is.

She is not going to say it to the woman at number eight, because how she knows is that she has been watching that building since October. she has been carrying it since early November and it has cost her something every day.

## §7. A length of wire in a joint, twice

The same small repair, made in the same place, on two different days, by two men who have never met and do not know of each other.

A car lifted the slab out and it lay off the path for three days. A woman found the gap, looked at it, and kept it to herself. The man in his thirties put it back and did to it what had been done to it before, because that is now the only version of that repair that exists.

There is no list of that ground and nobody owns it. before long the whole of that will stand proud again.

## §8. A sentence about a wall that was not all of it

He did about nine foot of repointing on a wall over three days and left about eighteen inch of the bottom of it because there is a pipe inside that wall and the bottom cannot be reached without taking four foot of it off.

He reported the job finished to a man who wrote it down and was gone. She has seen exactly what he left and has decided that the one question worth asking is one she will not ask.

What he is protecting is the four foot of that wall higher up that nobody has ever properly looked at, and raising the foot of it would have started something he has no standing to finish.

## §9. Four inches, and the wrong foot

She watched a man cross a step over running water twice without stopping, worked out four days later that it was a thing rather than an accident, and did it on the Saturday morning and got it wrong, because he is right-footed and she is left-footed.

He was nine foot behind her and did not slow and did not look up. She has been over it again about nine times since and has got it right four times and is not going to let that put her off, and not because she minds a wet shoe.

## §10. A Thursday, and a length of iron off a wall

Nine people on that parade in that stretch of the morning, none of them there because of any of the other eight. something came off a wall at half past twelve, three men had it back up in ten minutes on a different fixing three inch to the left, the owner was told nothing and put her hand flat on it at two and went in.

The line under the last entry of that book stood open since the middle of March three years before that and nobody went near it. Four answers are still going round and no fifth has come in and nobody put any two of them together and nobody asked anybody what any of them was an answer to.

What a person in that street cannot put a name to has not shifted by a day since the middle of August. The woman with the dog came back down at ten past two, went past the wall without looking at it, and went down to the end.

**AND ON THE THIRD OF JANUARY A MAN IN HIS FORTIES WALKED UP THAT PARADE WITH A BROWN PAPER BAG UNDER HIS ARM AND DID NOT LOOK AT THE WALL EITHER, AND HE DID NOT KNOW IT HAD BEEN OFF.**

A man reported a length of wall complete and left a foot of it unpointed, and a woman living in that building saw the join and decided the only question worth asking was one she would not ask. ## §1. A cat, a coping, and a fortnight of going round

A man had walked the same cut twice a day for nine years and something small that had always been on a wall in it was not there on a Sunday in January. He went the long way for a fortnight. On the third Monday he went through. He has never asked anybody about it. The woman on the other side of that corner has the animal and had stopped letting it out before Christmas and has not opened her door about it since. Each of them arrived at the same impasse from opposite ends of a wall neither of them can see over, and neither of them knows that the other is in it.

## §2. Three floors, one stair, and a noise through a ceiling

Two people in a building of three flats had each built a version of a woman on the top floor out of a sound at half past two in the morning. In January he saw her leave. In January she saw her go. Each of them learned one thing and neither learned the other thing, and the reason each of them will not put it to her is a different thing entirely, and his is a man who does not want to be listened to and hers is a woman who has decided that eight months of lying awake entitles a stranger to be left alone.

## §3. Two minutes of noise at half past five

A man walked from his own door to his van making a sound for about two minutes every weekday morning. A woman above a garage behind his house asked him once, in about eleven seconds and seven words, to leave off. He stopped for a week. Then he did it again, and the reason he did it again is a removal she has booked for April that he worked out from two things and has never mentioned to anybody.

## §4. A landing, and a side that was chosen in 2013

A woman has stood on one particular side of a man on a landing since a March in 2013, because she had a thing to say once and did not want to say it twice. In January he told her, without any edge on it, that the ear she had chosen is the one that hears everything and the other one has gone. She is not going to change sides, and the reason is not the ear.

## §5. A thing carried out of a house every morning

A man has carried an armchair out of his own front door and left it on a kerb every weekday since 2013, and a woman at the end of the row has carried it in at one every day of that without either of them ever referring to it. On the twenty-fifth of January he put it down and walked on. It rained on it. He has parked on the far side of that road ever since and has no reason he would say out loud.

## §6. Two minutes at a car, and a window that was already there

A man stands at his own car every morning with his hand flat on the door for about two minutes and does not get in. A woman four houses away takes her cup to a window she has always sat at and did not know until the seventeenth of January that she did it on purpose. He has not looked up since that morning. Thirteen days of neither of them raising it, and she has decided she would rather be a woman who watches him than a woman who announces she has stopped.

## §7. A machine at the back of a building, and two women under it

Two women live one above the other over a machine that runs for twenty-two minutes. The older has wanted it to stop for two years and nine months and has said nothing to anybody. The younger started minding after Christmas and has spent a fortnight angry that the older never said. A man changed a timer and an arm of metal for reasons of his own. Both women now know and neither can say anything, and the older is worse off than she was, and neither will ask him.

## §8. A flank wall, and a fact nobody can be given

A man has known since 2014 that the boundary wall of a kitchen is carrying the side of the house next door, and he is right, and the whole of why he cannot hand that to anybody is in two occasions on which he was inside that wall in 2013 and 2016 with nobody in either house knowing. He said it once in September and was asked not to say it again. She has added up the three things she could do and cannot afford any of them, and has decided not to ask him, because asking him would be asking him to be somebody he has told her he is not.

## §9. Ten seconds at a corner

A woman stopped at a corner in January and let a man get to the kerb first and said nothing while he did. He has worked out what it meant and cannot ask, because there are three things it could have been and he has settled on one and cannot weigh it against the other two. She is not going to find out which of the two she is in, because one of them is a thing she has carried for nothing and the other is a thing she would have to answer for, and she has no answer.

## §10. A Sunday, and four foot of pavement

Nine people went up and down a parade on the twenty-fourth of February for reasons of their own. A man swept nine foot of pavement an hour earlier than usual. Underneath the grit there is four foot of paving a different colour from the rest of it, and it was in the sun for about two minutes, and nobody looked at it and nobody has ever looked at it. A door in a wall at the top end is not locked and has no bench in it and has not been through since before Christmas. The four answers went nowhere. The page is still empty.

## §1. What the people of this batch are each carrying now

**A MAN AT NUMBER SEVEN IN A ROW OF TWELVE.** He wanted thirty square yard at the top of an acre behind him and he asked for it in 2015, in 2017 and in October, and he was refused three times without any unkindness, and in November the woman who owns that ground told him she had let the whole of it to somebody from the town, and he said one word and shut his own front door. He has a second hive than he had in February and he has three where the ground will take two, and he put them in nine foot at the back of his own house, between his own wall and the next one, in full view of a window. He has worked out that he does not mind that. He has not got as far as why. Nobody in that row knows that he ever wanted anything, and he has not told one person, and he has not been near that door since November.

**A WOMAN AT NUMBER THREE IN THAT ROW.** She heard him say in a July that is nine months gone that there was no point in anybody asking, and she heard the wrong half of that sentence, and she went in January. Three times. On his behalf, with his number said out loud on a doorstep, twice making sure it was not for herself. In January she was told that nobody had ever asked about that ground in about twenty years, and she believed it, and the belief has been sitting on her since, and what it amounts to is a charge against a man who is not in the room. In the second week of April she was told the whole thing went in March. She said one word to the owner of that ground and carried on with what she was carrying. She has not told him any of it and she is not going to, and the reason she has settled on is that there is no way of telling a man who has given up that somebody went to a door about it that does not charge him with something.

**A WOMAN AT NUMBER FOUR IN A PASSAGE, AND A WOMAN AT THE TOP OF IT, AND A MAN WHO WENT IN FOUR MORNINGS A WEEK FOR SIX YEARS.** The woman at number four has stood on her own step every morning since about 1990 for air and has wanted, since about November, for a man to give up something that was not hers to give up. In the third week of February she gave the woman at the top of that passage a true answer to a question she had not been asked. The woman at the top of it heard it and went on being exactly the same, which was worse than either of the two things she had braced for, and she has not said one word about it to anybody in nineteen years. The man came for six more weeks and she watched every one of them. He came out of that house on the first of April with empty hands, which he had never done, and he stopped in the middle of that passage and looked back up it, and he did not go back. She was fourteen yard away and did not move for about two minutes. She has two possible explanations and one of them is her own mouth in a market, and she cannot put the other one out of her head, and the only way to find out is the one thing she is not going to do. The woman at the top of that passage now has nobody in her house on a weekday morning and has told nobody and is worse off than she was in February.

**TWO MEN INSIDE A RULE, AND A WOMAN BEHIND SIX FOOT OF WALL.** A third man made the rule in 2008 in about a minute and has never explained it. Asking would be telling, which is why ten years on neither of the two knows whether the other is keeping it. They spent an hour in March on the third man's life and neither of them got to the part of it that mattered, and one of them said out loud that nothing was going on and both have since treated that as something that was said rather than something that was true. They each went home certain they had been quietly written off, and neither of them was wrong about the other's behaviour and neither of them can say so. The woman behind the wall has seen the third man come in at four in the morning four times since January and has said nothing to anybody and is not going to.

**A MAN IN HIS SIXTIES AND A DOG.** He has walked one stretch of that street, at one hour, for twelve years. In January he found out that a man new to the row had gone to a neighbour twice to ask a question about waste bags, and that told him everything, and he has been carrying it since December. In January the new man did something on purpose in front of him. In March he stood still on a far kerb and let a dog be over rather than cross a road at ten past six in front of about nine people. He has drawn one conclusion from all of it and it is about himself rather than about the other man, and he is going to keep drawing it every morning, and he knows that is what he is doing.

**A WOMAN AT THE LAST DOOR IN A COVERED WAY, AND A MAN EMPTIES A HOUSE.** She has a floor two foot away from where he put it down and she has used it, and she has kept the small account rather than the large one, and she is going to keep the small one for the rest of her life because the large one involves her. What she has not put down is the second he spent standing still with a dying plant in his hands, and she saw it from a doorway. He has a sentence for everything that comes out of that house and he has used it about four hundred times and it is not a lie, and he has now used it about a thing that is nine foot inside somebody else's door and is standing on a floor. Neither of them has said anything and neither is going to.

**A MAN WHO CAME TO MEASURE A FRAME, AND A WOMAN WHO CAME OUT INTO HER OWN DOORWAY.** He was seventeen in 1974 and he cut nine marks and nobody ever told him what they were for, and under them there are two he did not cut, and he has known since the eighth of March and has not said so, because the frame comes out in April and the marks go with it and nobody has told her there is anything in it to lose. She has been carrying a second thing since 2004 without knowing she was carrying it, and it is about her son, and she is right about it. They talked for about ten minutes and neither of them mentioned the other's to the other, and a piece of joinery went down that street in April with two sets of marks on it.

**A WOMAN WHO HAS DRIVEN FOUR MILES EVERY SUNDAY SINCE 1999, AND THE MAN SHE DRIVES.** He has never asked her anything in twenty years and the reason is not that she seemed unwilling. Her hours changed in January. She did not come on the tenth of March, and when he drove to her street at four in the afternoon and put the question to her, the question that came out of his mouth was about the twenty years and not about the missing Sunday, and she answered it properly, and she is not going to take the answer back. He drove himself the following Sunday and was not late. She went back to that corner the same afternoon with a bag and stood on it. Neither of them has any idea what the other did and neither is going to ask.

**TWO PEOPLE AND A BLOCKED WAY.** Each of them has worked out, separately and without ever putting it to the other, that the other is the person who ought to cut four yard of green wood back off a hundred-yard way. His reason is that a stranger will put it forward again inside a year and a bigger reason he has not told anybody. Her reason is that the bed is not hers and there is nothing about the outside of that house anybody could point at. They met in the rain for about two minutes in February and the whole of what was said was two words and neither offered nor refused anything, and both of them had been ready to, and neither has mentioned it since, and her lease is up in June and nobody in that row knows.

**THE MAN IN HIS THIRTIES, WHO HAS GONE PAST A BOARDED BUILDING TWICE A DAY SINCE THE MIDDLE OF FEBRUARY, AND THE WOMAN WHO GOES IN AND OUT OF IT.** Five weeks of going past has produced one thing he cannot put down and no decision, and what he has not done is knock on a door, and the reason is a torch in 2013 and a ladder in 2016 and two afternoons he has never spoken to anybody about. He has not got to whether he is right, and he has not got to whether being right is the thing that would stop him either. She has gone in and out of the front of that building on a weekday for five weeks with something in her arms, and he has counted her twice a day and worked out three things about her and told himself that three is where he stops. They have been about four paces apart in that street thirty times and neither of them knows what the other is doing there. He went to work at ten to eight on the morning the front of that building came down off a scaffold, and he will go past it tomorrow.

**NINE PEOPLE ON A PARADE, A VAN, A PLANTER, AND A ROOM BEHIND A FLANK WALL.** Nine people on that street on a Wednesday evening and none of them for the same reason, and the only thing that went wrong was a van coming back the wrong way and a concrete planter ending up four inch out from a shop wall. Nine people went round it. Nobody stopped and nobody said anything and the driver came back on foot and apologised and offered to pay for another one and the woman at that counter said it would not go. A man shut the shop next door, as he has for about seven years, and nobody has asked him and he has never said no. Along the side of the last building on that street there is a door that stands open along its bottom edge, is not locked, and is not storage anybody rents; behind it is a ground-floor room that has had nothing in it since about 2011 and that nobody in this borough has been inside in about eight years, and the reason no one goes in is that getting in means standing on a piece of ground at the side of that building, two hundred square yard of it, with no way out through the back, and a person with no reason to be on it does not stand on it.

## §1. What the people of this batch are each carrying now, grouped by person and not by chapter

**THE OLDER OF TWO SIBLINGS WHO BOTH WANTED THE OTHER ONE TO RAISE IT.** He came round to the truth of that house on his own, on foot, in the middle of March, and he has been carrying it since without once setting it down in front of anybody in his family. What stops him is not caution and it is not indifference. It is that he has decided his mother makes every decision in the last few minutes before she is forced to, and that a knock from him would have forced her to make one on a Saturday evening with nobody else in the house. So he watched, and then he went to work, and he has told nobody. When his sister telephoned that evening he gave her the fact of the man in the garden and kept back everything underneath it, and what came back down the line was a pause long enough for both of them to have said something, and neither did.

**THE YOUNGER OF THOSE TWO SIBLINGS.** A woman at her children's school told her something in a car park on a Monday in March, and then apologised for telling her, and the apology made it worse. She turned it over for a fortnight. She built a plan in one afternoon in which she passes the whole thing to her brother, and she built the opposite plan in the same sitting, and she has never told either version of herself which one she meant. When he did eventually put the bare fact to her down the telephone she answered him with a noise that was not a question, because a question would have started it, and she has sat on the end of her own bed since with the telephone still in her hand. She has no idea he was carrying the same thing, and he has no idea she was, and neither of them has ever said so to the other.

**THEIR MOTHER.** She has had that house since about 2011 and she was widowed slowly. In February she handed over one key off a ring she had been given years ago and she did not add a word to the handing of it. She gets herself ready when the grass man comes, and does not when her son is on the step, and she has caught herself doing both and has not sat with it. Neither child has ever asked her what she makes of any of it. She has no idea that two separate people in her family each worked out the same fact about her house in the same fortnight and neither of them said a word about it to the other, and if she had been told she would not have had a way of holding both of those at once.

**THE MAN AT NUMBER FOURTEEN, WHO CUTS THAT GRASS AND DRIVES HER TO THE SHOPS.** He took the job on in February and has been inside that house most days since March, and does the front strip and the back and takes her into town twice a week and puts her at her own kerb. He has tested twice, in his own head, whether she is glad to see him, and the evidence he keeps returning to is a coat. **The trouble is that she puts that coat on for the bread as well, and does not put it on when her son is on the step, and he has decided the difference is about the reason she is letting him in and not about her feelings, and he has not gone one step past that and is not going to.**

**THE MAN WHO HAS DRIVEN UP TO THE TOP OF THAT CAR PARK AT TEN O'CLOCK ON A WEDNESDAY NIGHT SINCE 1989.** Thirty years of a Wednesday night and the thing at the top of it has never had a single witness who wanted an account of it, and he has never offered one. A woman from the hospital at Cleeve cornered him in April and he answered her, and the reason he answered her is not that she asked but that he had read her inside of about half a minute and was certain of where the conversation would stop. What came out was not an explanation of anything. The seventeenth was the first night in something like a quarter of a century that he did not go up, and the nineteenth was worse, because on the nineteenth he got as far as the foot of the ramp, stood there in front of four orange cones and a barrier that had not gone up, and went home. He has not decided whether the cones did that.

**THE WOMAN WHO PARKED THERE ON HER WAY BACK FROM A SHIFT.** She had driven in behind him twice a year for about two years and had never once treated him as a thing that was happening. Then her hours changed in February and a colleague said something careless in a staff room about a man who crosses a river on a Wednesday to stand on a car park, and she worked out within a minute which man it was, because of the car. She went and asked him at ten past ten on the tenth of April, and he gave her three sentences, and what he gave her was a way of describing himself rather than an account of anything. She has not been back since, and she will not write, and neither of them has treated that as a falling out, because there was nothing in the conversation to fall out over.

**THE TWO PEOPLE AT NUMBER TWENTY-TWO.** There was an intruder in that house on a Friday night in April and there is not one thing missing from it, which is the part that frightens her and not the rest. A neighbour who was up in the small hours saw a light moving low down the outside of the house and thought nothing of it until a week later, when she was pegging out. A man further down the street was sitting in his own car at that hour waiting on somebody who never arrived, and he saw the same light and sat on it for twenty minutes before deciding to say something. **She took her account of it as a threat to the two of them and has kept it from him, because she has decided in advance what he would do with it, and it would be a man out at night with a second chain and a purchase. He took his account of it as a man about his own height in his own dark coat and cannot get past that, and has decided she does not need the trouble of it.** Both of those decisions are protective and neither of them is a conversation, and there has not been one. On the Tuesday morning he secured the other entrance before she was down and she found it standing there and neither of them said a word about it.

**THE TWO MEN AT THE END OF THAT LANE WITH THE HORSE.** They grew up four doors apart and have never once been the sort that talks about anything, and what they bought at that gate in March 2016 they did with two cans between them and no paper. Three years on, one of them runs the whole operation and the other one does every animal job in it, and the arrangement has never once been said out loud between them. The one who wanted his money back asked four times over two years, always in the autumn, and gave up in a field in three seconds after being told that there was no such thing as a half of this. **Each of them has built the same false picture of the other and they are opposite pictures: the man with the cart is convinced his partner never cared, and the man who does the feeding is convinced his partner had never noticed the asking at all.** Neither has anything that would let him check. In April one of them walked the full length of that lane in bad weather to help a horse up a rise, was refused, said nothing at all, and then stood at the animal's head anyway and got her up it.

**THE WOMAN WHO HAS HAD THE GARDEN BEHIND THOSE TWO HOUSES SINCE 2003.** She owns the left-hand of that pair and nobody has been on that ground in sixteen years but her. One strip at the bottom of it has been wrong since the spring of 2011: lower than its neighbours, yellow in late June, green again when the rest has gone. She has reseeded it twice with the correct seed and it has died twice, and since 2016 she has been buying something else from a man in a shop four miles off who asks how she is getting on, which is the only reason she keeps buying it. She waters that one strip and no other part of that lawn. **Asked why it is different she would say that is simply how that end of the garden is, and she would believe it completely.** She has never suspected a person and never wondered whether there is anything owed on that ground, and that is not generosity, because there is nobody she could say it to.

**THE MAN WHO PUT A MACHINE OVER THAT STRIP IN 2011 AND DOES NOT LIVE IN EITHER HOUSE.** He took turf off that lawn in four pieces in February 2011 to get at ground that was not the woman's, tipped what came out of it back on top, went over the same ground four times, and put the turf down in pieces that did not line up with anything. Nobody was on the ground all week and there was no hole left behind. In January of this year he was waiting at that gate in the dark for somebody else and found himself looking straight at eight years of it, and he had the whole of it in a few seconds from that distance. **He has said none of it to anybody and has not gone back, and he has turned up at that gate twice since for work that has nothing to do with the woman.** What he cannot put down is not her loss, which he accepts entirely, but his own part in not returning to look at what he had left. On the eighth of May he had as long as the evening would give him and used none of it.

**THE MAN WHO LOCKED UP A BUILDING OFF THAT PARADE.** Two words, said to a table in a back room in February 2016, in a building he had been the last out of for twelve years and had never once been given a name for. Four people were close enough to catch it and the four accounts that came out of that room that night have never been laid side by side. One of the four was not in the room at all and has said publicly that she was not listening. **He has been asked about it three times since and has given a different answer to each of them, and on the thirteenth of May the fourth one came to his own front room and asked, and he had four answers loaded and picked one in about a second because it was the one that would empty his room fastest. It is true. It is also not what he means, and he is the only person alive who knows there are three others, and he has told nobody and does not intend to.**

**THE TWO WOMEN AT NUMBER THIRTY AND NUMBER THIRTY-FOUR.** In May 2016 an articulated lorry carrying a boat came down that street before anybody was up, stopped outside the lower of the two houses for long enough that it was noticed, and went on. The woman at the lower number has spent three years on a version of it in which the length of the stop was the point and not the boat, and she has never wanted to know why, because knowing would oblige her to act. The woman at the upper number was not in that street for most of that year and learned the whole thing secondhand, in one telling, with no questions asked of her, and what she has carried since is not the lorry but the not-asking. **They do not argue. They nod. Neither has heard the other's version, and after about two years the first question became a question neither of them could begin.** In May of this year a lorry slowed in the same stretch of road and both of them saw it from where they were and neither went out, and later that morning one of them crossed the road to the other's gate and could not remember on the way what she had come to say, and turned round in the road and went home.

**THE MAN WHO PUTS A BOWL OUT AND THE WOMAN WHO PUT ONE OUT.** A dog went out through a front door in June 2013 and was never seen again by anybody in the borough, and there is nobody on that street who could have let it out and not shut the door behind. **He has kept a bowl on his own back step every night since, without missing one, washing it each morning, and nobody has ever asked and he has never said.** She began putting one out on her own step a fortnight later, half an hour after his, and went on doing it for five years, and stopped in the first week of November of last year after working out, with a bowl in her hand, that her own mother had done exactly this after a dog of hers had gone in 1981 and had told nobody in that family either. It is in a cupboard under her stairs now. He noticed on the night of the frost and has said nothing to anybody. **In March he changed his own hour because of the shade behind that row, which put him out in the same daylight as a thing she used to do, and neither of them has ever been able to say how the other one came to be out at that hour at all.** On the twenty-third of May they met at the corner of his yard, said good morning, and she went back in with it in her hand and neither of them said anything else.

**THE MAN ON THE ROUND WITH THE BOXES AND THE WOMAN AT NUMBER TWENTY-NINE.** He has carried other people's deliveries into other people's houses for four years and goes in through whatever door is open, because that is the whole method and it has never once cost him anything. On the twenty-seventh of May he took a box that was not for that house, set it down on the table you always pass in a place like that, and was gone before the woman had come down. **She found it, did not open it, did not look at anything on it, and worked out on her own what it was and where it belonged, and carried it back herself, put it where it belonged, struck the door once with the edge of her hand, and went home.** It was four minutes out and four minutes back. Neither of them has said a word about it to the other or to anybody, and neither of them is going to remember it.

## §12C. THE REPAIRS, AND WHAT THEY WERE

1. **AND THE FINDING OF THE CONTROL, WHICH IS THE ELEVENTH TIME IN TWELVE BLOCKS THAT THE CHAPTER IMMEDIATELY ABOVE IS THE WORST PLACE IN A WINDOW, AND THIS TIME IT WAS THE LAST CHAPTER AGAINST THE LAST CHAPTER AGAIN.** 0029's control came back at 10 RAW, 9 REUSES and a longest of 23, seven of the nine being 0484 against 0474. **0030's card asked for the same shape — a parade, about nine people, a shop off it and a place with a door in it — for the tenth time, and the repair is the fifth part, which is the hour, the weekday, the small wrong thing and the door.** 0494 was written from nothing at about half past six on a Monday morning out of a man carrying a box into the wrong house, and the control came back at **1 RAW, 0 REUSES, LONGEST 0**, and it was taken at the END and not at the start, which is the argument the 0028 block set down and it held again.
2. **AND THE FINDING OF THE CARD CLASS, WHICH IS THE TWELFTH CONFIRMATION, AND IT REPRODUCED TWICE IN THIS BATCH, BOTH IN CHAPTERS, BOTH REPAIRED IN THE CHAPTERS.** In 0486 a paragraph in the body reproduced its own card's *MAJOR TURN* in the card's own words — that he told her because she asked and because she was not going to tell anybody — and it came back at RUN FIVE at ten tokens against the prompt for this batch. It was rewritten from nothing about him and about the two conditions, and **no card was edited after its chapter existed and no card may be narrowed toward the prose afterwards.** In 0492 an opening block and a closing block both reproduced a stock phrase this account uses constantly, and both were rewritten in the chapter's own words.
3. **AND THE FINDING OF THE 385–394 WINDOW, WHICH BROKE TWICE IN THIS BATCH AND WAS CLEARED TWICE IN THE CHAPTERS AND NOT BY ADDING ANYTHING TO ANY EXCLUSION LIST.** It came back first at 4 RAW, 3 REUSES and a longest of 11, on 0485, 0488 and 0489, all three of them ordinary sentence skeletons and none of them a by-name tag. Two ordinary clauses in 0488 and 0489 were rewritten, and it came back at 1 RAW and 1 REUSE on a further paragraph added to 0490 in a later repair pass, and that clause was rewritten too. **THE FIGURE FOR THAT WINDOW IS NOW 0 RAW, 0 REUSES, LONGEST 0 AND HAS NOW HELD FOR ELEVEN BLOCKS RUNNING.**
4. **AND THE FINDING OF RUN TWO, WHICH IS A FINDING ABOUT A WRITER AND NOT ABOUT THE CHAPTERS.** The ten against each other came back at 14 RAW and 4 REUSES on a longest of 11 in four pairs, and two of those four were one sentence skeleton inside this batch — *and there are about nine people in this borough who have* in 0488 and 0491, and *with his coat over his arm and stood at the* in 0488 and 0494. Both were rewritten at source in 0488 and 0494.
5. **AND THE FINDING OF RUN FOUR AND RUN FIVE, WHICH COST 0028 SEVENTY AND 0029 SEVENTY-SEVEN AND COST THIS BATCH ELEVEN AND FOURTEEN, AND EVERY ONE OF THEM WAS A CHAPTER REPEATING A FILE OR A CARD.** Both fell in one pass and both went to nil without a section being thrown out, because the passages that carried them were ordinary clause shapes — *has said one word about*, *is not going to*, *that is the whole of* — and the repair was to write each of those sentences again rather than to take anything out. **THE STATE FILES FOR THIS BATCH WERE WRITTEN AFTER THOSE REPAIRS AND BEFORE RUN ONE WAS TAKEN A SECOND TIME, AND §1 TO §10 OF BOTH THE CONTINUITY AND THE OPEN-THREADS BLOCKS WERE WRITTEN GROUPED BY PERSON AND FROM NOTHING ABOUT ANY EVENT, WHICH IS THE THING 0029 SET DOWN AND WHICH HELD.**
6. **AND THE FINDING OF RUN SEVEN, WHICH IS THE THIRD OF ITS CLASS IN THREE BLOCKS AND THE BIGGEST OF THEM.** The ten datelines came back at **10 RAW, 10 REUSES, LONGEST 16**, every one of them, because all ten of them had been written in one frame and the frame is nine tokens long. **ALL TEN DATELINES WERE REWRITTEN IN THE TEN CHAPTERS — five with a full stop after the date and two with a dash, and different connective skeletons in each — AND NOT ONE DATE, WEEKDAY, MONTH, YEAR OR HOUR WAS ALTERED WHILE DOING IT.** A DATELINE IS DETECTED STRUCTURALLY BY THE METHOD AND A PARAGRAPH BEGINNING WITH THE NAME OF A DAY IS STILL WHAT ALL TEN OF THEM DO, AND THE DRIVER PRINTED ALL TEN AND ASSERTED ONE PER FILE BEFORE IT REPORTED, AND THE ASSERTION PASSED.
7. **AND THE THIRD SCRIPT FAULT, WHICH WAS FOUND AND FIXED IN THE DRIVER AND NOT IN THE CHAPTERS.** The positive-control plant was being taken from chapter 0482, which is not in the set of chapters this batch is measured against, so the control returned **0 RAW, 0 REUSES** — which looks like a pass and is a failure, and would have closed the pass. It was repointed to 0485 and came back at **1 RAW, 1 REUSE, LONGEST 14**, which is what a fourteen-token plant is for. **THE RUN-SEVEN FUNCTION INHERITED INTO THIS BATCH KEPT ITS PRINTED CONFIRMATION: IT PRINTS EVERY DATELINE IT READS AND ASSERTS ONE PER FILE BEFORE IT WILL REPORT, AND A WRITER OF 495 HAS TO LOOK AT WHAT ITS OWN FUNCTION PRINTED FIRST.**
8. **AND THE FIVE FINDINGS OF THE REVIEW THAT FOLLOWED THIS BATCH, ALL OF WHICH WERE THINGS NO RUN IN THIS REPOSITORY CAN SEE, AND ALL OF WHICH WERE REPAIRED IN THE CHAPTERS WITHOUT ALTERING A SINGLE DATE, EVENT, FIGURE, STANDING OR MAJOR TURN.** **THE REVIEWER'S OWN WORST FIGURE IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS MOST: A CHAPTER OF THIS BATCH OPENED WITH A DRAWING OF ITSELF ON A CHALKBOARD, WHICH NOTHING MEASURES.**
   - **(a) A SINGLE ORDINARY WORD HAD BECOME THE BATCH'S FILLER.** The word *nine* stood at **113 across the ten chapters**, against 64 in 475–484 and 40 in 465–474, and it was being used for durations, widths, spans, counts of years, counts of sentences, counts of loads and counts of households in a single chapter, and 0492's own title was built on it and its body said it nine times. **NONE OF THE NINE-TOKEN RUNS COULD SEE IT, BECAUSE A SPREAD-OUT WORD IS NOT A SPAN.** It is now at **44 in the ten, and the places that are left are clock times, two door numbers and a count of sentences in a chapter about a lorry.** The repair was to send each use somewhere else in its own sentence, and no date, no gap and no day-count moved.
   - **(b) TWO CHAPTERS THREE APART RAN THE SAME DOOR.** 0485's opening block was a man letting himself in through a side door, and 0487 was titled for a side door on the latch, and **they are not adjacent, so no window in this repository compares them and the collision was invisible to every run.** 0487 now turns on the back door it already had in its own body, which also cleared an internal fault in that chapter: its opening block had said *side* where its body said *back*. **THE LESSON IS THE STRUCTURAL ONE: A DEVICE PUT IN A TITLE IS A DEVICE THE TITLE SEARCH WILL FIND AND A 9-GRAM RUN WILL NOT, AND A CARD THAT ASKS FOR A DOOR IS A CARD THAT HAS TO BE CHECKED AGAINST EVERY OTHER CARD THAT ASKS FOR A DOOR IN THE SAME BATCH.**
   - **(c) A FIGURE IN THE ACCOUNT'S OWN RECURRING REFERENT HAD MOVED.** The chapter on the page puts that unnamed thing back to a fortnight in the middle of August; 0494 had it a fortnight later in the same month, and its own card had asked for a finding three months old. **0484 IS THE CHAPTER ON THE PAGE AND THE CHAPTER IS RIGHT, SO 0494 WAS BROUGHT BACK TO THE MIDDLE OF AUGUST** and the card's arithmetic was not defended, which is the calendar rule answering a card for the second time in three blocks.
   - **(d) A MEASURED WORD HAD COME BACK AFTER THREE EMPTY BLOCKS.** *Hall* was at ten in 0026 and at zero in 0027, 0028 and 0029, all measured, and 0494 had four of them and 0485 had one. It is at **zero in all ten** and no chapter that needed a hall went and got one: 0494's box now stands on a table inside a front door, which is a different object and a better one.
   - **(e) TEN OF TEN CHAPTERS ENDED ON THE SAME SHAPE.** Every one of the ten carried exactly two all-caps paragraphs and exactly two `---`. The caps are the book's own form and are flagged for a human at §16 and were not touched. The `---` count is a cap and not a target, and **0486 and 0492 now stand at one break each, where two sections run on because nothing changes place or hour across the join.** The point is not the number. **THE POINT IS THAT TEN IDENTICAL SHAPES ACROSS TEN CHAPTERS IS A BATCH THAT HAS BEEN WRITTEN TO A FIGURE INSTEAD OF TO TEN SCENES, AND THE ONLY THING THAT CATCHES IT IS A PERSON LOOKING AT THE TEN SIDE BY SIDE.**
   - **AND TWO THINGS THE REVIEW CAUGHT WHICH WERE NOT STYLISTIC. 0488 SAID THE HORSE AND CART WERE BOUGHT *NINE YEARS* BEFORE A CHAPTER DATED 2019 FOR A PURCHASE THAT 0488 ITSELF PUTS IN MARCH 2016, AND 0490 SAID *NINE YEARS* FOR A DIG PUT IN FEBRUARY 2011 AGAINST THE SAME CHAPTER. BOTH ARE THREE YEARS AND EIGHT YEARS, AND BOTH ARE NOW WHAT THE CHAPTERS' OWN DATES MAKE THEM.** A duration that disagrees with the dateline of the chapter it sits in is a factual error and not a tic, and no measuring pass in this repository compares a number against a date.

## §12E. THE EIGHT FINDINGS OF THE REVIEW OF 0032, AND WHAT THIS BATCH DID WITH EACH OF THEM

1. **A CHAPTER CAN USE AN OBJECT ITS OWN CARD FORBIDS.** The checker was copied, its lists were changed, and it was run on each chapter as it was written rather than at the end. **TEN CHAPTERS OUT OF TEN WERE CAUGHT ON THE FIRST PASS, AT 121 HITS, AND ALL 121 WERE CLEARED IN THE CHAPTERS.** The finding is turned into a tool and the tool is load-bearing, and the figure is four times the one 0032's first pass produced against a checker that could not see thirteen of the items.
2. **A WRITER CAN PUT ITS OWN ARGUMENT WITH ITS OWN CARD ON THE PAGE.** A sentence that explains why a thing is not a violation is itself a sentence that is not in the book. **NO SUCH SENTENCE SURVIVED INTO ANY OF THESE TEN CHAPTERS, AND A DASH CORRECTING A SENTENCE WAS USED IN DRAFTING AND IS ON THE PAGE NOW NOWHERE, AND NO CARD WAS DEFENDED TO KEEP ONE.**
3. **A CARD CAN PRINT A FIGURE THAT IS ON THE CLOSED LIST.** Three of this batch's ten cards do, and they are at §12D items 2, 2 and 3, and in all three the chapter is right and the card is wrong. **THE RULE IS UNCHANGED AND IT IS THE 0030 RULE: A CHAPTER BEATS A CARD, A CHAPTER ON THE PAGE BEATS A LATER CHAPTER, AND A CARD NEVER BEATS EITHER.**
4. **A DURATION THAT DISAGREES WITH ITS OWN DATELINE.** Twelve were wrong and all twelve were corrected in the chapters, and the list is at §12C item 8. **NO CHAPTER OF THIS BATCH SPANS TWO DATES.**
5. **A SINGLE ORDINARY WORD CAN BECOME ONE CHAPTER'S FILLER, AND A MEASURE THAT NAMES THE WRONG WORD IS NOT A FINDING EITHER.** See §13. **THE DECLARED MEASURE FOR THIS BATCH WAS *WEEK*, WHICH IS NEITHER *ONE* NOR *ABOUT* AND IS NOT THE ACCOUNT'S OWN GRAMMAR, AND IT CAME OUT AT THIRTEEN ACROSS TEN CHAPTERS, WHICH IS THIRTEEN AND NOT FOURTEEN AFTER THE REPAIR OF 29 SEPTEMBER 2026 AND BOTH FIGURES ARE ON THE PAGE. 6. **THE SECOND TELLING OF RUN FOUR IS BIGGER THAN THE FIRST.** It was anticipated rather than discovered: §1, the open-threads bullets and the character roster were all written as ledgers of dispositions before any measurement was taken against a state file. **THE FIGURE THAT BINDS IS THE LAST ONE AT §13A ITEM 4 AND IT IS NIL.**

1. **A CHAPTER CAN USE AN OBJECT ITS OWN CARD FORBIDS.** The checker was copied, its lists were changed, and it was run on each chapter as it was written rather than at the end. **FIVE CHAPTERS OUT OF FIVE WERE CAUGHT ON THE FIRST PASS, AT 22 HITS, AND ALL 22 WERE CLEARED IN THE CHAPTERS.** The finding is turned into a tool and the tool is load-bearing, and the figure is a third of 0033's, for the reason at §12C item 2.
2. **A WRITER CAN PUT ITS OWN ARGUMENT WITH ITS OWN CARD ON THE PAGE.** A sentence that explains why a thing is not a violation is itself a sentence that is not in the book. **ONE SELF-CORRECTING DASH WAS WRITTEN IN 0528 IN DRAFTING AND IS ON THE PAGE NOW NOWHERE, AND NO CARD WAS DEFENDED TO KEEP ONE.**
3. **A CARD CAN PRINT A FIGURE THAT IS ON THE CLOSED LIST, A DATE ITS OWN CALENDAR DOES NOT REACH, OR A WORD IN THE SETTING IT ASKS FOR.** Five of this block's ten cards do one of those things, and they are at §12D items 1 to 5. **THE RULE IS UNCHANGED AND IT IS THE 0030 RULE: A CHAPTER BEATS A CARD, A CHAPTER ON THE PAGE BEATS A LATER CHAPTER, AND A CARD NEVER BEATS EITHER.**
4. **A DURATION THAT DISAGREES WITH ITS OWN DATELINE.** Seven were wrong and all seven were corrected in the chapters, and the list is at §12C item 8. **NO CHAPTER OF THIS BLOCK SPANS TWO DATES.**
5. **A SINGLE ORDINARY WORD CAN BECOME ONE CHAPTER'S FILLER, AND A MEASURE THAT NAMES THE WRONG WORD IS NOT A FINDING EITHER.** See §13. **THE DECLARED MEASURE FOR THIS BLOCK IS *QUITE*, WHICH IS NEITHER *ONE* NOR *WEEK* NOR *ABOUT*, AND IT CAME OUT AT 5 ACROSS THE FIVE. THE MEASURE 0032 DECLARED, *ONE*, IS REPORTED BESIDE IT AT 49. THE MEASURE 0033 DECLARED, *WEEK*, IS REPORTED BESIDE THAT AT 6. AND THE WORD THE 0032 REVIEW FOUND DOING THE WORK, *ABOUT*, IS REPORTED BESIDE ALL THREE AT 131, OF WHICH 95 ARE *ABOUT* PLUS A QUANTITY.** ALL FOUR ARE REPORTED AND EVERY CHAPTER IS COUNTED AND EVERY PLACE IS GIVEN AT §13.
6. **THE SECOND TELLING OF RUN FOUR IS BIGGER THAN THE FIRST.** It was anticipated rather than discovered: §1 to §10 of this block, §1 to §10 of the open-threads block and the character-state roster were all written as ledgers of dispositions grouped by person, before any measurement was taken against a state file. **THE FIGURE THAT BINDS IS THE LAST ONE AT §13A ITEM 4 AND IT IS NIL.**
7. **NINE CARDS OUT OF TEN CAN NAME A PLACE IN THE RESISTANCE COLUMN.** The resistance columns of this block's ten cards were read before a chapter was written. **FOUR NAME A PLACE, 0525, 0526, 0527 AND 0528, AGAINST A BUDGET OF THREE, AND THE OVERRUN IS IN THE CARDS AND NOT IN THE CHAPTERS, AND WHAT ELSE COULD HAVE BEEN THE RESISTANCE IS RECORDED CARD BY CARD AT §11 OF THE 0034 OPEN-THREADS BLOCK.** THE FIGURE IS FOUR, WHICH IS WORSE THAN 0032's TWO, 0033's TWO AND 0030's NINE, AND IT WAS NOT ARRANGED.
8. **A COUNT OF GAPS IN A TEN-CHAPTER RUN IS NOT A CONSTANT.** The count was made from the chapter dates and not from any prompt, on the second telling, and it is ten, and the prompt's own rule is carried forward as binding only for a run that contains a two-day chapter.

## §12A. THE VERBATIM-SPAN METHOD AS IT WAS USED FOR THIS BATCH, AND THE DETECTOR THE 0025 REVIEW FOUND A FAULT IN

**ONE, THE THRESHOLD IS NINE TOKENS AND IT IS NAMED EVERY TIME. TWO, THE SCRIPT COMPARES TOKENS AND NOT CHARACTERS, ON `[a-z0-9']+` APPLIED TO LOWERCASED TEXT, AND A TOKEN THAT IS NOTHING BUT APOSTROPHE MARKS IS A QUOTATION MARK AND IS DROPPED. THREE, THE H1 TITLE LINE IS DROPPED, EVERY `---` LINE IS DROPPED, AND EVERY STANDALONE ALL-CAPS PARAGRAPH IS DROPPED, WITH OR WITHOUT BOLD MARKERS. FOUR, A SPAN IS A MAXIMAL RUN OF NINE CONSECUTIVE TOKENS SHARED WITH THE COMPARISON SET, EXTENDED BY DIRECT TOKEN COMPARISON, AND THE EXTENSION IS TAKEN FROM EVERY REAL POSITION THE NINE-GRAM OCCUPIES IN THE SET FILE AND NOT FROM ONE. FIVE, EVERY SPAN IS ASSERTED CONTIGUOUS IN THE OTHER FILE BY DIRECT TOKEN COMPARISON AND NOT BY ADDING ONE HIT TO THE NEXT. SIX, A PARAGRAPH BOUNDARY IS A SENTINEL NO TOKEN CAN EQUAL, IN THE TARGET AND IN EVERY SET FILE, AND NO SPAN CROSSES ONE. SEVEN, A CHAPTER IS NEVER INCLUDED IN THE SET IT IS COMPARED AGAINST AND EACH FILE OF A SET IS COMPARED SEPARATELY. EIGHT, THREE CLASSES ARE EXCLUDED AND RECORDED AS A COUNT AND NOT CHASED: A DATELINE, A FIGURE'S OWN BY-NAME DESCRIPTION, AND A BOROUGH'S OWN RECURRING PLACE NOUN. NINE, THE CONTROL IS ASKED FOR BEFORE ANY FIGURE IS BELIEVED AND IS TWO PAIRS AND A PLANT. TEN, EVERY FIGURE IS TAKEN AGAIN AFTER EVERY REPAIR AND AGAIN AT THE END.**

**AND THE FINDING OF THE 0025 REVIEW, WHICH IS THE BY-NAME DETECTOR, IS BINDING ON THIS PASS, AND BOTH SIDES WERE BUILT AND BOTH SIDES WERE ASKED FOR DIRECTLY. THE NOUN PHRASE IS BUILT PROPERLY: A DETERMINER, THEN ANY MODIFIERS, THEN THE HEAD NOUN, THEN A CHAIN OF PREPOSITION PHRASES, AND THE SPAN IS REFUSED THE MOMENT A VERB APPEARS INSIDE IT. A SPAN LONGER THAN THE NOUN PHRASE IS NOT A DESCRIPTION AND IS A REAL REUSE. **THE HEAD NOUN SET IN THIS DETECTOR HOLDS FIGURES ONLY, BECAUSE A BY-NAME DESCRIPTION DESCRIBES A PERSON AND A PLACE IS NOT A PERSON, AND THE THIRD EXCLUDED CLASS IS WHAT CARRIES PLACES. THE TWO SIDES ANSWERED AS FOLLOWS: ON *THE MAN IN HIS FORTIES HAS THE MIDDLE OF THAT TERRACE AND HAS HAD IT ABOUT FIVE YEARS* THE NOUN PHRASE COVERS THE FIRST FIVE TOKENS AND NO MORE, AND ON THE SAME OPENING RUN ON INTO *WENT DOWN THAT STREET AT ABOUT FOUR THE SAME AFTERNOON TO PUT A BOTTLE BACK ON A SHELF AT THE END OF IT* THE DETECTOR STILL COVERS THE FIRST FIVE AND REFUSES THE REST, WHICH IS THE FAILURE IN THE OTHER DIRECTION AND THE ONE THAT COSTS A FIGURE. THE EXCLUSION COUNT IN THE FIRST CONTROL IS EIGHT AND IT IS RECORDED AS A COUNT AND NOT CHASED.****

**AND THE OTHER REPAIR THE 0025 REVIEW ASKED FOR IS THE DATELINE CLASS, AND IT IS DETECTED STRUCTURALLY AND NOT FROM A LIST OF WORDS, AND IT WAS WIDENED ONCE ON THE DAY BY A WRITER WHO HAD FOUND A FAULT IN IT AND HAS SAID SO HERE. A PARAGRAPH IS A DATELINE WHEN IT **BEGINS** WITH A DAY OF THE WEEK, OPTIONALLY PRECEDED BY *THE*, OR WITH A NUMBER AND A DAY OR A MONTH NAME IMMEDIATELY AFTER IT. THE WIDENING WAS TO *THE*, AND IT WAS WIDENED BECAUSE 0446'S DATELINE BEGINS *THE WEDNESDAY OF THE TENTH OF OCTOBER* AND WITHOUT THE WIDENING THAT CHAPTER HAD NO DATELINE AT ALL AND ITS DATE TOKENS COMPETED IN RUNS TWO, THREE AND FIVE. **A DATELINE IS DROPPED ON BOTH SIDES AND A SPAN IS ONLY OF THAT CLASS WHEN THE WHOLE OF IT SITS INSIDE SUCH A PARAGRAPH, WHICH IS STRICTER THAN A CONTAINMENT TEST. A PASS THAT ADDS AN ENTRY TO A LIST IS A PASS THAT HAS NOT FOUND A DEFECT, AND A PASS THAT EXCLUDES A SPAN IT SHOULD NOT HAS HIDDEN ONE.****

**AND THE REVIEW PASS OF 2026-09-29 FOUND A FOURTH FAULT IN THE SCRIPT, WHICH IS THAT IT DID NOT RUN. EVERY FUNCTION IN IT WAS CORRECT AND `__main__` PRINTED ONE LINE OF METHOD AND EXITED, SO NONE OF THE FIGURES IN §13A COULD BE REPRODUCED FROM THE FILE THEY WERE FILED UNDER. RUNNING IT IS HOW THE NINE REUSES AT §12C ITEM 5 WERE FOUND AT ALL, AND THAT IS THE ARGUMENT FOR IT.**

## §1. Nine foot of ground, and two people who would not be second

She had it in October and never asked. He has wanted it since about the end of October and has never once taken it.

Twice in one afternoon they were close enough to have spoken about it and neither did, and at six o'clock the ground was as it had been, and she went off to a bus and he shut a gateway up the street.

Neither has the other's half of it. He has not seen her. She has not seen where his things go. Each came to the same conclusion independently, and the conclusion was that whoever goes second is the one who looks like they took something, and neither is willing to look like that, and neither will raise it.

## §2. A store door, and a man who shut it

A door at the back of that kitchen was moving in the draught and he closed it as he passed, and there was a store behind it that had not been empty for some weeks.

What he took out of that room with him was a ring in the dust on a box, and there is no way to account for it.

He has not gone back in, has not questioned the neighbour, and has slowed down for nothing on four passes of that building. She put the boxes to him and he gave her the short answer and she let it lie, and six weeks have gone by with nothing said.

## §3. Six minutes longer, every weekday morning

A woman she has never spoken to was missing from a spot she had been in the habit of seeing for years, and rather than raise it with anybody she altered her own route to avoid passing it, at a cost of six minutes a morning.

Ten days of it, and the whole of that street has seen her pass every morning and has not remarked on anything. She will not open the subject herself.

There is nothing to revert, because nobody was keeping a record but her.

## §4. A door, held for a fortnight and then let go

He had been shutting that door for six years out of habit and she had been leaving it for four months out of a principle about not making people stop, and the two of them had never discussed either.

She did it once, and he understood inside a couple of seconds that the change was hers, and he sat on it for a fortnight before doing the same.

Both know and neither has said anything, and the door is now shut more often than it is not, and nobody could date the change.

## §5. A true answer to the wrong question

She put a question to him in a passage that she could not put in any other way, and he gave her an answer that was true and that he believed he had earned.

He worked out four days later that she sleeps at the front and that stair is at the back and that there is a woman on the third floor and a man on the ground floor, and that her question had not been about his sight at all.

She has asked him nothing since, of anything. He will not go back and take the answer back, because withdrawing it would hand her a different problem and he does not know which one.

## §6. A building worked out through two windows

Seven weeks of watching from her own front room, and what she has is not a thing anybody told her but a thing she assembled out of what that building gives away to anybody on the opposite pavement.

She has also worked out that the man who stands outside that shop is not a passer-by, and he has not spoken to her once in all of the seven weeks and could not say who she is.

She is not going to say it to the woman at number eight, because how she knows is that she has been watching that building since October. she has been carrying it since early November and it has cost her something every day.

## §7. A length of wire in a joint, twice

The same small repair, made in the same place, on two different days, by two men who have never met and do not know of each other.

A car lifted the slab out and it lay off the path for three days. A woman found the gap, looked at it, and kept it to herself. The man in his thirties put it back and did to it what had been done to it before, because that is now the only version of that repair that exists.

There is no list of that ground and nobody owns it. before long the whole of that will stand proud again.

## §8. A sentence about a wall that was not all of it

He did about nine foot of repointing on a wall over three days and left about eighteen inch of the bottom of it because there is a pipe inside that wall and the bottom cannot be reached without taking four foot of it off.

He reported the job finished to a man who wrote it down and was gone. She has seen exactly what he left and has decided that the one question worth asking is one she will not ask.

What he is protecting is the four foot of that wall higher up that nobody has ever properly looked at, and raising the foot of it would have started something he has no standing to finish.

## §9. Four inches, and the wrong foot

She watched a man cross a step over running water twice without stopping, worked out four days later that it was a thing rather than an accident, and did it on the Saturday morning and got it wrong, because he is right-footed and she is left-footed.

He was nine foot behind her and did not slow and did not look up. She has been over it again about nine times since and has got it right four times and is not going to let that put her off, and not because she minds a wet shoe.

## §10. A Thursday, and a length of iron off a wall

Nine people on that parade in that stretch of the morning, none of them there because of any of the other eight. something came off a wall at half past twelve, three men had it back up in ten minutes on a different fixing three inch to the left, the owner was told nothing and put her hand flat on it at two and went in.

The line under the last entry of that book stood open since the middle of March three years before that and nobody went near it. Four answers are still going round and no fifth has come in and nobody put any two of them together and nobody asked anybody what any of them was an answer to.

What a person in that street cannot put a name to has not shifted by a day since the middle of August. The woman with the dog came back down at ten past two, went past the wall without looking at it, and went down to the end.

**AND ON THE THIRD OF JANUARY A MAN IN HIS FORTIES WALKED UP THAT PARADE WITH A BROWN PAPER BAG UNDER HIS ARM AND DID NOT LOOK AT THE WALL EITHER, AND HE DID NOT KNOW IT HAD BEEN OFF.**

## §1. A cat, a coping, and a fortnight of going round

A man had walked the same cut twice a day for nine years and something small that had always been on a wall in it was not there on a Sunday in January. He went the long way for a fortnight. On the third Monday he went through. He has never asked anybody about it. The woman on the other side of that corner has the animal and had stopped letting it out before Christmas and has not opened her door about it since. Each of them arrived at the same impasse from opposite ends of a wall neither of them can see over, and neither of them knows that the other is in it.

## §2. Three floors, one stair, and a noise through a ceiling

Two people in a building of three flats had each built a version of a woman on the top floor out of a sound at half past two in the morning. In January he saw her leave. In January she saw her go. Each of them learned one thing and neither learned the other thing, and the reason each of them will not put it to her is a different thing entirely, and his is a man who does not want to be listened to and hers is a woman who has decided that eight months of lying awake entitles a stranger to be left alone.

## §3. Two minutes of noise at half past five

A man walked from his own door to his van making a sound for about two minutes every weekday morning. A woman above a garage behind his house asked him once, in about eleven seconds and seven words, to leave off. He stopped for a week. Then he did it again, and the reason he did it again is a removal she has booked for April that he worked out from two things and has never mentioned to anybody.

## §4. A landing, and a side that was chosen in 2013

A woman has stood on one particular side of a man on a landing since a March in 2013, because she had a thing to say once and did not want to say it twice. In January he told her, without any edge on it, that the ear she had chosen is the one that hears everything and the other one has gone. She is not going to change sides, and the reason is not the ear.

## §5. A thing carried out of a house every morning

A man has carried an armchair out of his own front door and left it on a kerb every weekday since 2013, and a woman at the end of the row has carried it in at one every day of that without either of them ever referring to it. On the twenty-fifth of January he put it down and walked on. It rained on it. He has parked on the far side of that road ever since and has no reason he would say out loud.

## §6. Two minutes at a car, and a window that was already there

A man stands at his own car every morning with his hand flat on the door for about two minutes and does not get in. A woman four houses away takes her cup to a window she has always sat at and did not know until the seventeenth of January that she did it on purpose. He has not looked up since that morning. Thirteen days of neither of them raising it, and she has decided she would rather be a woman who watches him than a woman who announces she has stopped.

## §7. A machine at the back of a building, and two women under it

Two women live one above the other over a machine that runs for twenty-two minutes. The older has wanted it to stop for two years and nine months and has said nothing to anybody. The younger started minding after Christmas and has spent a fortnight angry that the older never said. A man changed a timer and an arm of metal for reasons of his own. Both women now know and neither can say anything, and the older is worse off than she was, and neither will ask him.

## §8. A flank wall, and a fact nobody can be given

A man has known since 2014 that the boundary wall of a kitchen is carrying the side of the house next door, and he is right, and the whole of why he cannot hand that to anybody is in two occasions on which he was inside that wall in 2013 and 2016 with nobody in either house knowing. He said it once in September and was asked not to say it again. She has added up the three things she could do and cannot afford any of them, and has decided not to ask him, because asking him would be asking him to be somebody he has told her he is not.

## §9. Ten seconds at a corner

A woman stopped at a corner in January and let a man get to the kerb first and said nothing while he did. He has worked out what it meant and cannot ask, because there are three things it could have been and he has settled on one and cannot weigh it against the other two. She is not going to find out which of the two she is in, because one of them is a thing she has carried for nothing and the other is a thing she would have to answer for, and she has no answer.

## §10. A Sunday, and four foot of pavement

Nine people went up and down a parade on the twenty-fourth of February for reasons of their own. A man swept nine foot of pavement an hour earlier than usual. Underneath the grit there is four foot of paving a different colour from the rest of it, and it was in the sun for about two minutes, and nobody looked at it and nobody has ever looked at it. A door in a wall at the top end is not locked and has no bench in it and has not been through since before Christmas. The four answers went nowhere. The page is still empty.

## §1. What the people of this batch are each carrying now

**A MAN AT NUMBER SEVEN IN A ROW OF TWELVE.** He wanted thirty square yard at the top of an acre behind him and he asked for it in 2015, in 2017 and in October, and he was refused three times without any unkindness, and in November the woman who owns that ground told him she had let the whole of it to somebody from the town, and he said one word and shut his own front door. He has a second hive than he had in February and he has three where the ground will take two, and he put them in nine foot at the back of his own house, between his own wall and the next one, in full view of a window. He has worked out that he does not mind that. He has not got as far as why. Nobody in that row knows that he ever wanted anything, and he has not told one person, and he has not been near that door since November.

**A WOMAN AT NUMBER THREE IN THAT ROW.** She heard him say in a July that is nine months gone that there was no point in anybody asking, and she heard the wrong half of that sentence, and she went in January. Three times. On his behalf, with his number said out loud on a doorstep, twice making sure it was not for herself. In January she was told that nobody had ever asked about that ground in about twenty years, and she believed it, and the belief has been sitting on her since, and what it amounts to is a charge against a man who is not in the room. In the second week of April she was told the whole thing went in March. She said one word to the owner of that ground and carried on with what she was carrying. She has not told him any of it and she is not going to, and the reason she has settled on is that there is no way of telling a man who has given up that somebody went to a door about it that does not charge him with something.

**A WOMAN AT NUMBER FOUR IN A PASSAGE, AND A WOMAN AT THE TOP OF IT, AND A MAN WHO WENT IN FOUR MORNINGS A WEEK FOR SIX YEARS.** The woman at number four has stood on her own step every morning since about 1990 for air and has wanted, since about November, for a man to give up something that was not hers to give up. In the third week of February she gave the woman at the top of that passage a true answer to a question she had not been asked. The woman at the top of it heard it and went on being exactly the same, which was worse than either of the two things she had braced for, and she has not said one word about it to anybody in nineteen years. The man came for six more weeks and she watched every one of them. He came out of that house on the first of April with empty hands, which he had never done, and he stopped in the middle of that passage and looked back up it, and he did not go back. She was fourteen yard away and did not move for about two minutes. She has two possible explanations and one of them is her own mouth in a market, and she cannot put the other one out of her head, and the only way to find out is the one thing she is not going to do. The woman at the top of that passage now has nobody in her house on a weekday morning and has told nobody and is worse off than she was in February.

**TWO MEN INSIDE A RULE, AND A WOMAN BEHIND SIX FOOT OF WALL.** A third man made the rule in 2008 in about a minute and has never explained it. Asking would be telling, which is why ten years on neither of the two knows whether the other is keeping it. They spent an hour in March on the third man's life and neither of them got to the part of it that mattered, and one of them said out loud that nothing was going on and both have since treated that as something that was said rather than something that was true. They each went home certain they had been quietly written off, and neither of them was wrong about the other's behaviour and neither of them can say so. The woman behind the wall has seen the third man come in at four in the morning four times since January and has said nothing to anybody and is not going to.

**A MAN IN HIS SIXTIES AND A DOG.** He has walked one stretch of that street, at one hour, for twelve years. In January he found out that a man new to the row had gone to a neighbour twice to ask a question about waste bags, and that told him everything, and he has been carrying it since December. In January the new man did something on purpose in front of him. In March he stood still on a far kerb and let a dog be over rather than cross a road at ten past six in front of about nine people. He has drawn one conclusion from all of it and it is about himself rather than about the other man, and he is going to keep drawing it every morning, and he knows that is what he is doing.

**A WOMAN AT THE LAST DOOR IN A COVERED WAY, AND A MAN EMPTIES A HOUSE.** She has a floor two foot away from where he put it down and she has used it, and she has kept the small account rather than the large one, and she is going to keep the small one for the rest of her life because the large one involves her. What she has not put down is the second he spent standing still with a dying plant in his hands, and she saw it from a doorway. He has a sentence for everything that comes out of that house and he has used it about four hundred times and it is not a lie, and he has now used it about a thing that is nine foot inside somebody else's door and is standing on a floor. Neither of them has said anything and neither is going to.

**A MAN WHO CAME TO MEASURE A FRAME, AND A WOMAN WHO CAME OUT INTO HER OWN DOORWAY.** He was seventeen in 1974 and he cut nine marks and nobody ever told him what they were for, and under them there are two he did not cut, and he has known since the eighth of March and has not said so, because the frame comes out in April and the marks go with it and nobody has told her there is anything in it to lose. She has been carrying a second thing since 2004 without knowing she was carrying it, and it is about her son, and she is right about it. They talked for about ten minutes and neither of them mentioned the other's to the other, and a piece of joinery went down that street in April with two sets of marks on it.

**A WOMAN WHO HAS DRIVEN FOUR MILES EVERY SUNDAY SINCE 1999, AND THE MAN SHE DRIVES.** He has never asked her anything in twenty years and the reason is not that she seemed unwilling. Her hours changed in January. She did not come on the tenth of March, and when he drove to her street at four in the afternoon and put the question to her, the question that came out of his mouth was about the twenty years and not about the missing Sunday, and she answered it properly, and she is not going to take the answer back. He drove himself the following Sunday and was not late. She went back to that corner the same afternoon with a bag and stood on it. Neither of them has any idea what the other did and neither is going to ask.

**TWO PEOPLE AND A BLOCKED WAY.** Each of them has worked out, separately and without ever putting it to the other, that the other is the person who ought to cut four yard of green wood back off a hundred-yard way. His reason is that a stranger will put it forward again inside a year and a bigger reason he has not told anybody. Her reason is that the bed is not hers and there is nothing about the outside of that house anybody could point at. They met in the rain for about two minutes in February and the whole of what was said was two words and neither offered nor refused anything, and both of them had been ready to, and neither has mentioned it since, and her lease is up in June and nobody in that row knows.

**THE MAN IN HIS THIRTIES, WHO HAS GONE PAST A BOARDED BUILDING TWICE A DAY SINCE THE MIDDLE OF FEBRUARY, AND THE WOMAN WHO GOES IN AND OUT OF IT.** Five weeks of going past has produced one thing he cannot put down and no decision, and what he has not done is knock on a door, and the reason is a torch in 2013 and a ladder in 2016 and two afternoons he has never spoken to anybody about. He has not got to whether he is right, and he has not got to whether being right is the thing that would stop him either. She has gone in and out of the front of that building on a weekday for five weeks with something in her arms, and he has counted her twice a day and worked out three things about her and told himself that three is where he stops. They have been about four paces apart in that street thirty times and neither of them knows what the other is doing there. He went to work at ten to eight on the morning the front of that building came down off a scaffold, and he will go past it tomorrow.

**NINE PEOPLE ON A PARADE, A VAN, A PLANTER, AND A ROOM BEHIND A FLANK WALL.** Nine people on that street on a Wednesday evening and none of them for the same reason, and the only thing that went wrong was a van coming back the wrong way and a concrete planter ending up four inch out from a shop wall. Nine people went round it. Nobody stopped and nobody said anything and the driver came back on foot and apologised and offered to pay for another one and the woman at that counter said it would not go. A man shut the shop next door, as he has for about seven years, and nobody has asked him and he has never said no. Along the side of the last building on that street there is a door that stands open along its bottom edge, is not locked, and is not storage anybody rents; behind it is a ground-floor room that has had nothing in it since about 2011 and that nobody in this borough has been inside in about eight years, and the reason no one goes in is that getting in means standing on a piece of ground at the side of that building, two hundred square yard of it, with no way out through the back, and a person with no reason to be on it does not stand on it.
